543401|2026-09.headline: Go Fashion Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore; gross margin 60.8% and SSSG roughly flat amid festive shift and RM inflation.
543401|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue declined 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore as the festive season shifted into October, with LFS dispatches moving out of September. Gross margin fell to 60.8% as higher-cost fabric inventory flowed through; management estimates a 200 bps hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps again in Q3. EBITDA before exceptionals was Rs 56 crore (25.8% margin) and PAT was Rs 9 crore. Store network consolidation continued: 23 closures and 9 openings in Q2, taking the EBO count to 737 with total retail area up to about 4.4 lakh sq ft. Management guided to lower closures and price hikes from post-festive, but gave no formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 impact of about 200 bps from RM inflation (management estimate)
Store-closure capex write-offs; H1 FY26 was Rs 1.73 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow pre-Ind AS 116 (H1 FY27)

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth broadly flat in Q2 after +0.6% in Q1; 737 EBOs across 196 cities. Stores above 750 sq ft reportedly at +2-3% SSSG while smaller stores are negative; average EBO size about 608 sq ft.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue hit by festive timing, with dispatches moved from September to October. LFS was about 23% of H1 FY27 sales; management says supply chain is normalised.

segments.name: Dailywear concept
segments.commentary: 21 operational stores vs 15 in Q1, with a target of 25-30 by end FY27 (8-9 more planned). Management cites about Rs 1,000 sales per sq ft per month as a benchmark.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce / Amazon
segments.commentary: Online receivables rose after quick commerce and Amazon SOR tie-ups began from March; receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.

guidance_outlook: SSSG target: positive for FY27 as a whole; management says it is 'keeping fingers crossed' and Q3 'should deliver a good number'.
Gross margin: 100-200 bps impact expected in Q3 FY27; margins expected to stabilise over the next 2 quarters as calibrated price hikes offset RM costs.
Store closures: Q3 closures visibility at 15-20 stores, sharply lower than Q1 (58-59) and Q2 (23); management says closures will 'considerably' decline in H2.
Dailywear: target of 25-30 stores by end FY27.
Inventory days to remain within the 90-100 day range guided earlier in the year.
Long term: about 2x square footage over the next 5 years, COCO model retained; bottomwear stores to move to 700-900 sq ft.
capex_capacity: Retail area about 4.4 lakh sq ft at 30 Sep 2026, up from 4.34 lakh at 31 Mar 2026 (about 14,220 sq ft added in H1 despite net closures).
H1 FY27 openings 24 and closures 89; Q2 openings 9 and closures 23.
Store renovations undertaken in H1 (a couple of stores), included in other expenses; value not disclosed.
Men's and women's topwear pilot: 21 stores above 1,500 sq ft; plan to add 8-9 more to test the topwear format.
demand_pricing: Festive timing shifted; management says a portion of pre-festive demand moved from September to October. Festive season started decently; 49 days to festive used as the leading indicator.
Price hikes taken on certain articles recently, with more planned post-festive; ASP for EBOs Rs 827 (H1). Management says ASP rise of 6% is mainly product mix, not price.
Fabric/yarn costs up 8-10% blended, after the geopolitical situation; management had expected cooling in Jul-Aug but prices stayed high.
Full-price sales ratio 93% in H1 FY27.
Value-added non-leggings portfolio now 70% of revenue; new bottomwear products in the Rs 800-900 price band.
Shraddha Kapoor brand campaign went live in Q2 (ambassador from July); effect to be assessed after the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Why have costs not fallen after closing about 75 net stores YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was flat at about Rs 46.3 crore in Q2 vs Rs 45.75 crore a year ago, after April increments. Rent was about Rs 37 crore vs Rs 36 crore. Advertising rose to Rs 12.63 crore in H1 from Rs 7.85 crore, and exceptional write-offs rose to Rs 9.87 crore from Rs 1.73 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company taking price hikes to offset cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Some hikes have been taken and more are planned post-festive. Management expects margin offset to take a couple of quarters, with stabilisation in the next 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will closures slow down, and will H2 be better than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closures will be considerably lower from Q3 (15-20 stores visible), and Q3 should deliver a good YoY number. On whether FY27 SSSG turns positive, management said it was 'keeping fingers crossed'.

qa_highlights.question: How much new-cost inventory is flowing through, given the inventory and COGS figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to isolate because products sell at different rates and price hikes are happening. It estimated a 200 bps GM hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps in Q3, and acknowledged older inventory at old prices.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore despite lower LFS revenue; why?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly non-LFS: online receivables from quick commerce and Amazon SOR since March, plus some export receivables for the Dubai store.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the LFS discount jumped to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 44.5 crore in FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFS credits are margin-linked (about 5-6% of LFS sales, reconciled in Q4) rather than discounts. It did not confirm the Rs 61 crore figure and promised a clarification note; FY26 LFS decline was due to Q3 supply chain disruption at a large partner.

risks_watch: Gross margin: management expects 100-200 bps pressure in Q3 and says the 200 bps Q2 hit is not a precise figure; the timing of price-hike pass-through is uncertain.

SSSG: Q2 was flat with a festive shift; Q3 needs to be strong for FY27 SSSG to turn positive. Smaller stores (<300 sq ft, roughly 120-150 units) remain negative and 20-30% of the network is seen as problematic.
Competition and store format: management attributes slowdown to store size, not merchandise or competition (Zudio, Westside), but this is not independently verified.
Clarifications pending: store-count split by size (to be shared via SGA), LFS discount quantum (Rs 61 crore vs Rs 44.5 crore), and receivables rise from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.
Topwear and menswear pilot (21 stores) is unproven; a 8-9 store test is still to come.
543401|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the long-term store-format transition and the early signals, but cautious and at times evasive on specific numbers (store-size breakup, SSSG timing, margin quantum, LFS discount), promising follow-up data via SGA.
key_quotes: As I said last quarter, one quarter does not make a trend in either direction.
So, if you ask me, the store is the real reason for our slowness. And I think the larger store is what is going to fix it.
This is a shift in timing rather than demand and the supply chain with the key LFS partners remains normalized.
Considerably lower, Ankit.

rows.why: Dailywear stores at 21 vs 15 in Q1, with a firm target of 25-30 by FY27-end (8-9 more), plus an 8-9 store topwear pilot; retail area only ~4.4 lakh sq ft, so these are small adds against 89 closures in H1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue fell 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore and H1 fell 1.5% to Rs 440 crore, with SSSG flat in Q2; management hopes Q3 'should deliver a good number' but FY27 SSSG positivity is only 'fingers crossed'.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond store renovations (value undisclosed) and the long-term plan of about 2x square footage over 5 years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given, and management is only 'keeping fingers crossed' on positive FY27 SSSG with H1 revenue down 1.5% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 gross margin hit of 100-200 bps is guided, price-hike pass-through timing is uncertain, and smaller stores (20-30% of network) remain problematic with negative SSSG.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New bottomwear products in the Rs 800-900 price band are already in place, and the topwear format is being tested in 21 stores with 8-9 more planned; value-added non-leggings are 70% of revenue.

rows.label: Store closures slow sharply in H2
rows.why: Q3 closure visibility is 15-20 stores vs 58-59 in Q1 and 23 in Q2, and management says closures will 'considerably' decline in H2.

rows.label: Post-festive price hikes
rows.why: Some hikes are taken, more are planned post-festive, and management expects margin offset over a couple of quarters; fabric costs are up 8-10%.

rows.label: Quick commerce and Amazon SOR channel
rows.why: Online receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore after the quick commerce and Amazon SOR tie-ups began in March, showing channel traction.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term store-format shift, Dailywear and the lower Q3 closure count, but cautious and at times evasive on SSSG timing, the margin quantum and the LFS discount, promising follow-up data via SGA; analysts pushed on margin, store-size breakup, receivables and the LFS

543411|2026-03.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q4 FY26 volume rose 27% to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue rose 102% to INR1,480 crores, while FY27 volume guidance is 6.5-7 lakh tons.
543411|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong Q4 FY26 volume growth of 27% YoY to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue of INR1,480 crores, up 102% YoY. FY26 volume rose to 5.32 lakh tons from 4.85 lakh tons, and EBITDA grew 8% to INR174 crores. Total comprehensive income in Q4 was INR18 crores against INR17.5 crores a year earlier. Management reiterated a 2 million ton capacity roadmap with 1 million tons to be added by FY29, and the call drew heavy questions on a large stock-in-trade cost line that analysts saw as depressing per-ton margins.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY vs 1.16 lakh tons in Q4 FY25
+37% as stated by management (base quoted as INR367 crores, likely a transcription error)
+33% YoY vs INR35 crores (management compared against 'Q4 FY26' in error)
vs INR17.5 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Contribution reached 39% of business mix in FY26; management expects around 50% by end of FY27 as DFT and Hindupur capacity ramp. 300x300 hollow sections were launched during FY26.

segments.name: Stock-in-trade (trading)
segments.commentary: Trading cost was about INR21 crores in Q3 and about INR300 crores in Q4, around INR700 crores across two quarters per the CFO. Management described margins on this as very nominal and said it will decline as the newly operational plants ramp up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of 6.5-7 lakh tons.
FY28 volume estimate around 8.5 lakh tons, based on 1.4 million tons capacity at 62-65% utilisation (70% peak).
EBITDA per ton of INR3,500-4,000 for FY27 and FY28, assuming no volatility and balanced demand-supply.
Capacity target of around 1.4 million tons by end FY27 and 1.7 million tons exit in FY28; 2 million tons is the longer-term goal, with INR300 crores of capex still needed (INR75-100 crores in FY27).
Value-added share expected to reach around 50% by FY27 end.
capex_capacity: Sanand Unit 2 Phase 3 DFT facility expected operational by Q3 FY27; Sanand APA pipes facility readiness by Q3 FY27 per Q&A (Q4 FY27 per prepared remarks). Oil and gas entry to start with water applications.
Greenfield Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) facility, about 1.5 lakh tons coated/pre-galvanised/galvanised tubes for solar, expected operational by Q4 FY27; fully integrated for ERW pipes and solar tubes.
Chennai (Sri City) facility on track, expected commissioning in FY27 with full-year benefit in FY28.
FY28 capacity additions: Sanand 1.5 lakh tons, Hindupur 2 lakh tons, Sri City Chennai 1.5 lakh tons, UP plant about 2 lakh tons.
Incremental 1 million ton capex: around INR100 crores already in CWIP; another INR300 crores needed to reach 2 million tons.
Solar capacity 16.5 MW installed, about 35% of power needs; green hydrogen trial started at Secunderabad Unit 1.
demand_pricing: Management cited robust demand across segments including data centres, railways, solar, infrastructure and power projects.
Q4 headwinds: gas price volatility, intermittent gas availability, and elevated ocean freight, creating temporary pressure on input costs and export realisations industry-wide.
Rupee depreciation cited as making Indian exports more competitive; international certifications secured for Europe, America and Middle East.
Management said the stock-in-trade purchases were partly due to geopolitical import cargo and supplier commitment volumes; discounts and rebates would be hit if volumes were not lifted.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose and pricing of the INR90 crore preferential issue to promoters (individual investor).
qa_highlights.answer: Anish Bansal said the INR90 crore issue is by promoters and funds the working capital needs of the 1 million to 2 million ton expansion. No issue price was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What products Hindupur will make and the FY27 volume guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Hindupur is a coated steel tube facility of about 1.5 lakh tons, making coated, pre-galvanised and galvanised tubes mainly for solar. FY27 volume target is 6.5-7 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield vs brownfield split of the extra 1 million tons.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanand is brownfield and Hindupur greenfield, a 50:50 split; capacity reaches about 1.4 million tons by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and approvals for oil and gas (API) pipes.
qa_highlights.answer: Full readiness of the Sanand API unit expected by Q3 FY27 after 1.5 years of equipment installation and testing. Start with water applications, then migrate to oil and gas, with export potential.

qa_highlights.question: Stock-in-trade cost jump and its margins; whether trading continues.
qa_highlights.answer: Stock-in-trade cost was about INR700 crores across Q3 and Q4 per the CFO, covering HRC, CR and galvanised products, with very nominal margins. Management said trading will fall as three newly operational plants (Secunderabad, Gujarat, Jammu) ramp up, and that stock was sold in March to avoid price-volatility losses.

qa_highlights.question: Capex breakdown and FY28 capacity and volume.
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores is in CWIP and INR300 crores more is needed; INR75-100 crores targeted for FY27. FY28 capacity exit about 1.7 million tons, volume around 8.5 lakh tons, EBITDA per ton INR3,500-4,000.

risks_watch: Stock-in-trade purchases (about INR700 crores across Q3-Q4) depress gross margin and per-ton profitability; the company says this will fall as new plants ramp up.
Q4 EBITDA margin per ton (INR3,150) is well below the FY28 guidance of INR3,500-4,000, which assumes stable markets.
Execution risk on Hindupur (Q4 FY27), Chennai (FY27 commissioning), DFT (Q3 FY27) and API readiness (Q3 FY27), with the 2 million ton target spread into FY29.
Energy input costs, gas availability and ocean freight remain volatile.
Transcript inconsistencies (FY26 revenue base, Q4 EBITDA comparison, APA timeline Q3 vs Q4 FY27) should be checked against the filed results.

Guidance is stated firmly, with FY28 EBITDA per ton of INR3,500-4,000 conditional on no market volatility.

So, if the markets and all, if there is no volatility and if the markets are aligned, the demand and supply, so about INR3,500 to INR4,000 is a very comfortable number.
And March was a month of extreme volatility and extreme uncertainty. So, we did not want to incur any loss on the price volatility. So, it was best to get rid of stock.

rows.why: Oil and gas (API) pipes start with water applications once the Sanand API unit is ready by Q3 FY27, and Hindupur coated, pre-galvanised and galvanised solar tubes come by Q4 FY27; 300x300 hollow sections were already launched in FY26.

rows.why: Stock-in-trade cost was about INR300 crores in Q4 and about INR700 crores across Q3-Q4, with nominal margins; management says trading falls as Secunderabad, Gujarat and Jammu plants ramp, but the stock was sold in March to avoid price losses and the timing is unconfirmed.

rows.why: Promoters are raising INR90 crores via preferential issue to fund working capital for the 1-2 million ton expansion, with no issue price disclosed.

543411|2026-06.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR1,413 crores on 26% volume growth, but PAT was flat at INR20 crores.
543411|2026-06.overview: Sales volume reached 1,56,136 MT, up 26% YoY, with revenue of INR1,413 crores (up 79% YoY). EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR49.37 crores, and EBITDA per ton was about INR3,162, roughly flat against Q4 FY26. PAT was INR20 crores against INR20.92 crores a year earlier, as higher gas, logistics and ocean freight costs and working-capital-driven finance costs weighed on earnings. Management reiterated 2 million tons capacity by FY29, with 6.5-7 lakh tons of FY27 sales guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Marginally up vs INR3,148/t in Q4 FY26
Vs INR20.92 crores in Q1 FY26 (broadly flat)
Down from INR420 crores in Q4 FY26
Similar to Q4 FY26, per analyst

segments.commentary: Management cited about 50% construction and infrastructure, 20% water and oil and gas transportation, with the balance from engineering, solar and other specialised segments.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: VAP share is about 35% currently; management targets 45-50% for FY28, with the full DFT benefit expected in FY28.

segments.name: Solar torque tubes
segments.commentary: Company is gaining share and adding lines this year; solar exports started this year.

segments.name: Data centre large hollow sections
segments.commentary: New segment; management targets 15,000-20,000 tons in FY27 from matured orders for gigawatt-scale data centres.

FY28 sales volume target of 1 million tons.

2 million tons capacity by FY29 expected to be met comfortably; a further 1 million tons to be added over the next 2-3 years, with 0.5 million tons construction starting by end FY27.

Stock-in-trade purchases expected to fall to INR50-100 crores per quarter going forward.

Expansion across UP, Andhra and Gujarat facilities under way; total capex for the 1 million ton expansion about INR650 crores, with about INR200 crores in FY27, and part already spent in FY26.
Management said INR350 crores remains for the next two financial years, after excluding amounts incurred through FY26 (reconciling the earlier INR300 crore figure).
demand_pricing: Infrastructure and construction demand described as very strong, with previously stalled projects restarting; next 2-3 quarters called crucial.
Blended realisation of about INR90,500/t per analyst calculation; management said it would normalise to about INR75,000/t.
Dealer rebates offered to penetrate the market are expected to be withdrawn once new plants reach critical mass.
Gas prices more than doubled, with higher logistics and ocean freight costs pressuring EBITDA per ton.
Monsoon and geopolitical conditions cited as near-term volume headwinds; July-August volumes described as similar to Q1.
Export focus on Europe, America, Canada and Australia; repeat orders reported.

qa_highlights.question: How is the demand outlook across infrastructure, construction, water, solar and industrial for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure and construction demand is very strong with previously held projects restarting; company is gaining solar share and adding lines this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the end-use mix, and which new industries are emerging?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% construction and infrastructure, 20% water and oil and gas transport, rest engineering, solar and specialised; data centres are an emerging segment.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for EBITDA per ton to reach INR3,750-4,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to exceed INR4,000/t once the three new plants reach critical mass and extra dealer rebates are withdrawn; the target is for FY28 per later comments.

qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost about INR15 crores against a much lower year-end debt base?
qa_highlights.answer: Three plants were commissioned within 4-5 months, lifting working capital; debt is expected to stay near current levels and per-ton finance cost to fall as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.question: Has the INR300 crore capex guidance changed to INR650 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: INR650 crores is the total for 1 million tons, of which part was spent in FY26, leaving about INR350 crores over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stock-in-trade purchases fall from INR420 crores to INR280 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of an import consignment was disposed of at sea due to geopolitics; a baseline of INR100-150 crores per quarter is expected to fall to INR50-100 crores.

risks_watch: Gas price spike (more than doubled), higher logistics and ocean freight costs pressuring EBITDA per ton.
Working-capital intensity and finance cost of about INR15 crores per quarter; analyst estimated finance cost near 17-18% of year-end debt, which management attributed to ramp-up timing.
Dealer discounts may persist until new plants reach critical mass, delaying the INR4,000/t EBITDA target.
Execution risk on DFT (Q3 FY27), API pipes (Q4 FY27, subject to approvals) and Hindupur (Q4 FY27) commissioning timelines.
Monsoon and geopolitical conditions may keep Q1-Q2 volumes flat before H2 pickup.

543412|2026-03.headline: Star Health Q4 FY26 underwriting profit rose to Rs 186 crore on a 95.7% combined ratio, but reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss on a Rs 558 crore MTM hit.
543412|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP rose 17% YoY (N basis) to Rs 6,259 crore, with fresh retail growing 38% and the loss ratio improving to 65.2% from 69.2%. Full-year GWP crossed Rs 20,000 crore (Rs 20,369 crore, up 16%) and FY26 underwriting profit turned positive at Rs 206 crore versus a Rs 165 crore loss in FY25. Reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss against a Rs 271 crore profit a year earlier, driven by the equity-market MTM loss. Management introduced a normalised investment yield of 8%, under which FY26 PAT was Rs 1,222 crore (up 45%) and ROE 13.1%.

segments.name: Retail Health
segments.commentary: Fresh retail grew 38% YoY in Q4 and 37% for FY26 (N basis); retail policies grew 11% in Q4 and 8% for FY26. Market share was 31.3% in FY26; retail loss ratio 64.8% in Q4 and 68.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Group Health / SME
segments.commentary: Management said SME was 78% of group business in FY26 versus 58% in FY25, with a recalibrated strategy that drove the group loss ratio improvement. No explicit group GWP figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management targets sustainable high-teen growth and mid-to-high-teen ROE.
Annual price increases will continue across all products; management said no change beyond normal pricing is foreseen, and about 80% of the book is to be repriced from Q4 FY26 through Q1 FY27.
Reporting moves to 1/n basis for business and growth from FY27.
NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth because of long-term policy sales, with catch-up expected in coming quarters.
Management expects the long-term share of NEP to keep rising next year.
Agent network to reach 1 million in two years, adding about 1 lakh agents a year.
capex_capacity: Home Healthcare, telemedicine and condition management usage rose 4-5x over the year, with Q4 consumption up about 9x. FY26 included over 90,000 telemedicine calls and over 40,000 pure telemedicine calls.
Claims platform migration to the Medi Assist platform is nearly complete, with the last product set to shift by Q1 FY27 end.
Customer app has over 14 million downloads and more than 1.5 million monthly active users; 95% of fresh premium is collected digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail Health premiums grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 versus 11.2% for non-life. For full FY26, retail health grew close to 20% and non-life 9.3%.
New-to-insurance share of fresh premium was 94% in Q4 (90% a year earlier) and 93% for FY26 (89% in FY25).
Volume retention improved 1-1.5% YoY; the company cited about 86-87% volume retention and a renewal ratio of 99%. GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps and NOP-based 100 bps.
Agent productivity rose about 37% on fresh and 18% on total business. Over 90% of retail comes from agency and D2C channels.
Senior citizens are about 20% of the portfolio; the senior citizen commission reduction took effect April 2024 (FY25) and drove part of the commission ratio gain.
Long-term vs annual NEP split is about 80:20, moving 100-150 bps toward long-term on premium basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will the retail loss ratio (about 68%) get back to 65-66% levels seen in FY23-24, and how will seasonal vector-borne claims be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said frequency and severity were managed in the high-single digits for FY26 and that Q4 benefited from lower frequency. It cited telemedicine and home healthcare usage growth and repricing of about 80% of the book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27, but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail growth lagging the industry, and how should the gap evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises quality and profitable geographies over market share. Its market share was 31.3% in FY26, growth on N basis was 39% for FY26, and the company is not chasing share at the cost of profit.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the loss ratio improvement: renewal book, new business, severity or fraud controls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain is a sum of parts: renewal repricing, sourcing quality, geography selection, and fraud, waste and abuse controls. Q4 frequency improvement cut across the whole book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the retention ratio uptick linked to long-term policies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the Q3/Q4 retention noise to renewals pulled into September after the GST cut, with some spillover into Q1. Volume retention improved 1-1.5% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for a major repricing in FY27, and is the current price rise enough for the target combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no need for above-normal increases. It expects the current annual pricing strategy to be sufficient to hit the target combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bima Sugam expected to affect sourcing and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bima Sugam is a consumer platform for affordable plans, that it will not be zero-cost, and that Star Health is a shareholder and supportive of it.

qa_highlights.question: Did the GST cut lift renewals and sum insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Walia said GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps, with customers opting for higher sum insured and riders, and that distributor income had risen over 50% since the GST announcement.

qa_highlights.question: Management did not answer on the EoM regulation's treatment of non-compliant companies and declined to comment on it, saying IRDAI guidance on EoM is awaited.

risks_watch: Retail loss ratio is still about 68% for FY26 versus the 65-66% seen in FY23-24; sustainability of the Q4 frequency improvement across a full cycle is unproven.
Equity-market volatility: Rs 558 crore Q4 MTM loss turned reported Q4 PAT negative; the normalised 8% yield is a new reporting basis.
NEP growth lagging GWP growth due to long-term policy sales; deferred revenue quantum was not disclosed and will be shared offline.
Pending IRDAI EoM / commission guidance and the Bima Sugam rollout could change distribution economics.
Growth gap versus industry retail growth (about 19% vs about 29% in Q4, per an analyst) persists; the company is prioritising profitable cohorts.
Group Health volume is being deliberately reduced; the SME mix is rising.
543412|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the loss ratio and underwriting turnaround, with specific metrics given throughout. Evasive on EoM regulation (declined to answer) and on the retail growth gap versus the industry, which was framed around profitability rather than share.

So, we are not desperate to grow our market share at the cost of profits.
It's a sum of all parts, right? It's not one can lay a finger on any one particular item.
We are probably the only company in this space operating within the current guidelines.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
543412|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail market share 29% vs 31% a year earlier; new-to-insurance mix in fresh retail 94% vs 90%. Proprietary channels (agency and D2C) are 90%+ of retail business.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

guidance_outlook: Insurance revenue growth is expected to rise from 13.4% towards 15-16% as the quarters progress, and to increase further in FY28.
Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.
Steady-state ROE target is mid-to-high teens on an Ind AS basis; no specific number given.
Fresh-business growth expected to moderate in H2 FY27 and into H1 FY28 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds; management agreed this framing.
capex_capacity: Agency network added about 20,000 agents in the quarter to 8.5 lakh; agent productivity up 19% YoY.
Non-metro fresh business growth is 3.5x metro growth.
Customer app has about 16 million downloads and 1.5 million+ monthly active users.
97% of new applications are digitally sourced; generative AI being layered on existing AI/ML claims analytics.
Long-term policies are about 40% of retail fresh business; fresh-to-renewal share about 20:80 in insurance revenue.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.question: How will GWP growth of 19% convert into insurance revenue growth, and when will they converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

risks_watch: Seasonal Q2 loss ratio pressure from vector-borne and infectious diseases.
Regulatory changes to commissions and claims reforms; management declined to comment until rules are final.

Fresh growth may moderate in H2 FY27 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds.
Other expenses rose about 23% YoY to Rs 283 crore, driven by loss of GST input credit and annual rate hikes.
Accounting questions open: finance income under PAA on long-term contracts (Rs 38.8 crore) and DAC balance were not fully explained.

543412|2026-09.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
543412|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. Normalized PAT (at an 8% investment yield) rose 70% YoY to Rs 390 crore in Q2. Management flagged that headline growth will moderate in H2 as last year's GST-led surge enters the base, and that regulatory proposals on distribution commissions and expense of management (EoM) are the next key uncertainty.

segments.name: Retail health (fresh)
segments.commentary: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% YoY in Q2 and 36% in H1 on reported 1/n basis; new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% from 89%, with new-to-insurance policies up over 10% and average sum insured up 13%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Network reached 8.7 lakh agents after adding 39,000 in H1; agency productivity up 19% YoY; agency contributes about 70-75% of fresh business and grew about 25% in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C grew 137% YoY in H1 and its share of business rose from 8% to 13%; management says D2C has superior combined ratios. Proprietary channels (agency plus D2C) account for over 90% of retail business.

segments.name: Renewal book
segments.commentary: Management says the standalone renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio; vintage book is about 80% of portfolio. Group business is now a very small share of premium.

guidance_outlook: Company aspires to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently over a long period and hopes to maintain that for FY27, though optical growth moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4 due to GST-led base.
ROE ambition to move from mid-teens to higher-teens over time, with combined ratio as the key lever.
Retail market share and like-for-like comparability under 1/n reporting expected to be restored only by FY28.
Management believes it has a credible path to the proposed EoM limits through operating leverage, productivity and digitization, but will give more detail once regulation is final.
Company will not disclose point-to-point guidance on individual loss ratio metrics.
capex_capacity: Equity allocation about 14% (slightly less than 14%), with internal strategy to cap at around 15%; management may go beyond 15% if markets are very attractive.

Portfolio duration increased toward a target of about 4 years after G-Sec yields rose; management said it has taken some long-duration G-Sec calls and may extend duration further if yields keep rising.
REITs and InvITs: fully invested against the 3% regulatory limit with a small margin of safety; AIF allocation about 2.1-2.2% of funds and growing slowly.
Digital SBU created last year; Salesforce CRM upgraded; AI bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume at under 20% of human cost.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is driven by a mix of price, volume and higher average sum insured; management did not split the contribution.
Around 80% of the book was repriced in the last cycle; the remaining portion is being repriced this year, with further correction as needed based on loss ratios.
Packages account for about 80% of claims; hospital negotiations described as business as usual, with the Supreme Court drug-pricing order not yet notified.
Management estimates a fresh-to-insurance market share near 40% (not a reported figure) and notes the reported fresh figure includes portability.
Commission ratio moderated YoY because the senior citizen commission cut (15% to 10%) and other efficiencies now show a full 12-month impact.

qa_highlights.question: How is fresh growth tracking in October and by channel, now that the GST-led base is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects optical moderation in Q3 and Q4 but aims for 20%+ fresh growth; it tracks policies sold, agent activations and digital activations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the loss ratio improvement driven by fresh business or by the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Improvement is driven by the vintage book (about 80% of portfolio), since the fresh book at about 20% of the portfolio could not drive it alone; renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio. Fresh and renewal loss ratios are not disclosed separately.

qa_highlights.question: Loss ratio decomposition in Q2 (frequency, severity, pricing) and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss cost held at mid-single-digit growth while earned premium grew close to double digits; management did not give point-to-point metric guidance and will focus on combined ratio going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Equity and duration positioning, and whether there is an equity cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity about 14%, no incremental purchases this quarter; the 15% level is an internal strategy, not a formal cap. Duration lengthened toward about 4 years via G-Sec calls.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to the Rs 59 crore investment-related loss and its FVTPL classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity, ETFs, REITs and InvITs are classified as FVTPL; debt is held to maturity. No breakdown of the Rs 59 crore between realized and unrealized was provided in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the insurance finance income and expense restatement, and will it stay nil?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance finance income and expense (significant financing component on long-term policies) was discontinued as an optional treatment; it is now nil and has no PAT impact because the offsetting income sits in restated insurance revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How are multi-year policies commissioned, and what is the impact of the proposed distribution rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Multi-year policies are around 50% of the fresh book; good agents are paid upfront under Indian GAAP and the amount is deferred under IFRS; clarification is awaited on whether years two and three count as fresh or renewal under the new rules.

543413|2026-03.headline: Tega Q4 FY26: FY26 revenue up 5% to INR17,736 mn, adjusted EBITDA 22%; consumables flat as orders slipped to Feb–Mar, and Molycop acquisition closed 1 June 2026.
543413|2026-03.overview: Tega reported FY26 revenue of INR17,736 mn (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR3,967 mn (22% margin), after exceptional items of INR775 mn (Molycop deal costs) and INR64 mn (labour code), with a further INR839 mn total labour-code charge cited. The Molycop acquisition completed on 1 June 2026 with Apollo Funds as a minority partner; consolidation starts from Q1 FY27, and management flagged about USD30 mn of transaction costs payable in Q1 and a target of 3x leverage in 3 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the revenue ramp is expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; it is early days, and quantified guidance will come in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Molycop's margin seasonal, is the current margin steady state, and are there one-off RM or macro items?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said there is little quarter-to-quarter seasonality, June was historically Molycop's strongest quarter, and margin should be relatively flat in coming quarters. Molycop manages to per-ton margin because about 85% of contracts are steel-index linked.

qa_highlights.question: Chile plant commissioning status?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the plant is on track for soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory clearances expected within a two-month window.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any further one-time costs beyond the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka confirmed the Q1 one-time costs are the full amount. The analyst tallied INR110cr this year plus about INR75-80cr last year, totalling about INR190cr, which management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Group and Molycop debt levels and year-end expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi said group total debt is INR112bn including about INR26bn of redeemable preference shares. Patrick Koley said Molycop net debt was USD672mn at June 30 and is expected to fall by year-end, with ABL swings driven by bar payments.

qa_highlights.question: Molycop capex and volume outlook, plus Latin America competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said 10-month capex is about USD28mn, normalised capex is in the low USD30mn range, and volume is expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on a 10-month comparable basis. Volume was 1.204mt for the 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year. Lance Dawber said Molycop has competed with China for decades and retains its lead through lead times and local support.

543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
543415|2026-06.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

543417|2026-06.headline: RateGain Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR785 crores (up 188% YoY, 17.5% organic) and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 22.5-23.5%.
543417|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was RateGain's highest-ever quarter, with revenue of INR785 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR193.4 crores at a 24.6% margin, helped by a one-time USD2.5 million FIFA World Cup uplift. Organic growth for the combined Sojern-Adara entity was 17.5% YoY in INR terms. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to around INR3,100 crores (upper end of the earlier range) and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 22.5-23.5%, up about 100 bps. Debt repayment continued, with USD47.5 million repaid (38% of the acquisition loan), and management expects to be net debt-free by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR6.8 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Net debt INR615.4 crores; cash INR255.6 crores; net worth INR2,114.2 crores (as of June 30, 2026)

segments.name: Martech
segments.commentary: Now over 81% of revenue; grew 341% YoY on consolidation of Sojern, with organic growth of about 18.2%. Destination, property and corporate sub-segments all cited growth, with APMEA new customer wins up 200% YoY.

segments.name: DaaS
segments.commentary: Grew 22.7% YoY with healthy performance across Air, OTA and Car. Management expects airline large deals and revAI order book to add upside.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 3.1% YoY, described as modest. Management is betting on Agentic ARI, RateIQ and the direct stack, and expects double-digit growth by fiscal year end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue now expected at the upper end of the prior range, around INR3,100 crores, implying 70% YoY growth and double-digit growth for the combined base.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 22.5-23.5% from 21.5-22.5%.
One-time FIFA uplift of USD2.5 million is not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2; management expects revenue to normalize marginally.
Management aspires to grow 15-20% in the near to medium term and sees the higher end of that range for FY27 exit; it expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger.
Sojern deferred consideration of about INR80-90 crores a year (INR20-22 crores per quarter add-back) runs until Q3 FY29.
FCF conversion of 75% or better expected for full FY27; net debt-free by FY28.
Gross margin expected to remain around 70% in the near term; management says upside is possible but will not commit yet.
M&A expected in 2027, not in 2026, despite debt prepayment.
capex_capacity: Debt: additional USD16 million repaid after quarter end; cumulative USD47.5 million repaid (38% of original loan), outstanding USD77.5 million.
Shared AI-powered platform across Martech, Distribution and DaaS; no capacity or capex figures disclosed.
Product launches in Q1: Parity Plus next generation, ChatGPT ads on property, AI Digest for AirGain, Uno Viva extended to 50+ languages including WhatsApp.
Property-side team unification complete in APAC; Europe and US still to be unified, which management expects to accelerate deal velocity.
demand_pricing: Middle East revenue fell from about USD970,000 a month pre-disruption to about USD425,000 a month currently; treated as a headwind with recovery potential.

Pricing power: management says discounting need has fallen since Sojern and Adara stopped competing; a regional Indian chain is being signed at higher outcome-based fees; destination competitors are weak and one approached RateGain to be bought out.
Contract wins are reported as new logos only and exclude upsizing of existing customers; management is revising KPI reporting. The quarterly run rate of about INR96-98 crores was cited by an analyst.
RateIQ is in discussions with about a dozen customers; management cited 10-100% booking uplifts for some chain pairings. Uno Viva is near a very large Middle East customer win.
Airbnb is a customer, not a competitor; management says it provides connectivity and DaaS to Airbnb.

qa_highlights.question: Are there examples of pricing power in the combined entity, and will deal velocity improve after people integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reduced need to discount in destinations, higher outcome-based fees with a large Indian regional chain, and weaker distant competitors. It expects deal velocity to rise as the Europe and US property teams are unified.

qa_highlights.question: Is organic growth in INR and could the exit run rate near 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed 17.5% organic growth is in INR. Management sees the higher end of the 15-20% range and expects acceleration in Q3 and Q4, while noting FIFA is not large and revenue is mostly recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the one-off items?
qa_highlights.answer: Net one-off of about USD1 million (USD2.5 million FIFA less about USD1.5 million Middle East dip), with about 70% gross margin implying roughly USD600,000-700,000 of EBITDA benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Can Sojern alone be assumed to run at about 30% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to attribute margins; synergies come from both Adara and Sojern and the businesses are now one team and platform, so attribution is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why are contract wins and distribution growth low?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract wins count only new logos and understate upsizing. Distribution grew 3.1%; management expects double-digit growth by year end on direct stack and RateIQ traction, plus airline large deals in DaaS.

qa_highlights.question: Is Martech organic growth disclosed separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Martech grew about 18.2% organically; it declined to split Sojern from Adara because teams and platforms are unified.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to stay similar near term; a rise is possible but not committed. M&A is possible in 2027 but nothing expected in 2026.

risks_watch: One-time FIFA uplift (USD2.5 million) and Middle East revenue decline (about USD1 million a month lower) affect Q1 comparability; Q2 normalization.
Distribution growth (3.1%) lags DaaS and Martech; newer launches need to convert to revenue.
Contract-win KPI definition is being revised, so the reported figures are not comparable with prior disclosures.
Deferred Sojern consideration of INR80-90 crores a year runs to Q3 FY29, while other income fell sharply to INR3.1 crores.
Management did not attribute margins between Adara and Sojern, which limits visibility into the acquired business's economics.
543417|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on growth and margins, with management raising guidance. It was less forthcoming on specifics: it declined to split Sojern and Adara figures, would not commit to a gross margin increase, and was vague on contract-win metrics.
key_quotes: We now expect full-year revenue to come in at the upper end of the range we shared with you last quarter, around INR3,100 crores for FY27.

On margins, we now expect adjusted EBITDA margins of between 22.5 % to 23.5% for FY27, roughly 100 basis points or 1 percentage point uplift from the earlier 21.5 % to 22.5% range I shared with you last quarter.
This quarter marked a shift from building the foundations on one RateGain to operating as one company.
Airbnb is a B2C. It's in the area of vacation rental. Airbnb is actually a big customer of RateGain.

543417|2026-09.headline: RateGain Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR745 crore (+153% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA margin 22.7%; FY27 guidance maintained, corporate MarTech down ~14% organically in H1.
543417|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth from the Sojern consolidation, with operating revenue of INR735.4 crore (call opening cited INR745 crore) and adjusted EBITDA of INR169.1 crore at a 22.7% adjusted margin. Sequentially revenue fell about INR40 crore from Q1, which management attributed to the non-recurring FIFA World Cup benefit (about USD2.5 million in Q1) and normal Q2 seasonality in destination marketing. Organic growth for the combined entity was 15.7% in H1 and 14% in Q2, above the 12-15% FY27 guidance band. Management maintained FY27 revenue guidance at the upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore and the 22.5-23.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, and reiterated net debt-free by FY28. Corporate MarTech, which fell about 14% organically in H1 (close to 20% in constant currency per management's later remark), was the main drag and is the key H2 watch item.

financial_highlights.value: INR735.4 crore (call opening cited INR745 crore)
financial_highlights.change: +152.6% YoY; down about INR40 crore QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (adds back Sojern deferred consideration of INR16.1 crore)
financial_highlights.value: INR169.1 crore, margin 22.7%; H1 adjusted margin 23.7%

segments.name: MarTech (over 80% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 300% YoY in Q2 largely from Sojern consolidation. Properties (44.7% of MarTech revenue) and destinations (39.7%) each grew more than 20% organically in H1; the two together are about 84% of MarTech.

segments.name: MarTech – Corporate (15.6% of MarTech)
segments.commentary: Declined about 14% organically in H1 (about 20% in USD terms per management's Q&A remark). Management expects it broadly flat in H2 and is changing leadership and organising sales by vertical.

segments.name: DaaS
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY in Q2 and 14% in H1. Management guides double-digit rupee growth for FY27; AirGain added Philippine Airlines (July), Vietjet Qazaqstan (August) and Vietnam Airlines (October).

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Broadly flat YoY in Q2. FY27 guided to single-digit growth, with Smart Distribution now live (over 800 directly contracted properties connected) and FY28 double-digit growth targeted.

segments.commentary: Record Q2 with new sales of about USD2 million, more than 3x a year ago. Over 50 properties signed on the direct stack in Q2. Middle East revenue run rate was about USD500,000 a month in Q2, versus about USD970,000 before the disruption and USD425,000 in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue maintained at the upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore, consistent with 12-15% organic growth over pro forma FY26.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin maintained at 22.5-23.5%, as guided last quarter.
Growth expected to build through H2, with corporate moving from about 20% constant-currency decline in H1 to roughly flat in H2.
DaaS guided to double-digit rupee growth in FY27; distribution single-digit in FY27, with double-digit targeted in FY28.
Net debt-free by FY28; management now says net debt positive by end of FY28 (wording inconsistent on the call). Medium-term aspiration remains 15% organic constant-currency growth.
capex_capacity: Sojern acquisition loan: USD53.75 million repaid so far (about 43% of original loan), including a payment on November 5, 2026.
USD40 million of debt refinanced at SOFR plus 165 bps.
Reinvestment of spend above 20% EBITDA margin directed mainly to commercial and sales & marketing teams; AI reduces product build costs.
Cloudbeds property ramp-up planned for October; Duetto commercial ramp-up pending after partner testing.
Commission for experiences launched in beta for attractions; TikTok agreement signed and connected TV being added for corporate.
demand_pricing: Properties and destinations are growing above 20%; new property additions on the commission model continue, with churn of low-performing "bronze and orange" hotels a stated concern.
Most new wins came from MarTech, mainly properties; pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech.
DMO business fell about 21% QoQ in Q2 (seasonal, July-September budget cycles) but grew more than 20% YoY on a like-to-like basis.
Management sees no impact from Google AI-mode shifts on property marketing budgets; says AI channel shift is manageable and scraping in DaaS is protected by data partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments and industries drove Q2 deal wins, and will this win pace continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Most wins came from MarTech properties (hotels); pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech. Management credited cross-sell in APMEA (team grew from about 15 to 100 people) and a global key accounts team for the top 10 accounts.

qa_highlights.question: How does organic growth reach 15% constant currency from roughly 9-10% normalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said arresting the corporate decline could add about 200-300 bps, and properties and destinations (over 80% of MarTech, growing above 20%) could accelerate further if churn is reduced.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be treated given team build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable with anything above 20% and will reinvest above that, mainly in commercial and sales teams; AI is lowering the cost of product build.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance dependent on a DMO recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 growth also depends on corporate moving from about 20% constant-currency decline in H1 to flattish, alongside DMO seasonal recovery in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin expansion linked to currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Garg said currency benefit is not meaningful because most revenue and cost is USD-based; Bhanu Chopra attributed margin gains to cost synergies from merging Sojern and Adara platforms and shared HR and finance services.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI pose a fundamental risk to DaaS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing anti-blocking technology, formal data partnerships with subscribers, and data purchases; monetisation is per data volume regardless of channel (APIs or LLM interfaces such as Claude or ChatGPT via MCP).

risks_watch: Corporate MarTech: H1 decline of about 14% organically (about 20% in USD) must flatten in H2 for guidance; management acknowledged the segment was deprioritised under Sojern.
Middle East: revenue run rate still about 48% below pre-disruption levels (USD500,000 vs USD970,000 a month); management called it a continuing headwind.
Property churn: pay-for-performance model with low-performing hotels churning; management expects the integrated stack to reduce it, unproven so far.
Q3 and Q4 must grow sequentially to reach the upper end of INR3,100 crore, which depends on DMO seasonal recovery and corporate stabilisation.
Cash flow: H1 EBITDA-to-FCF conversion of 87% was flattered by one-time Sojern collections; net debt-free timing needs watching.
543417|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the core MarTech properties and destinations business and APMEA, but candid and cautious on corporate MarTech, which management says needs fixing. Some answers on AI, Europe and pipeline were hedged or unclear, and the call contained several numeric inconsistencies (INR735.4 vs INR745 crore revenue, and "net debt-free" vs "net debt positive" by FY28).
key_quotes: We are maintaining our guidance of revenue that we expect to be at the upper end of the INR3,000 crore-INR3,100 crores range that we had shared in the beginning of the year.
Our medium-term aspiration remains 15% organic growth, constant currency year-on-year growth.

The margin expansion that you have seen is not a result of anything to do with currency. It's really the cost synergies that we were able to realize as a result of taking all the platforms that we had, especially Sojern and Adara, and make it into one platform.
We only get paid if we deliver bookings for our customers, so it's an outcome-based model.

rows.why: Commission for experiences in beta for attractions, TikTok agreement signed with connected TV being added for corporate, and Cloudbeds property ramp planned for October.

543419|2026-03.headline: Shriram Properties FY26 revenue rose 39% to INR1,357 crores and net profit crossed INR100 crores for the first time, with FY27 guidance of INR3,300-3,500 crores sales value.
543419|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,357 crores (+39% YoY) and net profit rose 30% to INR101 crores, driven by a strong Q4 handover push in Bangalore, Chennai and Kolkata. Full-year sales value was flat at INR2,354 crores, with Q4 sales of INR663 crores, as several launches slipped due to approval delays, mainly in Bangalore. Management guided FY27 to be stronger than FY26, with sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores, collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units. Analysts pressed on margins, the rising other-expense line, the cash flow trend, and the funding of new land acquisitions; management said these would be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly intermittent debt.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Core market; Songs of the Earth launch sold over 85% in launch year. Management says the growth strategy is centred on Bangalore and Pune, with North Bangalore flagged for higher pricing upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Maiden launch at Undri (Spectrum) sold over 300 units in under a year, against roughly 850 units absorbed annually by the micro-market over the last three years. Pune revenue is recognised under percentage-of-completion.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Land settlement with the Government of West Bengal done; 314 acres originally, 42 acres surrendered, 100+ acres still available. Skyblooms Villas over 50% sold and Signature Square about 40% sold at launch. Approval exists for 2.3 million sq ft of apartments, with plotted development planned.

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Contributed to Q4 revenue recognition from completed projects; a launch is expected within about a week of the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 5-5.5 million sq ft and sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores.
FY27 collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units.
FY27 pipeline addition of 7-8 million sq ft and GDV addition of INR5,000-6,000 crores; land-related capital commitment of INR350-400 crores.
FY27 project completions of about 3.8 million sq ft, with revenue recognition potential of about INR1,740 crores.
Mission FY28 targets: sales of INR5,000 crores, revenue of INR2,500 crores and PBT of INR250 crores; management reiterated PBT margin of 10-11%.
Management expects 8-9% PAT margin on a normalised 3-year basis, with the effective tax rate below 25% due to carried-forward losses.
Construction capital spend of INR900-1,000 crores expected in FY27, versus roughly INR90-95 crores per quarter recently.
Finance costs may decline slightly, but gross debt of about INR600 crores will continue; the company may take intermittent bridge debt.
capex_capacity: Ongoing projects: 16.7 million sq ft, 85% sold; 2.6 million sq ft unsold in ongoing projects, plus 18.6 million sq ft upcoming pipeline; total unsold potential over 21 million sq ft, GDV about INR13,950 crores.
Seven projects acquired during FY26; approvals under way; over 7 million sq ft expected to enter the launch pipeline in the next 3-6 months. Target to double the upcoming pipeline in 18-24 months.
FY26 completed and delivered 8 projects, about 4 million sq ft. FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata.

New business development investment of INR372 crores in FY26, one of the highest annual outlays; about 80% of cumulative operating cash of over INR900 crores over four years was reinvested into new projects.
Liquidity of over INR520 crores: cash of INR172 crores plus undrawn funding lines of INR358 crores. Equity about INR1,460 crores; cost of debt 11.2%; CRISIL A-/Positive.
demand_pricing: FY26 sales value INR2,354 crores (marginal increase); sales volume 4.15 million sq ft; Q4 sales INR663 crores. Management said a couple of Q4 launches slipped into Q1 FY27.

Pricing: management expects organic price growth of no more than 5-6% a year, against 8-10% construction cost inflation; margin protection rather than expansion is the aim. Tiles, paints and PVC windows face 5-10% price pressure.
Management flagged IT employment trends, interest rate affordability and longer sales cycles as sector risks; focus is on mid and upper-mid housing.
Kolkata: management said the new state government is positive. Long-term outlook strong, but near-term recovery expected to be slower than Bangalore or Pune.
Competition: management said the market favours branded and organised developers.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising operating cash outflows and higher new-project investment lead to a cash crunch or more debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 free cash flow fell slightly due to construction spend ahead of finishing stages; no additional debt is needed for construction, as liquidity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR126 crores to INR172 crores, and will they rise further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said higher accelerated revenue recognition (about INR1,200 crores vs about INR800 crores) brought about INR25 crores of brokerage charges, with INR7 crores impairment on Bengal land and INR10 crores of provisions; he said other expenses should not rise in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What PBT and PAT margins should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said PBT margin of 10-11% is the target; PAT margin is expected to be 8-9% on a normalised 3-year basis, because the effective tax rate may be below 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 presales slightly below the INR2,600 crore guidance, and why are there few Kolkata launches?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said a couple of projects slipped into Q1 FY27, with one launched that week and another in Chennai in about a week. Kolkata plotted development is being tested before the remaining 100+ acres are monetised; 2.3 million sq ft of apartment approval is already in hand.

qa_highlights.question: When will construction spend ramp up, and how much new project investment is planned in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said construction capital spend is expected at INR900-1,000 crores in FY27. The 8 million sq ft pipeline addition implies INR350-400 crores of land commitment, to be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly bridge debt.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,000 crore revenue recognition potential over three years conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said ongoing projects alone can deliver about INR4,400 crores, to be unlocked in 2-3 years. Upside exists from Kolkata and the pipeline, but management preferred conservative guidance.

risks_watch: Approval delays (approvals, e-Khata, OCs, Kaveri portal) that caused FY26 launch slippage and could affect FY27 launches of about 6 million sq ft.
Other expenses (INR172 crores) and provisions, including the INR10 crore recoverable from a landowner; management said these should not rise in FY27.
Operating cash flow fell YoY, and construction capex is set to rise to INR900-1,000 crores in FY27; monitor collections against the INR2,100-2,200 crore guidance.
Rising material costs (tiles, paints, PVC) and limited ability to pass on price increases beyond 5-6%.
Finance costs and net debt; management said gross debt of about INR600 crores will stay and bridge debt may be taken.
Q1 FY27 launch execution: Chennai project and Kolkata plotted development.

key_quotes: Therefore, while we remain cautious in the near term in terms of our guidance to the market on FY '27 KPIs, we are fully geared to seize the opportunities in the market and sustain our growth momentum in FY '27 and beyond.

But for now, I think it will be better to be conservative than saying something which is very big and then pulling back.

rows.why: Seven projects acquired in FY26 with over 7 million sq ft expected to enter launch pipeline in 3-6 months, and FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; approvals still under way and FY26 launches slipped on approval delays.

543419|2026-06.headline: Shriram Properties posted record Q1 FY27 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) but revenue of INR271 crores (+4%) and PAT of INR11 crores lag, with growth back-ended.

Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance, pointing to Q2 and H2 OCs (about 2,900 units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential) and a back-ended launch calendar. qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR2,500 crores revenue, INR250 crores PBT) still intact and how credible is a 10% PBT margin versus historic EBITDA of 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.
