qa_highlights.question: Dubai acquisition: business mix, geographic coverage, synergies, valuation, and financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The target (NatWest) covers UAE, Gulf and Saudi. Valuation was based on future orders from its promoters' linked customers. The deal is not complete, so no FY27 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Ocean freight: capabilities, carrier partnerships and medium-term revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Ocean team is centralised in Delhi; relationships with about 8–9 major shipping lines. No medium-term revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 41% Q2 YoY revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given. Management cited a sales process for volume growth and route-specific pricing, with fuel costs affecting freight rates.

qa_highlights.question: Courier shipments and tonnage decreased YoY; what is the driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to new routes (direct flights to destinations like Germany), new e-commerce customers and organic growth at existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil/South America: current stage and milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: A senior person hired in Brazil; inquiries have turned into some business. Own operations are possible in about a year once volumes increase.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company own land, and will margins improve with volume?
qa_highlights.answer: No land is owned and all warehouses are leased. Management expects margins and bottom line to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat.

risks_watch: Revenue split between volume and price for the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not disclosed.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) valuation rests on future orders and is incomplete; NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr.
Fuel-linked freight rate volatility and geopolitical route disruption could affect margins.
Thin PAT margin of about 1.5% leaves little buffer against cost swings.
Courier volume decline YoY was raised by an analyst but only partly reconciled by management.
Retail courier and tech platform (end-2026) are unproven; ocean freight and South America remain early-stage.
543420|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth plans and margin outlook, but answers were often unstructured and gave few quantified targets (no ocean revenue target, no acquisition financials, no volume/price split).
key_quotes: Whatever our margins are, even if the Freight is double, tripled, we'll still maintain our margins.
Currently, we do not have any warehouses that are owned, everything is leased.
So, margin, bottom line, you will see increasing quarter on quarter and year on year, definitely.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it aims to roughly double the PAT margin from about 1.5% and expects margins to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat, but fuel-driven freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026 and the H1 EBITDA margin is only 4.58%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: All warehouses are leased, no land or owned warehouses, and existing infrastructure is said to handle about double current volume, so no new physical capacity is quantified in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 tonnage rose about 32.84% (545 to 744 tons) and shipments about 56% (430 to 674), with ~70 Gulf charters since March and one customer's volume reportedly doubling, supporting the ₹580-600 Cr FY27 revenue guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with all warehouses leased and no capex discussed; infrastructure said to handle about double current volume, so utilisation pressure is not evident.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ₹580-600 Cr with H1 EBITDA at ₹12.5 Cr, but the brief gives no implied H2 run-rate and the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not split between volume and price.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Thin 1.5% PAT margin leaves little buffer, and fuel-linked freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026; the courier volume decline YoY was only partly reconciled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Retail B2C courier launched in October 2026 and a tech booking/rate platform is expected by end-2026, but neither has a revenue target and both are unproven.

rows.label: Dubai acquisition (NatWest) and South America entry
rows.why: Dubai deal is not complete with little FY27 contribution expected and NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr; South America has a senior hire in Brazil with local operations possible in about a year if volumes build.

rows.label: Ocean freight build-out
rows.why: Ocean freight is small today, centralised in Delhi with 8-9 shipping lines, and targeted for bulk and rice growth, but no revenue target was given and it will be taken slowly.

rows.label: Fuel-driven route-specific freight rate pressure
rows.why: Management expects fuel-driven freight rate pressure to persist at least until end-2026, and says it passes through cost changes while industry margins run 7-25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue of ₹580-600 Cr, margin doubling and new ventures, but was vague on the volume/price split, Dubai financials and ocean targets, while analysts pressed on the courier volume decline and the mix of the 41% Q2 growth.

543425|2026-03.headline: MapmyIndia Q4 FY26: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY), but FY26 revenue only INR474 crore vs INR463 crore.
543425|2026-03.overview: Management reported a sharp sequential Q4 recovery: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA up 141% QoQ, PAT up 171% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 44.6% and PAT margin at 31.3%. Full-year FY26 growth was muted, with revenue moving from INR463 crore to INR474 crore, as government contracts were delayed or deferred into FY27. Management attributed the Q4 shortfall against its own expectations (about INR45-50 crore by an analyst's estimate) to customer-side delays of roughly INR20 crore in an automotive IoT order plus government push-outs, all described as timing rather than lost business. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY28 roadmap and an order book of about INR1,750 crore, but gave no formal FY27 growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR463 crore in FY25 (c.1-2% growth)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.50 per share (175% on INR2 face value)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR133 crore in March 2025 (per analyst)

segments.name: A&M (Automotive & Mobility)
segments.commentary: Grew about 9% for FY26 per management. Q4 automotive core business described as soft by an analyst; management said a Hyundai-related variation was a drag, while attach rates and program presence rose YoY.

segments.name: C&E (Consumer & Enterprise, incl. Government)
segments.commentary: Declined about 3% for FY26, which management attributed to government contracts delayed into FY27. C&E rose 142% QoQ in Q4. Government open order book closed above INR200 crore; government billing crossed INR100 crore and cash collection crossed INR100 crore in FY26.

segments.name: IoT-led business
segments.commentary: Management said IoT EBITDA margin rose from 14% in FY25 to 16% in FY26, with Q4 margin at about 33%. Management called this a quarterly high driven by operating leverage and a better SaaS mix, not a one-off.

segments.name: Mappls App
segments.commentary: Cumulative downloads above 45 million, with 10+ million added during FY26. Amazon Now was cited as a corporate API/SDK integration example, with rollout in Bengaluru and Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of growth 'above 20%' in FY27 per the 5-year trajectory, and an analyst asked whether 25% growth is achievable; management said there was 'no reason not to believe' 25% growth is possible but gave no formal number.
INR1,000 crore revenue roadmap for FY28 is unchanged; timing is under review year by year.
Open order book about INR1,750 crore (including 18% GST); billing about INR520 crore and sales about INR470 crore in the order book breakup.
Management expects the INR20 crore IoT order delayed in Q4 to reflect in Q1 and Q2 FY27, and government push-outs to Q1-Q2 FY27.
Management plans to change segment reporting from FY27 Q1 to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government, with restated FY26 quarterly figures.
Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27 and sees steady-state IoT margins above 16%.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation in FY26 was about INR120 crore for organic growth (government, IoT, intellectual property); small acquisitions were minor.
IoT hardware is capitalised as fixed assets and depreciated over 3 years under the opex subscription model, so IoT growth needs capital.

Inventory of IoT devices rose to support expected demand; management said purchases are based on portfolio forecasts, not specific orders, and that hardware price inflation is being offset through pricing and value engineering.
Government business requires working capital, mainly receivables, to fund delayed payments at Mappls DT and Gtropy.
No specific capex amount for FY27 was given.
demand_pricing: FY26 open order book began at about INR1,500 crore; about 18% (c.INR270 crore) converted to revenue, and INR780 crore of in-year new orders produced about INR200 crore of in-year revenue (about 25%).
Management said the FY26 conversion rate could be 'higher' in FY27, but gave no number.

Fixed-price contracts are used in government (milestone-based), corporate (lump-sum or minimum guarantee) and IoT (fixed fleet size or minimum guarantee, 3-5 year SaaS terms). Management described fixed-price visibility as 'very clear', with volume contracts historically flexing up.

Government receivables: management said there have been almost no bad debts in government, but collection periods are longer. Trade receivables rose from INR133 crore to INR176 crore YoY (per analyst), against flat revenue.
Management said a government 'Large Energy response system' order and a large government IoT tender (re-tendered) were delayed, outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a weak full-year performance in automotive/mobility and consumer-enterprise, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total FY26 revenue was INR474 crore vs INR463 crore; C&E fell about 3% because government work was delayed and A&M grew about 9%. Q4 C&E rose 142% QoQ. The government order book is above INR200 crore, and management is confident of significant growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book to revenue conversion outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book. Management declined to give a fixed range but said FY27 could be higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan for the roughly INR600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth comes first (IoT, government, IP). IoT hardware is capitalised and depreciated over 3 years, and government needs working capital. No acquisition, dividend or buyback plan was detailed beyond the FY26 final dividend.

qa_highlights.question: Where was the Q4 revenue shortfall of about INR45-50 crore vs expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly INR20 crore automotive IoT order delayed by customer regulatory requirements (now fulfilled, expected in Q1-Q2), a government Large Energy Response order delayed by the government, and a large government IoT tender sent to re-tender. Management called these push-outs, not lost business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is core C&E flat, and will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate API/SDK revenue ramps with usage (Amazon Now cited), with a gestation period. Segment reporting will move to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government from Q1 FY27 with restated quarterly FY26 figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and is there a collection concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government receivables reflect a longer collection cycle with no material bad debt; Mappls DT collected prior-year receivables, with overdue amounts expected to be lower than total receivables. DSO was described as better than industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IoT margins rise to about 33% in Q4 and is inventory a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to operating leverage, better mix (more SaaS) and cost optimisation, and denied inventory gains. Inventory rose to meet expected IoT demand. Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27.

risks_watch: Execution timing: revenue conversion is lumpy and dependent on customer readiness and government approvals; Q4 slippage of about INR45-50 crore by analyst estimate.
Receivables: trade receivables rose about 32% YoY to INR176 crore against flat revenue; watch DSO and government collections in Q1 FY27.
IoT input cost inflation (DRAM/NAND prices cited by an analyst) versus rising IoT margins; watch whether margins hold and whether inventory-linked gains recur.
Geopolitical and government budget pressure cited by an analyst; management said it saw no change to business as usual.
Revenue CAGR of 1-2% in FY26 versus the 25-30% growth an analyst asked about; watch Q1 FY27 for conversion to a FY27 growth rate and the FY28 INR1,000 crore target.
Segment reporting change from Q1 FY27 will affect comparability.
543425|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat about the Q4 inflection and FY27 pipeline, but became defensive and less specific when pressed on the FY26 shortfall, the revenue gap, and receivables. It gave no quantified FY27 guidance and declined to name accounts or quantify the delayed government orders.
key_quotes: Q4 marked a positive inflection point with improving business activity and stronger execution.
So our road map continues with INR1,000 crores. The team, the entire leadership team is working on it.
The gap is maybe 5 accounts or 6 accounts, but the orders exist.
Our first priority, which we believe is the right way to do is to provide organic growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY) and IoT margin about 33% in Q4 vs 16% FY26; management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27, though Q4 level is a quarterly high and IoT input costs (DRAM/NAND) are rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or branch capacity was discussed; IoT device inventory was built for expected demand but no capacity addition was guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Open order book about INR1,750 crore with government order book above INR200 crore; FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book, and management says FY27 conversion could be higher, with growth above 20% expected and 25% possible.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capital allocation was about INR120 crore for organic growth and IoT hardware is capitalised, but no FY27 capex amount was given and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said there is 'no reason not to believe' 25% FY27 growth is possible, but gave no formal number and Q1-Q2 FY27 depends on delayed orders converting.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue grew only about 1-2% to INR474 crore, with a Q4 shortfall of about INR45-50 crore by analyst estimate; trade receivables rose about 32% YoY to INR176 crore and government timing could slip again.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product, model or molecule launch was discussed; Mappls App and Amazon Now integration rollout is ongoing, not a new launch.

rows.label: Delayed government and IoT orders convert in Q1-Q2 FY27
rows.why: Management expects the INR20 crore IoT order and government push-outs to reflect in Q1 and Q2 FY27, against an open order book of about INR1,750 crore.

rows.label: Receivables build from government collections
rows.why: Trade receivables rose from INR133 crore to INR176 crore YoY (about 32%) against flat revenue, and government collection periods are longer; management says no material bad debt.

rows.label: Segment reporting change to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government
rows.why: Management committed to the change from Q1 FY27 with restated FY26 quarterly figures, which will affect comparability.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q4 inflection, IoT margins at 33% and a 1,750 crore order book, but turned defensive on the FY26 revenue shortfall and receivables; analysts pressed on the 1-2% FY26 growth, the INR45-50 crore Q4 gap and the 25-30% growth question.

543425|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore and EBITDA margin was 40.2%, despite a one-time INR4 crore government receivable write-off.
543425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR56.1 crore (40.2% margin) and PAT up 8.6% to INR49.7 crore (31.2% margin). Management said a one-time write-off of a government client's receivable (about INR4 crore gross, INR0.8 crore net P&L hit after a INR3.2 crore offset) cut the EBITDA margin by roughly 4 percentage points, with the balance sitting in other income. The company moved to a new three-segment reporting structure (Automotive, Enterprise, Government) and appointed Rohan Verma as Joint MD. IoT-led revenue rose sharply while Map-led revenue was nearly flat, and management attributed Automotive softness in FY26 H2 to OEM time-shifting rather than contract loss.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR98.2 crore in Q1 FY26 (flat)
vs INR23.4 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR4 crore gross; INR0.8 crore net P&L impact
financial_highlights.change: Offset by INR3.2 crore payable not paid; net effect booked in other expense/other income
vs INR7 crore (as cited for IoT-led comparison)
vs INR16.3 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Revenue INR58.8 crore in Q1 FY27, up 29% YoY from INR45.7 crore; FY26 full year INR190 crore vs INR182 crore in FY25, with H2 FY26 time-shifting of OEM vehicles cited as a drag.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Revenue INR64 crore, up 6% YoY from INR60.6 crore; wins cited across mobility and logistics, BFSI, manufacturing, telecom and renewable energy.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Government revenue was not disclosed for the quarter; management said Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter for Government and the write-off related to one government client.

segments.name: Map-led vs IoT-led
segments.commentary: Map-led flat at INR98.7 crore (from INR98.2 crore); IoT-led up to INR41 crore from INR23.4 crore, driving consolidated growth.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated an internal target of 35%+ EBITDA margin for FY27 and declined to guide quarter-by-quarter; asked about 43-44% margins, it said quarterly outcomes will vary.

Open order book at FY26 end was INR1,750 crore, up from INR1,500 crore a year earlier (and about INR1,350 crore before that); management cited it as visibility for future growth but would not comment on quarterly revenue.
Management expects Automotive contract volumes to recover as OEMs change vehicle programmes, but gave no quantitative FY27 Automotive growth target.
International: Southeast Asia JV loss reduced; international revenue not material to P&L in the near term; smaller investments in Middle East and other geographies.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were discussed on the call.
IoT hardware-first growth is expected to convert into SaaS revenue over time, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book split disclosed only annually as fixed-price versus volume-based; not disclosed quarterly for competitive reasons.
Pricing is bespoke, per vehicle, per API transaction, per user or per solution; contract tenure ranges from one to five years with no typical term.
Management said receivables from government are a longer cycle than Automotive and Enterprise; majority of FY26 receivables of INR176 crore were from government (exact share not given).
Digital twin cities opportunity (including Maharashtra's NAKSHA scheme) is being pursued selectively to avoid bad receivables seen at peers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Automotive OEM contract reduction a 2H FY26 event, and could 2H FY27 be better on a weaker base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not a contract reduction but time-shifting: one OEM chose not to deploy the technology in some vehicles last year, which may continue, though more vehicles are expected to carry the technology in future.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin run at 43-44% in coming quarters excluding the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 35%+ full-year margin target and said quarterly margins will vary.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone Map-led growth so low and subsidiary revenue down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated numbers should be used, as Government and IoT work is routed through subsidiaries; consolidated Map-led was flat at INR98.7 crore while IoT-led rose to INR41 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Order book mix by segment and e-commerce deal progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book split by segment was not disclosed; the fixed versus volume split is given annually. Management cited quick commerce and other enterprise wins without quantifying them.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile the write-off: INR80 lakh P&L impact vs 4% EBITDA margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The gross INR4 crore receivable was offset by a INR3.2 crore payable not paid; the net INR0.8 crore went to other expense, while the payable saving sat in other income, so the EBITDA margin was hit by about 4 points.

qa_highlights.question: Is IoT services revenue seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IoT services follow hardware sales with a lag and billing cycles vary (monthly to biennial), so sequential comparisons mislead; Q1 FY27 IoT services INR18 crore vs INR16.3 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is there material international revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said international revenue is not material and the Southeast Asia JV loss has reduced.

risks_watch: Government receivables: longer collection cycle and a one-time write-off this quarter; watch the government receivable balance and any further write-offs.
Map-led revenue flat YoY at INR98.7 crore; growth is now dependent on IoT-led and Automotive recovery.
IoT hardware-led growth carries lower margin until SaaS converts; margin dilution expected to persist as IoT scales.
Automotive OEM programme timing: continued time-shifting could keep the segment below its potential in the near term.
Southeast Asia JV and other international investments remain loss-making with no near-term material revenue.
543425|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the order book and diversification, but evasive on quarterly guidance, segment order mix, pricing and government receivable details, deferring to the investor presentation or offline follow-up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Open order book rose to INR1,750 crore from INR1,500 crore a year earlier (about 17%), and IoT-led revenue grew to INR41 crore from INR23.4 crore, but Map-led revenue was flat at INR98.7 crore and no quantitative volume target was given.

rows.why: Management gave no quantitative revenue guidance and kept only the 35%+ margin target, so there is no guided upgrade to anticipate.

rows.why: Order book rose to INR1,750 crore from INR1,500 crore a year earlier, which management cites as visibility for future growth, though it gave no quarterly revenue split.

rows.label: Automotive OEM volume recovery
rows.why: Automotive grew 29% YoY to INR58.8 crore, and management expects contract volumes to recover as OEMs change programmes, but it gave no quantitative FY27 Automotive target and the OEM may keep time-shifting.

rows.label: Government receivable collection
rows.why: Majority of FY26 receivables of INR176 crore were from government on a longer cycle, and one INR4 crore gross write-off hit Q1, so further write-offs or slower collections remain a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, IoT growth and the 35%+ margin target, but evasive on quarterly margin, segment order mix, pricing and government receivable details; analysts pushed on the 43-44% margin path, the Automotive decline and the write-off accounting.

543425|2026-09.headline: MapmyIndia Q2 FY27: revenue up 15.8% YoY, EBITDA up 60%, PAT up 90%; management guides to EBITDA margin of 35%+ for FY27.
543425|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 15.8% YoY, EBITDA growth of 60% and PAT growth of 90%, with H1 revenue up 18.4%, EBITDA up 20.4% and PAT up 32%. Map-led and IoT-led both grew strongly, with Map-led at INR 76.7 crore revenue and IoT-led at INR 55.1 crore. Management attributed the government segment's sharp sequential/YoY drop to a one-off execution in the prior-year quarter, and said receivables (around 120-122 days) are a focus, mainly government collections of about INR 100 crore. Management declined to give numeric guidance for H2 beyond EBITDA margin, but said H2 should be better than H1 on the open order book.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 30 crore (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 22 crore (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 174-186 crore (analyst figures); receivable days around 120-122 (analyst reference), 133 days cited by analyst

segments.name: Map-led
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 76.7 crore with 41.6% EBITDA margin; H1 EBITDA margin of 47%.

segments.name: IoT-led
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 55.1 crore with 23.8% EBITDA margin; H1 EBITDA margin about 19.2%. Margin expansion attributed to operating leverage and group-wide IoT sales synergies.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Grew about 52% in Q2 and about 40% in H1; wins included a localised navigation solution for commercial vehicles and a 2-wheeler OEM contract renewal.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Grew about 44% in Q2; wins in last-mile delivery, quick commerce and logistics, and a large workforce-automation software stack deal. An existing quick-commerce customer scaled volumes 5x.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY against a one-off win in the prior-year quarter, but rose sequentially in Q2. New Go-Lives include oil and gas upstream digital twin and a first national disaster response win.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain consolidated EBITDA margin of 35% or more; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin is 37.2%.
Management believes H2 FY27 can be better than H1 FY27, citing growth momentum and conversion of a substantial open order book.
Management said Q3 should be good as well as Q4, with a large oil and gas IoT government subscription contract now live and its subscriptions starting to flow.
Management declined to give a specific revenue growth number; said it is 'very encouraging and quite bullish' on returning to 20%+ growth but gave no figure.
Management said the company has not been impacted by geopolitical developments so far and has no visibility of any impact.
capex_capacity: No capex amounts, capacity expansion, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Management said it is investing in technology 'in a big way for future readiness' and is embedding AI, ML and neural networks across Map-led and IoT-led platforms; no rupee capex quantum was given.
Inventory was said to have been brought down to half; supplier accounts are being settled faster and cash flows were described as strong.

Commissioning and go-live timelines discussed: a large oil and gas IoT government subscription contract has gone live and subscriptions have started to flow; oil and gas upstream digital twin and a first national disaster response win were cited as Go-Lives, with no dates or values.
demand_pricing: Strong funnel and open order book in enterprise and government, including defence; management declined to quantify the next-quarter growth.
Government: company is being selective in bids, seeking portfolio with collectability and margin, to avoid later issues.

Pricing and revenue models vary by customer: annual licence fees, delivery-based, per transaction, consumption-based, per asset/vehicle, per user per month. This drives seasonality (Enterprise peaks in Q1 and Q4; Government peaks towards Q4).
Data and API licensing grouped together as one revenue category; management said quarterly comparisons are misleading and should be viewed on a full-year basis.
IoT growth attributed to group-wide sales synergy, with automotive OEMs as a channel for IoT device sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is enterprise revenue seasonality so high, with one quarter nearly doubling versus others?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited varied revenue models (annual licences, delivery-based, per transaction, per asset, per user-month) and different contract sizes, which drive the peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be better than H1, and what will drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 should be better than H1, given three quarters of growth and conversion of the open order book; it highlighted a large oil and gas IoT subscription contract going live.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth return to 20%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no number, but said visibility is encouraging and it is bullish, with large open-order contracts going live.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days elevated at 120-122 days, and are there non-government projects with long cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-government receivables are healthy and stable; the focus is on collecting roughly INR 100 crore of government receivables sooner.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving IoT margin expansion despite higher hardware sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage on fixed costs, group-wide IoT sales synergy via automotive OEMs, inventory and cost optimisation, and growing SaaS follow-on revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the hardware and service revenue from IoT one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no one-off; device sales grow with customer count and should be viewed on an annual basis, not quarterly.

543426|2026-03.headline: Metro Brands Q4 FY26: standalone revenue up 20%, PAT up 18%, FY26 delivered within guidance (sales +15%, PAT mid-teens) despite slow start.
543426|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone growth of 20% with EBITDA up 20% and PAT up 18%, and said FY26 metrics landed in guidance after a slow start to the year. Digital commerce grew 53% and reached 12% of revenue in the quarter. The company ended the quarter with 1,032 stores after a net addition of 42, and opened its first two FILA stores since the acquisition. Management flagged input cost inflation from the Gulf crisis (around 10% on affected items), which it plans to mitigate through forward buying and pre-built inventory of about six months.

segments.name: Digital commerce (e-commerce and omnichannel)
segments.commentary: Grew 53% in Q4 and made up 12% of revenue. Management expects it to stay in a 12% to 15% share of business in the near term, with lumpiness around festive periods.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Has no stores in India currently per management; BIS impact is limited because production has moved to India.

segments.commentary: Expansion elevated in FY26; management said it is still refining the format for Tier-2 to Tier-4 towns and high streets, and that profitability and ROCE of the model are improving.

Input costs: management quantified inflation at around 10% on affected items; expects gradual impact given about six months of inventory and forward-protected orders, with no immediate price hikes planned beyond normal inflation.
Gulf crisis and geopolitical disruption are being monitored for raw materials and input costs.
capex_capacity: New DC opened in March 2026, adding 200,000 sq ft of storage capacity.
Store POS system upgrade to start in June 2026, targeted for rollout by year-end; SAP upgrade planned later in FY27.
Store rental competition has stabilised rather than reverted; management said it is not back to the earlier environment but acceleration has eased.
Store expansion guided as 'as many good ones as we can find'; company described itself as well capitalised.
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 demand improvement came from marketing initiatives, new product launches and CRM-driven acquisition of new customers, not from any single factor such as festive or wedding timing.
Management expects premium customers to be relatively insulated from inflation; Walkway's value customer is more exposed.
Management said footwear is infrequent and not a high-ticket purchase, limiting demand sensitivity to inflation.
Men's and unisex category shifts were attributed to reclassification by third-party brands; combined mix unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much is input cost inflation and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nissan Joseph put input cost inflation at around 10% on affected items, mitigated by bulk forward buying and six months of inventory; no knee-jerk price hikes, only normal inflation. Kaushal Parekh said higher inventory reflects front-loading ahead of the price rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by SSG or new stores, and what is footfall trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSG is the main driver along with new stores and annualisation; revenue per sq ft held at 4,500 sq ft; in-store footfall and new customer acquisition improved through the back half of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook for FY27 and store pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50 stores are available across FILA, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv in FY27, but BIS, rentals and timing remain uncertain; growth of around 15% is targeted long-term, with no quarter-by-quarter commitment.

qa_highlights.question: When will Foot Locker BIS issues and FILA repositioning normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not predict BIS clearance timing; FILA repositioning takes time with inventory clean-up, and management expects it to be meaningful in about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company out of the hyper-competitive rental market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not out of it, but the acceleration in rental competition has stabilised.

543426|2026-06.headline: Metro Brands Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 14% and PAT about 13%, with April-May soft and June recovering to mid-teens-plus growth.
543426|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 14% and EBITDA 9% in Q1 FY27, with PAT up 13%, per management's opening remarks. April and May were soft on the U.S.-Iran conflict overhang and a shift in wedding dates, while June rebounded to a mid-teen double-digit gain. The e-commerce SOR (3P) channel slowed to 9%, while D2C and marketplace omni each grew about 60%. Management reiterated gross margin near 55-57% (quarter at almost 60%), EBITDA around 30%, and full-year PAT of 13-15%, citing marketing, treasury income, new-store dilution and talent/tech investment as PAT margin drivers.

highest in past 5 quarters per management

segments.commentary: Women's range launched late CY2025 in about 200 MBOs, expanded to about 350 doors this spring, targeting 700 by year-end; men's range in under 100 stores. First Clarks EBOs from Q3 FY27, with a 100-150 store runway cited.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Opened 3 new EBOs and closed 1 legacy store (of 2 inherited); management said the brand is behind schedule, with acceleration expected toward end of FY27.

segments.name: MetroActiv / Walkway
segments.commentary: MetroActiv: 3 stores opened, 2 doing well and 1 underperforming, with BIS issues cited. Walkway: base of about 70 stores, over 30 opened in the quarter (about 50% growth), with mixed store performance.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Growth was weaker pre-monsoon because June 2025 had strong monsoon demand that did not repeat in June 2026; management said Crocs is performing to plan now.

Clarks EBO runway estimated at 100-150 stores; long-term sports runway of 300-500 stores across FILA EBO, Foot Locker and MetroActiv over 5-7 years.
Walkway medium-to-long-term target of ROCE of 25-30%, versus treasury yields of about 7-8%.
Management is testing a 2,000 sq ft store format and is still learning which markets can sustain it.
demand_pricing: April and May were soft from the U.S.-Iran conflict and a shift in Adhik Maas wedding dates (zero weddings in April and May per management); June rebounded to mid-teen double-digit growth.
Demand described as broad-based across price points, geographies and banners; management said it is not seeing it driven only by metros or Tier-3 cities.
Gross margin held near 60% through inventory discipline and forward buying 4-5 months ahead; normal inflationary price increases of 3-5%, with no direct oil-price impact yet.
Realisations up 6% YoY, mainly from mix (newer premium formats and Crocs), with full-year ASP growth expected at about 3-4%.
Premium 3,000+ price band at about 57% of sales (management said it is approaching 60%), with premiumisation expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why were April and May muted when peers held up, and was June materially stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited zero wedding dates in April and May and a consumer-sentiment distraction from the prolonged war. June rebounded strongly, helped by Crocs-friendly monsoon absence offset by other brands; the Crocs shortfall was timing-related.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SOR (3P) e-commerce slow, and will discounting cut growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SOR growth was lumpy from return-swap timing, plus a deliberate reduction in low price points and 3P discounts. Management expects e-com to grow well into double digits, with 20-30% a year as the healthy range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year margin outlook given wage hikes and input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided gross margin 55-57% (currently above), EBITDA around 30%, and PAT 13-15%. Front-end wages are above state minimums, but wage rules will be absorbed as they change.

qa_highlights.question: Why not guide to 20% growth when demand is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers measured guidance to avoid inventory overhang and brand-share loss; it guides to about 15% and says it aims higher. It cited three quarters of steady double-digit growth and rising conversion and new-customer counts.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the PAT margin decline and when does PAT growth return to mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from top-of-funnel marketing, plus lower treasury income versus last year's teens yields, new-store dilution (about 40 Walkway stores among 140 openings), and talent/tech investment. Management expects a return to 15%-plus PAT growth as these normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is BIS relief helping FILA launch timelines, and how is FILA inventory being discounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recent QC order allowing imports has no significant impact; ASEAN BIS renewals are the larger constraint. Heavy FILA discounting reflects legacy acquired inventory and 3-4 month sports life cycles with 9-month buying lead times.

543426|2026-09.headline: Metro Brands Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.2% to INR730 crore, with EBITDA up 15.9% to INR198 crore, while festive demand shifted into Q3.
543426|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.2% to INR730 crore and EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR198 crore, with margin at 27.1% versus 26.2% a year ago. PAT grew about 11% to INR77 crore with margin flat at 10.6%, as higher rentals, staff costs and marketing, plus lower treasury income, offset a gross margin gain. Management attributed much of the revenue slowdown to festive demand moving from September into October, and said net store additions were slowed to 12 in Q2 with selective openings. Newer brands (Clarks, Foot Locker, MetroActiv, FILA) remain constrained by BIS-related supply issues and are being scaled cautiously.

financial_highlights.change: lower vs prior strong treasury year; FY26 full-year other income about INR100 crore

segments.name: Metro / Mochi / Walkway / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands contributed about 70% of store product sales at Metro, Mochi and Walkway in H1. Walkway: over 35 stores opened in last 12-14 months on a base of about 60-70; roughly 30% performed well, 30% average, 30% poor.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Crocs is under 20% of total business across stores, Metro and Mochi multi-brand. Management said Crocs grew decently and Durga Puja/Shraddh timing, not Crocs, drove the quarter.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Women's range in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and limited men's range in more than 100; full exclusive store range expected in Q3 FY27, exclusive EBO launch targeted in H2 FY27. Clarks had about 80 EBOs in India at one point.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Local footwear manufacturing started in India in response to BIS concerns; repositioning expected over 12-18 months, with store expansion picking up from FY28.

segments.name: Foot Locker / MetroActiv
segments.commentary: BIS implementation challenges for selected external brands constrained supply and store expansion; early signs of normalisation, with openings calibrated to product availability.

Frontline staff costs expected to rise 0.5%-1% from the remuneration revision, offset if top-line improves.
Marketing spend expected at around 4% of revenue for the full year and next year.

Inventory-heavy: front-loaded stock for raw material inflation, FitFlop BIS renewals and Clarks/Foot Locker door fills.

Raw material inflation about 10%-15%; price hikes on raw material pass-through about 2%-4%, possibly 2%-5%, varying by article.
Management said October festive trends look good, with Durga Puja performing well and other markets indicating a good festive season.
Management sees landlord pressure from rental inflation: limited supply of new retail space, one-and-done negotiations; cited rising rents and new players competing for space.

qa_highlights.question: Why were store closures and the H1 store addition pace so low versus the 100-110 average adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Closures are not format-specific and are reviewed on a two-year profitability test; FY closures expected at 2-3%. Management said rentals are high and supply is tight, and it is not fixated on a number, having opened over 100 doors last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin gain is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower end-of-season discounts and online sales discounts were the main drivers, with some markup improvement and lower e-commerce mix. Management said discount benefits will not sustain in Q3; mix shift towards Walkway, Foot Locker and MetroActiv may pull gross margin lower over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT margin pressure driven by rentals, staff costs and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed rental and minimum-wage-led staff cost pressure, talent and marketing investment, and lower treasury income (H1 other income about INR54 crore). Benefits from Clarks EBOs and marketing are expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the real underlying sales growth excluding festive and Crocs timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to the Durga Puja and Shraddh shift, estimated at 250-350 bps, which takes growth back to about 15%. Crocs is under 20% of the business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory normalisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was front-loaded for raw material inflation, FitFlop BIS renewals and new door fills. Partial improvement by March 2027, return to about 80 working capital days around mid-to-end FY28, and ideal inventory about 7 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marketing spend and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing spend about 4% of revenue in H1 versus 3.25%-3.4% a year ago, expected to stay around 4%. Capex guidance is INR80-100 crore for FY27 and FY28, including remodels.

543427|2026-06.headline: MedPlus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR18,796 million (pharmacy +21.8% YoY) but operating EBITDA margin fell to 3.5%, and the board-approved capex was put on hold.
543427|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR18,796 million and consolidated operating EBITDA INR651 million (3.5%), with pharmacy EBITDA at INR588 million (3.2%). Margin pressure came from lower private label mix (about 100 bps), a smaller inventory provision release versus Q4 (about 70 bps), and absent year-end supplier discounts (about 40 bps), plus higher employee costs after minimum wage hikes in Karnataka and Telangana. Management put the board-approved capex (food park/oil extraction unit and a wellness services facility, about INR40 crore for the food park) on hold after investor pushback, and said the annual operating plan was not changed for now. Net store additions were 146 (131 franchisee), against the 800 net-addition FY27 target.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the approved capex put on hold, and is more large capex expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feedback from the market and investors led to a pause on all capex (food park and wellness); core business capex continues and will not stop, and the market reaction was the reason for the hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why did private label share fall and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employees over-pushed private label, causing some customer friction; the company will add influencer-led marketing and better selling, targeting about 0.3%-0.5% quarterly share growth from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 800-store guidance and franchisee mix stay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 800 net stores at net level are maintained; 131 of 146 net additions in Q1 were franchisee stores, and the internal split was broadly 50:50.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum wage increases from 1 June (about 60% in Karnataka and 25%+ in Telangana vs typical ~4%) only had one month in Q1; the retention bonus plan was stopped for new joiners from 1 March, and incentives are being restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA fall YoY despite flat private label sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix and higher costs, predominantly employee cost, drove the EBITDA decline; gross margin fell on mix.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the ~200 bps sequential gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from lower private label mix, about 70 bps from a smaller inventory provision release versus Q4, and about 40 bps from year-end supplier discounts not repeated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the promoter pledged debt outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to INR1,150 crore including interest; repayment decisions rest with the family office, not the listed company.

543434|2026-09.headline: Supriya Lifescience Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell 37.5% to INR45 crore (22% margin) on LATAM regulatory shock, Ambernath costs; FY27 margin guidance cut to 23-25%.
543434|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.2% YoY to INR206 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR45 crore from INR73 crore and PAT to INR29 crore from INR50 crore. Management attributed the margin drop to LATAM regulatory changes that made high-margin products controlled substances, Ambernath ramp-up costs (about INR60 crore for FY27 with little revenue), and higher raw material and solvent prices. EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 23-25% from the earlier range, while the INR1,000 crore revenue target for FY27 was reaffirmed. The Ambernath EU audit was scheduled for the week of the call, and a large CDMO contract was said to be close to signing.

segments.name: Exports (geography)
segments.commentary: Exports were 80% of Q2 FY27 revenue: Europe 43%, Asia 36%, LATAM 12%. LATAM share was up to 21% in an earlier period before falling back to 12%.

segments.name: Ambernath facility
segments.commentary: Ramping up; about INR60 crore of expenses expected in FY27 with near-zero revenue this year. Designed for INR450-500 crore revenue once EU approval is in place; breakeven seen at INR160-200 crore revenue.

segments.name: New launches
segments.commentary: Two anesthetic liquid inhalation products launched in Q2 FY27 from Ambernath; two ADHD products in pipeline. Traction is mainly in semi-regulated markets with lower ASPs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance revised down to 23-25%; management said it expects about 25% for the full year, with upside possible if raw material and solvent costs ease.

FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,000 crore reaffirmed; management said it is very confident, citing an order book and about INR265 crore of inventory. H1 revenue was INR396 crore, implying about INR600 crore needed in H2.
Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 20%+ per year for the next 3-4 years, driven by baseline business, new launches and CDMO deals.
Margin normalisation is expected in FY28 once Ambernath is approved and LATAM sales resume. Management declined to give FY28 margin guidance and will revisit after the EU approval.
Management said LATAM import permits could take 4-5 months, so the margin impact is expected to persist for the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex of INR18.8 crore and H1 FY27 capex of INR35.4 crore, mainly for Ambernath plus maintenance, the Ribo block and formulation plant.

Ambernath EU audit scheduled for the week of the call (November 2026); approval is a precondition for meaningful revenue. Product registrations could take about 1-1.5 years after approval to reach meaningful scale.
Module E API capacity can take the liquid anesthetic product to about 1,100 tonnes, with customer scale-up expected over 4-5 years.
Contrast media product said to be close to launch, with commercial-scale plant scale-up expected by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Margin decomposition by management: typical margin 34-35%, current about 22%. The 11-12 point gap is roughly 6 points from Ambernath costs, 3 points from LATAM regulatory and mix change, and 3 points from raw material and solvent inflation.

LATAM markets (Colombia, Peru, Uruguay and others) reclassified high-margin products as controlled substances with immediate effect and no stock window. Customers now need import authorisations, which management expects to take 4-5 months.

Raw material and solvent prices kept rising after Q1 because of geopolitical tensions. Contracts with larger customers were priced at older rates, so the price pass-through is expected to flow through over the next 2 quarters.
Statins intermediate: mid-level monthly volumes; the company is the only fully integrated Indian producer and competes with China on price.
ADHD API market estimated at USD100-150 million; a long-term supply contract with a US company is at an early stage. Regulatory approvals are expected in 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is hit by the LATAM regulatory change, and is the impact permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it transient, lasting a few quarters, while import authorisations are pending. It cited 4-5 months for customers to obtain permits; the change took effect immediately with no stock-up window across 3-4 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target given H1 of INR396 crore and about INR265 crore of inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident, citing the order book, and expects the new products in semi-regulated markets plus the anesthetic CMO deal to offset LATAM.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin decline split, and why is it larger than peers' given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Split: about 6 points Ambernath, 3 points LATAM and mix, 3 points raw material and solvent. The CFO attributed the solvent and raw material pressure to crude-derived basic chemicals and drum versus ISO tank pricing, plus customer pushback on price increases.

qa_highlights.question: When does Ambernath break even and what revenue is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the breakeven sweet spot is INR160-200 crore of revenue, versus about INR60 crore of expenses now. Meaningful scale is expected 1-1.5 years after EU approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide FY28 margin, saying it will come back after EU approval and the next couple of quarters. It said normalisation is expected once Ambernath and LATAM contribute.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a communication gap, given the margin guidance was held in the prior call?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the feedback and said the LATAM regulatory change happened after the Q1 call, so the lost POs could not have been pre-empted.

Management has not guided FY28 margin, and investors questioned communication after the Q1 call; further clarity is expected in the next couple of quarters.

543441|2026-03.headline: CMS Info Systems FY26 revenue rose 3% to Rs.2,487 Crores; FY27 services guidance held at Rs.2,700-2,800 Crores despite a weak year.
543441|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a reset year: SBI RFP delay, consumption weakness, offsite ATM market contraction and wage settlements together cost about Rs.150 Crores of services revenue, per management. Q4 services revenue recovered 6% QoQ to Rs.609 Crores and Q4 EBITDA margin improved about 280 bps, with EBIT margin at 19% versus 15% in Q3. Management retained its FY27 revenue goal and a 25% EBITDA margin aspiration, while declaring a Rs.168 Crores buyback at Rs.340 per share and completing two acquisitions (Securens closed, FSS signed and expected to close end-Q1 FY27). Management walked away from a Rs.700 Crores transaction-fee ATM contract, citing return thresholds.

vs ~Rs.100 Crores in FY24 and FY25

segments.commentary: ATM management solutions 58%, retail and currency logistics 26%, technology and payment solutions 16% of FY26 revenue; FY22 split was 63:37 across the first two with tech at 7%. Management said segment-level profit split is no longer meaningful.

segments.name: Technology and payment solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs.370 Crores (16% mix), up from 12% last year; Hawkai revenue about Rs.200 Crores, doubled in two years. Securens integration takes live monitored sites to 50,000 against a targeted Rs.8,000 Crores TAM.

segments.name: Managed services
segments.commentary: Moved from number five to number three in MSP ranking. Customer mix shift: top-customer share fell from 58.42% in FY25 to 48.52% in FY26. Mid-size MSP receivable stress addressed via FSS deal, a secured loan and escrow arrangement.

FY27 total revenue goal Rs.2,800-2,900 Crores (13-17% growth).

Q1 FY27 revenue run-rate target about Rs.650 Crores (implies about Rs.2,600 Crores annualised); HDFC contract expected to add Rs.50-75 Crores in FY27.

FSS acquisition expected to close at end of Q1 FY27; management would not yet say whether it is EPS-accretive in year one.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex Rs.350 Crores, up from about Rs.100 Crores in FY24 and FY25, with depreciation rising from Rs.54 Crores to Rs.59 Crores QoQ.
Route network cut by about 10% (Sept 2025 to Mar 2026) using ML-based optimisation.
Gig delivery model investment of about Rs.15 Crores to convert part of fixed cost network to variable and expand into tier 3 and 4 retail markets.
Securens acquisition closed and integrated; expected to be accretive in FY27. FSS deal signed in Q4 FY26, closing targeted end-Q1 FY27.
Algo MVS software going live in FY27 to enable value-added services on recyclers; ICICI recycler mix moved from 20% to 80% in two years.
demand_pricing: Order book: FY26 order wins about Rs.2,000 Crores, of which about 75% executed; Rs.400-500 Crores remains to be executed. All three large wins (SBI, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank) are fixed-fee, none transaction-linked.
Walked away from a Rs.700 Crores ATM contract at Rs.19 per transaction (about Rs.75 Crores annual revenue initially); management said the transaction fee model is effectively dead in ATM.
Market clearing transaction price for one recent bank RFP was close to Rs.25, versus interchange of Rs.19.

Pipeline of 6,000-7,000 ATM units across bank RFP stages in FY27, mostly product purchase plus services or fixed-price outsourcing; management expects banks to return to refresh cycles in FY27 but will update on pipeline at Q1 or Q2.

Pricing: CPI/WPI-linked contracts being expanded; annual price resets applied; off-cycle price increases sought for state minimum wage and fuel shocks. A peer price hike was reported the day before the call.
Q4 FY26 consumption and currency supply dipped in March and April; management flagged Rs.50-70 Crores revenue risk if weakness persists for 10-12 months.
Lower-yield retail and tail customers were exited; management may drop Rs.25-40 Crores of revenue in H2 to protect margin.

qa_highlights.question: What could cause FY27 revenue guidance to be missed, and how big is the gap to Rs.2,800 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.633 Crores Q4 annualised gives about Rs.2,500 Crores; HDFC adds Rs.50-75 Crores, reaching about Rs.2,600 Crores. The bottom end still needs about Rs.200 Crores from pipeline and new orders. Main downside is a consumption dip of Rs.50-70 Crores; no single large contract is assumed like SBI last year.

qa_highlights.question: Did a competitor take the Rs.700 Crores transaction-fee contract the company declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a competitor took it; management declined to name them. Management said Rs.19 per transaction is an attractive price for the bidder, but the company's return thresholds (25% margin, ROCE) were not met over the seven-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: How is ATM cash split for FY26 across ATM cash, retail cash and CIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give the split. It only said the 60:40 cash to MSP mix moved to 55:45, and that reporting now follows three platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Why would banks add offsite ATMs, and how do onsite and offsite economics differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks now treat ATMs as an alternate servicing channel; recyclers handle cash acceptance, video KYC and card issuance and replace branch transactions. Banks are increasingly funding capex themselves, which changes the economics for deployers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp for the SBI and ICICI contracts, and how should HDFC revenue be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: SBI runs 7-10 years, ICICI longer, HDFC about five years. Management suggested dividing total contract value evenly across years for simplicity, noting ramp, price changes and churn will vary.

qa_highlights.question: How do the FSS and Hawkai/Algo cross-sell and FSS transaction exposure look?
qa_highlights.answer: FSS contracts being transferred are the managed services ones; some carry transaction exposure, which management views as manageable given 2-4 years of history. Algo would be a new opportunity; Hawkai penetration among mid-size banks is low, and combined scale gives cost synergies. FSS is described as the highest-quality MSP business by management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from stressed MSP customers (28% of revenue) and the Rs.58 Crores of loans and advances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management converted unsecured receivables to secured loans for one MSP, took an escrow route on another and solved a third. Provision already taken in Q2 FY26. Management said there is no further risk expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on depreciation rising and on EBIT margin, and will the promoter tender in the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the depreciation rise reflects longer-term tech and capex investments, and that synergies from Securens and FSS may take a few quarters, while depreciation starts on day one. ROCE was about 25% in prior years. Rajiv Kaul said he will not participate in the buyback.

Fuel and wage inflation: fuel and vehicle costs about 6% of revenue; Q1 is seasonally lower-margin; the 25% EBITDA aspiration is not yet confirmed.
Revenue gap: about Rs.200 Crores still needed beyond the Rs.2,600 Crores run-rate to reach the bottom of the FY27 services goal.
FSS integration and closing at end-Q1 FY27; quality and network stabilisation take priority over pricing arbitrage.
MSP counterparty credit risk: mid-size MSPs under liquidity stress; recovery depends on escrow and secured structures.
Brinks-NCR merger could shift some MSP base over time; management sees it as a long-dated risk.
Depreciation step-up (Rs.54 Crores to Rs.59 Crores QoQ) ahead of revenue from new capex.

543441|2026-06.headline: CMS Info Systems Q1 FY27 services revenue hit a record INR625 crores (+9.3% YoY) despite a INR25 crore currency-supply hit; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to about 27%.

EBITDA rose 8.9% YoY to INR173 crores with margin up 170 bps QoQ to 27.2%, while EBIT fell to INR32 crores (10.3% margin) on higher depreciation from HAWKAI/ALGO capex and the FSS acquisition. Management trimmed FY27 services revenue guidance to INR2,650-2,750 crores (from INR2,700-2,800 crores) and raised the EBITDA margin guide to about 27% (from 25-26%). Currency fulfilment has since recovered to roughly 80-85% of indents, and management expects normalisation by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cash crunch transient or structural, and could banks have deliberately under-supplied low-potential ATMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is past (supply went from about 70% to 80-85%) and rejected the idea that banks chose which ATMs to starve, describing geographic imbalances instead. Demand is not the problem; the end-Q2 result will show it.

qa_highlights.question: What changes are being made to forecasting after repeated shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Kaul said FY22-24 met or exceeded forecasts while FY25-26 fell short, and the team will keep setting realistic stretch targets. He called the criticism fair and said Q1 shortfall was flagged early.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from FSS in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR20 crores of accrual, with contracts still being novated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of possible UPI MDR and polymer notes?

qa_highlights.question: How was the INR4,00 crore TAM for HAWKAI derived?

543517|2026-09.headline: Hariom Pipe Q2 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR 554 crore and PAT to INR 29 crore, with EBITDA per tonne at INR 8,140.

Management attributed the recovery to the Perundurai unit restarting on July 13 after a roughly 110-day closure in Q1. H1 revenue was INR 983 crore (up 23%), EBITDA INR 118 crore (up 17%) and PAT INR 46 crore (up 35%). Management guided to 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and FY28 and a 25% volume growth base case, while the solar portfolio and Andhra Pradesh steel MOU remain early-stage.

segments.commentary: 15 MWac is operational across three locations after 5 MWac in July and two 5 MWac projects in October (the latter after the half-year end). Portfolio is 60 MW across 13 locations in Maharashtra; target is 52 MW across 11 locations by January 2027.

segments.commentary: Completed documentation and obtained GST registration in H1; fuller operations are planned for the current quarter. No revenue contribution was disclosed.

Solar: 52 MW across 11 locations targeted by January 2027. Management expects roughly INR 28-30 crore revenue and INR 3-4 crore net surplus after debt, depreciation and interest once 52 MW is operational, over 4-5 years.

543523|2026-03.headline: Campus Activewear Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, EBITDA margin 19.2%, FY26 PAT margin 8.4%.
543523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, led by online (around 19%) and distribution (around 5.5%). EBITDA was INR 88.5 crore at a 19.2% margin (up 50 bps) and PAT was INR 44.1 crore at a 9.6% margin (up 100 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 11.4% to INR 1,774 crore, EBITDA margin rose 145 bps to 17.5%, and PAT margin rose 80 bps to 8.4%. Management said the mid-year raw material and minimum wage inflation was passed on via MRP hikes taken in early April, and that demand held up in April.

segments.name: Online (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; management said all online business is pure marketplace except Flipkart, with Amazon, Snapdeal and brand.com growing faster. Online salience rose in Q4, though GT charges dilute gross margin and billing changed from 16 June to net of freight (INR 82 billed against INR 100 earlier).

segments.name: Distribution (general trade and franchise)
segments.commentary: Distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26. Management said the annual distribution meet produced strong four-month forward orders, with AOP alignments with partners closed at over 100% of the target till September.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Sneaker portfolio grew about 100% YoY in FY26 and more than 50% in quarterly terms; the Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units are producing about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27. Management did not disclose sneaker revenue or volume share.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration band of 17% to 19% for FY27 but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
Management said pricing taken in early April covers the inflation impact and that raw material prices have peaked and are starting to ease; no further price hikes expected.
Plan to open 60 to 80 new EBO stores in FY27 (about 40% COCO and 60% FOFO), after closing 9 to 10 and opening 13 to 14 stores in FY26; store count stood at about 300.
Marketing budget for FY27 set to be aggressive, focused on brand building rather than performance marketing.

Capex in FY27 expected to return to normal maintenance, mold, EBO and IT levels; Pant Nagar expansion including assembly lines is planned over the next three years, after first optimising the upper facility.
Full BIS compliance expected by 31 July 2026, with very little BIS stock remaining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share of shoes priced below INR 1,000 rise versus Q4 FY25, and is the pricing MRP or realised price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the figures are realised ASP; the shift reflects MRP corrections after GST on footwear was revised from 12% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What size of price hike was taken and will it suffice against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give the percentage, said hikes were taken proportionately across the range and are enough to cover raw material and minimum wage inflation; peak RM seen, prices to ease in about a quarter, with no price reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses (ex-ad spend) rise only about 5% despite online growth of 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited dynamic online commission negotiations and event-based waivers, plus flat store count meaning no new EBO costs; other costs grew in the 5-6% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lease cash outflow rise sharply, nearly 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Pant Nagar land is a 71-year state government lease treated as lease liability payment; normalised FY26 rent excluding INR 65.4 crore is the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise 5-6 days in FY26 and where will they go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FG inventory was at a very minimal level last year and was rebuilt to the right level by March 2026, which will be maintained going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for sneaker growth, and what is the path to 2 lakh pairs a month?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said capacity is not a constraint now; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after two phases and HRD2 can reach 2 lakh (already running), targeting 8-9 lakh pairs per month in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins reach the 17-19% band or slip to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; CEO said the company will endeavour to stay within the 17-19% range guided earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBO expansion plan and capex for stores and facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 60-70 or about 80 new stores are planned after closing 9-10 and opening 13-14 in FY26; CFO said FY27 capex reverts to normal maintenance, mould, EBO and IT levels, with Pant Nagar expansion over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What were the distribution meet outcomes and demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said order bookings were strong on a four-month forward basis, numbers not shared; COO said AOP alignments with distributors were closed at over 100% till September.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the low Q4 ASP growth of 1.5% when D2C/online realisations should be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to online billing change from 16 June (INR 82 billed against INR 100) with freight of INR 18 billed directly by portals, which is not in last year's Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the BIS compliance position?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the company is hardly left with any non-BIS stock and expects full compliance by 31 July 2026; the reported BIS rethink is only chatter with no official communication.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company gaining share in competitive affordable athleisure, and what are its moats?
qa_highlights.answer: COO cited an integrated supply chain, strongest distribution network, R&D, 20-year brand loyalty; CEO estimated replicating the supply chain would need about INR 2,000 crore.
