543523|2026-06.headline: Campus Activewear Q1 FY27: revenue up 12.2%, volume up 11.7%, EBITDA margin 15.9%, PAT up 17.7%, with ASP drag from temporary accounting and mix effects.
543523|2026-06.overview: Campus reported 12.2% revenue growth, 11.7% volume growth, 15.9% EBITDA margin and 17.7% PAT growth in Q1 FY27. Reported ASP growth was held back by a Walmart (Flipkart/Myntra) GT-charge netting change (about 2.5%) and a school-shoe mix shift (about 2%), both described as Q1-only effects. An 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 gave underlying core-category ASP growth of about 5%. Management guided to mid-double-digit FY27 growth, split between ASP and volume, and reiterated a 17-19% EBITDA margin aspiration. Record Q1 production and record distributor orders were highlighted ahead of the festive season.

financial_highlights.change: Management says about 4.5-5% was temporary (GT netting ~2%, franchise SOR transition ~2.5%); normalised growth about 4%-plus ex these factors per management's framing
Analyst-cited figure; management did not dispute it

financial_highlights.metric: ASP impact from Walmart GT netting
Underlying ASP increase, core Stuck-On category
Additional depreciation from Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants
Minimum wage cost in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: about Rs. 5 crore for the quarter

financial_highlights.change: About 10% annualisation and increments, about 5% new hiring

segments.name: Stuck-On (core)
segments.commentary: Underlying ASP up about 5% after ~8% MRP increase; school shoes moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which management says has higher ASP and margin than DIP.

segments.name: School shoes
segments.commentary: Revenue up nearly 50% YoY; about 40% of Q1 volume growth came from this category, expected to normalise from Q2.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Q1 contributed about 12-13% of volume; management targets about 30% growth for the category in FY27, down from near-100% historically.

segments.name: Open footwear (sandals/slippers)
segments.commentary: Slower growth, about 4-5% below rest of category, attributed to CNG/LPG supply constraints affecting hot-and-cold machines during the war-related period.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO/SOR)
segments.commentary: Management cited about 25% de-growth in franchise revenue in Q1 from the outright-to-SOR model transition across 158 stores (about 2.5% revenue impact); 18 EBOs opened in Q1, the highest in 6-8 quarters.

segments.name: Marketplace and brand.com
segments.commentary: Marketplace operations up mid-double digits; brand.com up over 100% YoY; company-owned stores SSG about 20%.

segments.name: General trade Gujarat
segments.commentary: GT grew at least 20-25% faster than rest of country over the period; Maharashtra now second-largest GT state after UP.

segments.name: Elan by Campus
segments.commentary: Neo-casual launch about 60 days old, priced Rs. 1,899-2,599, selling in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com; next set planned for festive season.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: mid-double-digit overall revenue growth, split between ASP and volume; management said volume is expected to be high single digit and ASP growth of at least 6-7% from Q2 onwards.
Management is '100% confident' of delivering the 17-19% EBITDA margin band for FY27.
Store additions target: about 90-100 stores by end FY27 (guidance range 80-120).
Employee cost as % of sales expected to be proportionate to FY26; no further incremental wage cost expected beyond what is already baked in.
Festive timing: Diwali in November 2026; BBD shifts to October from September, so some marketplace revenue may move from Q2 to Q3.
Management does not plan further MRP increases; expects raw material cost relief to flow into P&L as volatility subsides.
capex_capacity: Record Q1 production, with July 2026 the highest-ever production month, to build festive inventory.
Installed annual capacity cited at about 31 million pairs, down from 36 million two years ago, due to shutdown of about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity.
New manufacturing facilities at Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar commissioned and ramping up; sneakers production also from Haridwar and Pantnagar.
Franchise EBO ROI cited at 18-30% depending on store economics; franchisees pay deposit on inventory, company controls inventory, discounting and replenishment.
Franchise master partners to rise from about 8-9 to about 16; about 8 new partners added this year.
demand_pricing: 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 across key categories; management says volumes grew despite it and resistance has been limited. No further hikes planned.
Management said some demand tapering was seen in the last quarter, citing geopolitical factors and floods in Maharashtra and Gujarat, but its demand reading remains positive.
Record orders at the distributor meet held in May 2026, giving visibility on festive demand.
Management sees some constraints at smaller organised and unorganised competitors due to working-capital stress, though impact on festive supply is unclear.

Price-point mix: management said Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core shoe segment; analyst pointed to about 7% two-year CAGR decline in sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue, which management attributed to the 8% price hike shifting products above Rs. 1,500 and reporting changes.

qa_highlights.question: Vidisha Seth (Ambit): Is the 8% MRP hike, above industry levels, risking volume or share given elasticity in economy key products, and will there be another hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8% is a fair hike, accepted with limited resistance, and volumes grew despite it; RM inflation has been fully absorbed and no further MRP hikes will be taken. Raw-material relief is expected to flow back into P&L as markets stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash (Motilal Oswal): Why did sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline about 7% on a two-year CAGR basis, and is the company exiting price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exiting price points and Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core; the decline reflects products moving above Rs. 1,500 after the 8% hike, a change in reporting, and faster closed-shoe growth versus open footwear. Gaps at economy price points are being filled over the next couple of months before the season.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash: Why did installed capacity fall from 36 million to 31 million pairs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity were shut as uneconomic; school shoes were moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which has higher ASP and margin. Stuck-On capacity is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta (Kotak): How much did school shoes contribute to volume growth, and is the margin 17-19% band still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: School shoes contributed about 40% of Q1 volume growth and will normalise from Q2. Management targets FY27 mid-double-digit growth split between ASP (at least 6-7% from Q2) and volume, and said it is 100% confident of the 17-19% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta: What drove the faster growth in other expenses excluding A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gupta said about Rs. 5 crore was minimum-wage cost, about Rs. 2.5 crore was advertising and marketing (distributor meet and logo launch), and about Rs. 2.5 crore was depreciation/indirect cost from the new Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (Emkay): Why is EBITDA growth 11% when revenue growth is about 15-16% ex-accounting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Walmart GT netting is an accounting change with no absolute EBITDA impact. Employee cost rose about 15% (10% annualisation and increments, 5% new hiring) plus higher SG&A, which drove the gap. FY27 employee cost as % of sales is expected to be in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Shraddha Kapadia (SMFS): Can volume growth stay double-digit for FY27, and what is the Elan by Campus traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not promise double-digit volume but said volume will be high single digit, with ASP and volume together delivering mid-double-digit revenue growth. Elan, about 60 days old at Rs. 1,899-2,599, sells in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com, with a second set planned for festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Prerna Jhunjhunwala (Elara): What is the store opening plan, and how do franchise economics work under the SOR model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 90-100 openings in FY27 (range 80-120), with master franchise partners rising from about 8-9 to about 16. Under SOR, the company controls inventory and discounting, franchisees pay an inventory deposit and bear rent, and EBO ROI is about 18-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Ajay Nandavar (individual investor): Why is open footwear growing slower, and how does Gujarat franchise growth coexist with trade growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandals use hot-and-cold machines dependent on CNG/LPG, which were constrained during the war period, so growth is about 4-5% below the rest of the category. Management said franchise stores have not cannibalised GT, which grew at least 20-25% faster than the rest of the country in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (follow-up): Is the 8% hike in line with industry, and what signs show consumer acceptance and lower competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers took similar or slightly lower hikes; the May distributor meet recorded record orders after the hike. Management cited marketplace growth in the mid-double digits, company-owned store SSG of about 20% and brand.com growth above 100%, and said some smaller and unorganised players faced production constraints due to working-capital stress.

risks_watch: Sustainability of ASP recovery to 6-7% from Q2: the 2.5% Walmart GT netting and 2% school-shoe mix effects must reverse as stated, and the 8% hike must hold without volume loss.
Volume normalisation after school shoes (about 40% of Q1 volume growth) taper, against a high-single-digit FY27 volume target.
EBITDA growth (11%) lagging revenue growth; the 17-19% margin band depends on employee cost (about 15% growth) and SG&A staying in line with FY26 and on raw-material relief.
Demand tapering noted in the last quarter (geopolitics, Maharashtra and Gujarat floods); record festive inventory built in Q1 and July raises inventory-risk exposure if festive demand disappoints.
Franchise transition: about 25% franchise de-growth in Q1 across 158 stores; the SOR model's accounting and store-opening pace (90-100 target) need to be tracked.
Sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue two-year CAGR decline of about 7%; management says economy price-point gaps will be filled before the season.
Elan by Campus and sneaker growth (about 30% target) are early-stage; the Diwali and Big Billion Day shift (October) may move some marketplace revenue from Q2 to Q3.
key_quotes: So, we are, yes, we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right?
Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.
RM inflation has been fully absorbed.
So, it is just a recalibration of the DIP.

543523|2026-09.headline: Campus Activewear Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.9% YoY to Rs 452 crore on 10.2% volume growth, while EBITDA margin fell to 13.5%; FY27 17% EBITDA margin guided.

EBITDA rose 12.5% to Rs 62 crore but margin slipped about 50 bps to 13.5%, with gross margin at 51.4% versus 53.9% a year earlier due to material inflation. PAT grew 21.3% to Rs 24 crore (5.3% margin). Management expects a sharp H2 margin recovery and reiterated a full-year FY27 EBITDA margin of 17% and mid-teens revenue growth.

543526|2026-03.headline: LIC FY26 net VNB rose 41.63% to ₹14,179 crore, with VNB margin up 360 bps to 21.2% on non-par mix and economic assumptions.
543526|2026-03.overview: LIC reported record FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 crore (up 19.25% YoY) and net VNB of ₹14,179 crore (up 41.63%), with margin at 21.2% versus 17.6%. Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% from 27.69% a year earlier, and the solvency ratio improved to 2.35 from 2.11. Embedded value grew only 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 crore because of ₹1.00 lakh crore-plus of equity and debt MTM declines in the year. Management flagged upcoming risk-based capital (RBC) rules as the reason it is cautious on dividend payout, even after raising the final dividend to ₹20 per share pre-bonus.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹43,335 crore; non-par APE rose 43.78% to ₹15,214 crore, 35.11% of individual APE. Individual market share fell to 36.6% from 37.46%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group premium ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%); group APE ₹23,626 crore. Group market share 70.11% vs 71.19%. Group contributed about 19% of VNB per the Appointed Actuary's breakdown.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Share of individual NBP 7.51% vs 5.59%. Policy count fell sharply, which management attributed to a microfinance corporate agency issue.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sourced 91.75% of new business premium and 98.42% of policies. Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851.

guidance_outlook: No formal numeric guidance. Management expects VNB margin to keep improving, driven by higher ticket size and better persistency, but said further expansion will be gradual and slower from here.
Management said it is not looking for major changes in the business mix from here and aims to consolidate, with VNB growth coming from either margin or volume.
Management said maturity outgo will stay high through January 2027 from 25-year-old Jeevan Shree-type assured-benefit policies.
Dividend payout policy will be finalised only after RBC outcomes are clear; management expects the increased payout to be sustained.

Upcoming Ind AS/IFRS transition and its effect on VIF-to-CSM translation, which is still being worked on.
Heavy maturity outgo through January 2027 from high sum assured legacy policies.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the non-par individual savings growth in Q4, and how much of that momentum continues into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Uthup Joseph said savings bucket grew about 48.40%, led by Jeevan Utsav on ticket size; Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium. No FY27 momentum figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin bridge from 17.6% to 21.2%, and what were the operating assumption and EV walk items?
qa_highlights.answer: A.K. Srivastava: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%. EV walk: unwind ₹74,748 crore, operating assumption changes -₹1,663 crore, operating experience variance +₹92,639 crore, equity MTM -₹53,698 crore, debt MTM -₹46,853 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the operating variance positive for several years, and what is the persistency variance breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency variance +₹3,509 crore, largely from participating and group business; par 13th-month persistency improved (+₹2,463 crore). Group persistency assumption was strengthened. Expense variance positive net of GST; mortality roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the solvency-driven dividend payout cautious even with solvency at 2.35, and how should the payout ratio be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Pant said the company wants clarity on RBC because equity exposure is high, and it does not want to create expectations it cannot sustain; growth also consumes capital. Doraiswamy said the payout will depend on regulation, with the increased payout (₹20 per share pre-bonus) expected to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par IRRs or offering rates be revised in FY27, and why did bancassurance policy count fall about 36%?

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

rows.label: New capex announcement

543526|2026-06.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.

543526|2026-09.headline: LIC H1 FY27 net VNB rose 33.95% to ₹6,846 crore, with VNB margin up 470 bps to 22.3%, while total APE grew only 5.72% to ₹30,696 crore.
543526|2026-09.overview: LIC reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) with profit after tax up 21.52% to ₹25,568 crore and net VNB up 33.95% to ₹6,846 crore. Margin expansion came from business mix (non-par savings and term) and assumption changes, partly offset by a 1.4% expense realignment. Individual APE was flat-to-weak because ULIP sales fell sharply, reflecting a deliberate push for higher ticket sizes, while individual NBP grew 14.86%. Solvency improved to 2.35x from 2.13x, but IEV fell 1.95% year on year because of MTM losses on debt.

financial_highlights.change: +470 bps YoY (from 17.6%); Q1 FY27 22.9%, so down ~60 bps QoQ
vs 59.41% a year ago; individual 37.51% (vs 37.21%), group 70.45% (vs 72.74%)

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹17,224 crore (56.11% of APE); ULIP APE fell more than 40% as agents shifted to higher-ticket monthly eNACH policies. Non-PAR share of individual APE rose to 34.02% from 36.31%, and PAR was 65.98%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group APE ₹13,472 crore (43.89% of APE), up about 14% per management; group new business premium up 20.63%. Market share fell to 70.45% from 72.74%, which management attributed to the cyclical term-group segment.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: New business premium ₹2,458 crore, up 21.44% YoY; bank channel ₹1,336 crore (+5.56%) and alternate channel ₹1,122 crore (+48.01%). Share of individual NBP rose to 7.53% from 7.12%.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sold 98.4% of policies and 91.81% of new business premium; agent count fell to 14,52,461 from 14,85,325 and agent market share fell to 43.70% from 45.86%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects individual APE growth to converge with individual rated NBP (WRP) growth by year-end, helped by H2 ULIP ticket-size recovery and newly launched health, cancer cover, deferred annuity and term products.
Management says it has a 'very positive outlook on margin for 2027-28', relying on product mix (non-par savings and protection) and expense optimisation, not on RFR benefit.
Q3 and Q4 are historically LIC's strongest quarters for first-year premium and WRP, per management.
Management is still assessing the RBC regime and the IRDAI distribution consultation paper; capital deployment decision deferred until reforms are rolled out.
Management says LIC's expense ratio is comfortably within the proposed distribution-cost caps.
capex_capacity: Office rationalisation is a work in progress, with digital adoption and process re-engineering to roll out over the next few quarters, expected to optimise expenses.
Bima Sakhi network: 3.04 lakh Bima Sakhis, 10.64 lakh policies sold, ₹1,548.80 crore NBP; covers 1,60,928 of 2,44,524 gram panchayats (66%).
Product count: 63 products as of 13 November 2026 (excluding PMJJBY), including 41 exclusive individual products, 13 exclusive group products, seven individual riders and one group rider.
Five new non-par individual products launched in H1; three more launched on 19 October 2026 (Jeevan Dhara-II deferred annuity, Health Shield and New Cancer Cover).
Hedging: about 80% of non-par premium is hedged, with maturities hedged up to 8 years.
demand_pricing: ULIP APE fell more than 40% YoY due to deliberate ticket-size push; monthly eNACH share of ULIP fell from about 24% a year ago to 14%. Protection APE is growing more than 50%.
Persistency (premium basis) at 13M/25M/37M/49M/61M was 74.69%/69.62%/67.17%/64.31%/61.03%, down from 75.29%/71.37%/67.70%/63.70%/63.81%. On a policy-count basis it improved at 13M, 37M and 49M.
Maturity claims ₹1,25,806 crore (+16.93% YoY); death claims ₹12,691 crore (+5.33%).
ANANDA agent-assisted app: 12,40,676 policies completed (+41.23% YoY).
WRP is about 55% of first-year premium and is growing 14.5%-15%, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IRDAI distribution reform (lower commissions) make LIC's agency-led non-par annuity products less competitive versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LIC is comfortable with the proposed expense caps and is well placed given its low overall expense ratio. It expects competitors to need significant work to reach these levels, so it does not foresee a near-term competitive disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: With solvency at 235%, above a typical 170-190% comfort range, how will capital be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping the current solvency margin under review until RBC and IFRS outcomes are clear, and will decide on profit distribution or capital deployment after the reforms are rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did VNB margin fall from Q1 to Q2 despite better mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business mix added 0.5% QoQ and the impact of assumptions was -1.2%, driven by an approximately 40 bps fall in RFR. Margin moved from 22.9% in Q1 to 22.3% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual APE growth lagging individual rated NBP growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a 40%+ fall in ULIP APE caused by the ticket-size push. Savings and protection growth was not enough to offset it, and convergence is expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will LIC keep growing individual APE for FY27 and what about the IDBI Bank stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong H2 APE growth from new health and deferred annuity products, term policies (over 100,000 collected), and the 70th-anniversary closed product ending 31 March. On banca, it said IDBI now accounts for about 20% of total bancassurance, and it does not foresee much depletion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY28 without RFR tailwinds, and how do group sub-segments differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to mix (non-par savings, term), expense optimisation and higher-margin group annuity and GTIS growth relative to fund-based group business. It expects a positive margin outlook for 2027-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 individual persistency on a premium basis fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said policy-count persistency improved at 13M/37M/49M, but premium persistency did not improve because persistent policies skew to lower sum-assured and premium cohorts. It called the issue product-agnostic.

risks_watch: Embedded value declined 1.95% YoY to ₹7,97,378 crore; management attributed the negative to MTM losses on debt, while core business was positive.
RFR decline (about 40 bps QoQ) may keep compressing VNB margin, and management says RFR is outside its control.
Agent network shrank (agents down about 2.2% YoY, agent market share 43.70% vs 45.86%) amid possible commission cuts under the IRDAI consultation paper.
ULIP recovery depends on market conditions; ULIP APE is down more than 40%.
Group market share fell about 230 bps YoY to 70.45%; group APE growth is cyclical and dependent on large term-group tenders.
Persistency on premium basis weakened in several cohorts (13M, 25M, 37M, 61M).
Bancassurance growth depends on IDBI Bank (about 20% of total banca) and on the bank partner mix after the IDBI privatisation.

rows.label: Bima Sakhi and alternate-channel growth
rows.why: Alternate channel NBP rose 48.01% to ₹1,122 crore and Bima Sakhi covers 66% of gram panchayats with ₹1,548.80 crore NBP, supporting volume.

543527|2026-03.headline: Prudent Q4 FY26: record ₹4,300 crore quarterly equity net sales offset MTM hit; AUM rebounded to ₹1.33 trillion by 5 May 2026.
543527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 average AUM rose 0.3% QoQ to ₹1,28,000 crore and 26% YoY despite a 14.5% market fall, helped by record quarterly equity net sales of ₹4,300 crore. Closing equity AUM fell 8.2% QoQ to ₹1,15,480 crore on ₹14,550 crore of mark-to-market losses. Revenue grew 5.1% QoQ and operating profit 19.5% QoQ, but PAT growth slowed to 2.6% QoQ because other income turned negative (₹-4.7 crore). Management flagged two regulatory items for FY27: SEBI's TER change (GST now inside the expense ratio) and withdrawal of the 5 bps exit-load benefit, with industry clarity expected by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the fee and commission expense ratio lower in Q4, and is it Indus-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a nil additional trail provision in Q4 (₹5.5 crore in Q3) plus about ₹4.5 crore of insurance revenue recognised in March, about ₹10 crore extra revenue in total. Full-year commission figures were said to be more representative.

qa_highlights.question: How will the exit-load pass-on and GST-driven TER change affect distributor payouts and yields?
qa_highlights.answer: New business yield expected broadly neutral; book impact 2-3 bps, pending clarity from a couple of AMCs. Payouts will be realigned net of GST, with the April calculation still pending, so the monetary impact cannot yet be quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 'lump sum' share of flows persist if markets recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lump sum is typically higher in corrections and the long-run mix is around 50:50; a market downturn would shift mix toward SIPs over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is SIP market share (3.5-3.7%) being lost to other platforms or direct?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct share is rising industry-wide. Prudent says it is gaining regular-plan share and rising monthly by a few bps, but it does not target a specific share level.

qa_highlights.question: What share of MFD AUM is held by larger distributors, and does leakage occur after scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no AUM share; 2,220 MFDs have crossed ₹10 crore AUM. No MFD has left after reaching ₹100 crore, per management; 40-50% of joiners are new to the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Indus AUM retention and further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Indus AUM has grown from ₹2,060 crore (Sept 2025) to ₹2,250 crore with the full team retained. Further acquisitions are being scouted but nothing is concrete.

543527|2026-06.headline: Prudent's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, with average AUM up 21% to INR1.33 lakh crores despite a 2.8 bps gross yield cut.
543527|2026-06.overview: Prudent reported Q1 FY27 with average AUM of INR1.33 lakh crores (up 21% YoY, 4% QoQ) and equity AUM of INR1.34 lakh crores as of June 2026. Operating profit rose 32.4% YoY to INR89.1 crores and PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, helped by treasury gains. New SEBI/AMC regulatory changes from April 2026 (GST treatment, exit load removal) cut gross yield by about 2.8 bps to around 88 bps and shifted commission expense lower, which management called a one-time reset. Management said the current margin should be the run-rate for the next three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: ~16% above FY26 average AUM of INR1.21 lakh crores
+18% YoY from INR1.14 lakh crores; +16.4% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Gross yield on MF average AUM
financial_highlights.change: down ~2.8 bps from 91.2 bps last quarter

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross margin last quarter and how has it moved this quarter, and what is the standalone MF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said MF margin was 91.2 bps last quarter and about 88.4 bps this quarter, a 2.8 bps fall due to the 5 bps exit load removal from TER. Segment margins are not disclosed; operating margin is the suggested proxy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 commission-to-revenue ratio (56.2% standalone) a steady-state number?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said the current margin can be used for the next three quarters and the spread should hold, as the regulatory changes were applied across the full book. Shirish Patel added that insurance mix in Q4 was higher, which also affects the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net revenue yield after commissions and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said current yield levels would likely persist in the near term; medium to long term it could fall 1 to 2 bps, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: Can MFD partners go direct once mutual-fund-only PMS is allowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said the risk is low since MFDs need a platform; a possible consolidation of licences is the bigger effect. No yield uplift is assumed from the 2.25% PMS fee structure.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the new MFD additions and what is the direct versus indirect AUM split?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said most of the increase in registrations came from existing distributors moving to Prudent's platform. Sanjay Shah put the split at roughly 90:10 (partners versus direct).

qa_highlights.question: How should AUM growth be viewed beyond MTM, and how fast is net sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said net sales historically add about 10-12% to AUM each year, and FY26 growth came mainly from net sales rather than MTM.

rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin below 17% (Q1 FY27 at 16.1%) and targets 18% within two years, with margin inching up from Q2 FY27 as fittings and spooling (10-15% of FY28 revenue) add mix and seamless utilisation rises from 85-90%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Seamless and fittings/value-added capacity live since May 20
rows.why: Seamless capacity commissioned end-May 2026 and fittings/value-added lines started May 2026, while the INR70 crore spooling facility is under construction with commissioning targeted end-Q3 FY27 against a INR185 crore LOI.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says volume growth above 15% in FY27 and FY27 revenue growth of ~20% is maintained; seamless utilisation of 85-90% is expected to rise to 80-85%+ with welded at ~60% rising to 60-65%, backed by an order book above INR600 crore (up ~INR150 crore QoQ).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is already set at ~INR100 crore (INR70 crore spooling), and seamless utilisation of 85-90% is high, but welded at ~60% is spare, so a new capex announcement is conditional on spooling execution and utilisation rising past 80-85%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth at ~20% rather than raising it, and exports (INR94 crore vs INR103 crore, down 9% YoY) are a drag with the Q2 recovery uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fittings approvals and spooling customer qualification may take months, and the spooling revenue timeline is inconsistent (INR37 crore run-rate vs ~INR70 crore FY27 target), so the ~5% FY27 spooling contribution could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (spooling end-Q3); fittings ramp FY27-28
rows.why: Fittings commercial production started May 2026 with 5-7% of FY27 revenue targeted, and the data-centre spooling line is targeted for end-Q3 FY27 with 10-15% of FY28 top line.

rows.label: Order book above INR600 crore plus INR185 crore spooling LOI
rows.why: Order book rose to above INR600 crore from about INR450 crore last quarter (~INR150 crore added), with export orders 40-45% of the book and the INR185 crore spooling LOI on top.

rows.label: Export recovery in Q2 FY27
rows.why: Exports fell to INR94 crore from INR103 crore (down ~9%) on geopolitical and container disruption, though management intends to keep exports above 30% of revenue and expects a Q2 pickup, with the recovery uncertain.

rows.label: Net debt of INR325 crore and working-capital borrowings
rows.why: Net debt is about INR325 crore at June 30, 2026 with FY27 capex of ~INR100 crore, so debt may stay elevated while the company funds spooling, and an analyst flagged interest costs against depreciation.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term 18% margin target, the INR600 crore order book and ~20% FY27 growth, but cautious on exports, fittings and spooling approval timing; analysts pushed on net debt and interest costs, the spooling revenue timeline, and export decline.

543528|2026-09.headline: Venus Pipes Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to INR361.1 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.3% from 16.3% on freight costs.
543528|2026-09.overview: Record quarterly revenue of INR361.1 crores (+23.9% YoY) and record exports of INR147.2 crores (41% of revenue) were driven by roughly 12% price increases and about 8% volume growth. EBITDA rose 9.1% to INR51.7 crores, but margin compressed to 14.3% as higher export freight and fuel costs hit; management said ex-price impact margin would have been about 15.5%. PAT was flat at about INR26 crores. The company completed a INR372 crore preferential allotment, of which about INR344 crores is earmarked to repay borrowings, with interest savings expected from H2 FY27. A spooling order of about INR29 crores from a data-centre customer was firmed, and the pipe order book is about INR640-670 crores.

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue grew around 20% YoY in Q2 FY27 per management; 54.7% of quarterly revenue. Seamless capacity utilisation above 80% in Q2, targeted above 90% in H2.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue grew around 20% YoY; 37.6% of quarterly revenue. Utilisation above 60% in Q2, targeted at 60-65% and then 70% in H2.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Only about INR9 crores revenue in H1 FY27 (2.5% of Q2 revenue). Management targets INR40-50 crores in H2 at EBITDA margin of 17-20%; new capacity of about INR60 crores completed in May 2026.

segments.name: Spooling (data centre)
segments.commentary: Firm order of about INR29 crores from a data-centre customer; revenue execution started and H2 target about INR70 crores at EBITDA margin above 30%. LOI balance of about INR155-185 crores pending conversion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Record INR147.2 crores; US was the main growth driver. Export order book is about 40% of pipe order book, with more than 50% from the US and about 40% from Europe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pipe volume growth target of around 15%; H1 volume growth was about 8% YoY, implying stronger H2.
Management expects overall value growth of 20%-plus for the year (per analyst recap, not restated in detail).
H2 pipe EBITDA margin expected to recover toward about 16% if freight rates normalise; freight fell over the last two to three days per management.
Finance cost savings of about INR12-13 crores expected in H2 FY27 after repaying about INR344 crores of borrowings; annual saving INR28-30 crores.
FY27 capex guided at INR130-140 crores (midpoint about INR135 crores), with INR30-35 crores in H2.
Spooling LOI balance expected to convert over the next 12 months, with most orders by Q2 FY28; data-centre execution targeted before December 2027.
Data-centre spooling EBITDA margin above 30%; oil and gas 20-25%; nuclear 35-40%; power about 30%.
capex_capacity: Seamless pipe facility (second) commenced operations in May 2026; volume growth expected from it.
Fittings capacity expansion completed in May 2026; spooling operations commenced ahead of original timeline.
Capex in H1 FY27 about INR105 crores, covering spooling and fittings expansion (about INR60-65 crores), solar power plant (about INR25-30 crores) and maintenance.
New capacity being added, expected operational by January or February 2027; existing and new capacity together can deliver about INR250-300 crores annual data-centre business.
Fittings: management says revenue of 3-3.5x investment is achievable, with peak revenue of INR180-200 crores on about INR60 crores investment.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR670 crores including about INR30 crores spooling order, per the call; the pipe order book is about INR640 crores, up more than 30% YoY, and expected to execute in four to five months.
Price increases above 10% YoY and above 5% QoQ; roughly 12% of the 24% revenue growth came from price, about 8% from volume and fittings.
Demand from power, engineering, oil and gas, plus newer areas such as CNG stations, semiconductor and solar.
Europe export quota cuts of about 15-20% YoY have not materially hit Venus's European volumes, per management.
Freight pass-through is partial: some export orders have freight-band clauses, and new orders are being priced to pass costs to customers. No pass-on clause for power and fuel generally.
Power and fuel costs above 3.5% of revenue, up about 1 percentage point of sales since April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the 24% revenue growth between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: About 12% from price and about 8% from volume and fittings; management targets around 15% full-year volume growth, with spooling and fittings contributing on top of pipes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per kg and margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per kg (ex-fittings) fell to INR62 from INR64 YoY, mainly due to export freight and fuel costs; management said margins should recover in H2 if freight normalises.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance changed?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in outlook: H1 spend about INR105 crores, H2 about INR30-35 crores, so FY27 about INR130-140 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pace of spooling LOI conversion and sector expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR29 crores firm so far, with the balance of LOI (about INR155-185 crores) to convert over 12 months; sector sequence is data centres, then power, oil and gas, and nuclear.

qa_highlights.question: Where do the export order book and growth come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the pipe order book, more than 50% is US, about 40% Europe, the rest Middle East and others; Q2 export growth was predominantly US-led.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the next two quarters' margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects pipe margins near 16% in H2 if freight eases, plus higher-margin spooling (above 30%) and fittings (17-20%) contributions, though it said the percentage margin may optically fall as prices rise.

risks_watch: Freight and fuel cost volatility linked to Middle East conflict; margin recovery depends on freight normalisation, which management says has only started in the last few days.
Employee expense grew about 34% YoY (analyst figure); management attributed it to capacity additions, and said further increases will be modest.
Spooling LOI conversion is uncertain (only about INR29 crores firm of about INR185 crores LOI); execution timing depends on design finalisation.
Europe quota restrictions may tighten; management says exposure is limited so far.
Working capital is about 120 days of sales, with debtors around 75-80 days.
Pipe order book is about 40% export and includes project orders that may not convert, per management.
543528|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and the spooling and fittings pipeline, but openly defensive on the Q2 margin drop, attributing it to freight and fuel costs. Management gave specific H2 targets but declined to quantify parts of the order book and spooling economics.
key_quotes: Excluding the impact of price increase, Q2FY27 EBITDA margin would have been ~15.5%.
We are hopeful, if this last two to three days, freight has already going towards downward trend.
Our export business achieved a new milestone, with exports reaching an all-time high of INR 147 crores and constituting 41% of revenue.

rows.why: Management targets ~15% FY27 pipe volume growth against H1 volume of only ~8% YoY, so H2 must accelerate, backed by a INR640-670 crore pipe order book (up >30% YoY) and spooling/fittings ramp.

rows.why: Seamless utilisation is above 80% and targeted above 90% in H2, FY27 capex guided up to INR130-140 crore with INR30-35 crore in H2, so further capacity announcements are plausible though none is named yet.

rows.why: Price increases above 10% YoY and a pipe order book up >30% support upside, but H1 volume at ~8% against a 15% target and the Q2 margin miss keep an upgrade conditional.

rows.why: H2 margin recovery depends on freight normalisation that has only just started, spooling LOI conversion is uncertain (INR29 crore firm vs INR185 crore LOI), and a 15% volume target needs H2 acceleration from ~8% in H1.

rows.why: Data-centre spooling (INR29 crore firm order, ~INR70 crore H2 target) and fittings (INR40-50 crore H2 target at 17-20% margin) ramp in H2, with sector sequence moving to power, oil and gas and nuclear afterwards.

rows.when: next 12 months, most by Q2 FY28
rows.why: Only about INR29 crore of the roughly INR185 crore LOI is firm; the INR155-185 crore balance is expected to convert over 12 months, but execution timing depends on design finalisation.

rows.label: Interest savings from INR344 crore debt repayment
rows.why: Repaying about INR344 crore of borrowings from the INR372 crore preferential allotment is expected to save INR12-13 crore in H2 FY27 and INR28-30 crore annually.

rows.why: Price increases above 10% YoY and above 5% QoQ drove about 12 points of the 24% revenue growth, and new export orders are priced to pass freight on, though power and fuel have no pass-on clause.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the spooling and fittings pipeline, and the H2 capacity additions, but defensive on the Q2 margin drop from freight and fuel costs; analysts pressed on the price-versus-volume split and margin recovery.

543529|2026-03.headline: Delhivery FY26 revenue reached ~10,486 crore with 7.3% service EBITDA and first full-year FCF positive at ~89 crore, a year ahead of plan.
543529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about 2,848 crore with PAT of about 87 crore (~3% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of 151 crore. FY26 was the first year of the Ecom Express integration, with over a billion express packages and about 2 million MT of PTL freight. Supply chain services (SCS) reached breakeven on adjusted EBITDA after a service EBITDA turnaround to 10.9%. Management said the company turned FCF positive, one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs; cash stood above 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~1,832 crore, up 46% YoY, with volumes of 306 million (up ~72-73% YoY, sequentially up on Q3). FY26 revenue ~6,685 crore and about a billion parcels; service EBITDA at upper end of 16-18% normative range.

segments.name: Part Truck Load (PTL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~622 crore and 549 thousand MT, both up ~20% YoY. FY26 about 2 million MT and ~2,254 crore revenue; management cited gross margin rising from 14% to 28% over roughly 2.5-3 years.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~729 crore with service EBITDA of 10.9% (~79 crore), up ~4x; segment at breakeven on adjusted EBITDA. Two mandates signed and activated in Q4.

segments.name: Delhivery Direct (intracity and intercity)
segments.commentary: Intracity on-demand service live in six cities; FY26 investment about 76 crore, with FY27 investment guided at 130-160 crore toward a 200+ crore external GMV run-rate.

guidance_outlook: Long-term transport ROIC target of 25%+, with adjusted EBITDA rising from ~6.3% toward at least 10%, and PTL service EBITDA moving toward ~18% and corporate overheads falling to ~7% of revenue.
Capital intensity (capex plus working-capital items) of ~21.5% of revenue could fall by 2-3 percentage points.
Capex to reach the 4% of revenue target from 4.7%; AGV and automation spend not expected to materially change capex guidance.
Net working capital at 11 days seen as sustainable; further reduction possible via faster billing and prepaid mix, though with limits.
FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore guided in the shareholder letter.
Management expects e-commerce industry to grow 15-20% in the medium term.
Management said the company does not plan a broad price increase now, though diesel pass-through clauses apply to PTL and some customers.
capex_capacity: Capex fell to 4.7% of revenue (from 7.8% in FY23); management reiterated a 4% target and said it is moving slightly ahead of plan.
Fleet metric: the 20,000 daily average fleet figure covers only contracted monthly vehicles; the decline reflects a shift to per-kilo variable fleet, while tractor-trailer count rose QoQ.
AGV pilots in Mumbai (Bombay) to be expanded to other mega gateways within FY27.
Delhivery Labs launched about a year ago; AI and automation deployed in claims, documentation and customer communication.
Company is the first in India to get a road train, after a 46-foot tractor trailer launch.
demand_pricing: Management said market structure is more settled after the Ecom Express deal, with less short-term price gouging than in the two years before FY26.
Share of 1P (first-party) logistics declined over the last year, per a listed marketplace; management expects a gradual shift towards 3P.
Long-tail D2C/SME share described as stable to slightly up YoY; heavy shipping share described as dominant.
Single largest customer was ~16% of revenue last year; management said it is well below its informal 35% concern threshold.

Diesel price hikes of about Rs 3/litre at pumps: prices indexed for PTL; express pass-through is via DPH clauses assessed customer by customer. Rs 1-2 price increases seen in some air-network pockets via surcharges.
Management dismissed Amazon's reopening of its 3PL offering as an old product with limited strategic value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising fuel prices on consumption and costs, and has Delhivery raised prices?
qa_highlights.answer: PTL prices are diesel-indexed; express uses DPH clauses. Pump prices rose about Rs 3, and no broad price hike is planned. Q4 margins rose over Q3 despite fuel, and a volatile environment is seen as favourable to the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon's 3PL push a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an old product in a new wrapper; first-party orders get priority at last mile and first-party logistics costs more than 3PL when fully loaded.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers included faster and more accurate billing, client selection (declining some RFQs), and more-than-monthly billing for preferential pricing. NWC was 11 days versus 38 three years ago; management called it sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will SCS pipeline remain margin accretive, and how much of new initiatives' investment is opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Each SCS project must clear an internal hurdle rate and the pipeline is in focus sectors. Short-term start-up costs can weigh on P&L. Management did not give a split of the 130-160 crore FY27 spend between opex and capex in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex intensity rise with express growth, and will the industry overbuild?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex intensity is expected to stay around the 4% target; growth is mainly PTL and heavy, and management does not expect irrational pricing like three or four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Delhivery Direct opportunity and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Intracity service live in six cities; FY26 spend ~76 crore; FY27 guided at 130-160 crore toward 200+ crore external GMV run-rate. Management described the TAM as very large without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: Is PTL leadership achievable, and what capabilities are missing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PTL growth from ~280-290k tons to ~550k tons per quarter over 2-3 years with gross margin from 14% to 28%. Varun Bakshi said the playbook is share-of-wallet expansion with key accounts.

risks_watch: Fuel-price pass-through: the impact on volumes and consumption is not yet quantified; management said Q2 would show more.
Competitive dynamics from 1P marketplaces insourcing or reopening 3PL offerings, plus possible share shifts in key accounts.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and gig worker laws, and potential increase in service costs.
Concentration: the largest customer rose above 16% of revenue; management says it is not near its informal 35% limit.
Working capital at 11 days may be hard to sustain; management flagged limits on further billing-cycle gains.
New businesses (Delhivery Direct, Rapid, SCS pipeline) carry 130-160 crore of FY27 investment that could weigh on margins.
Management noted a 'volatile start' to FY27 without details.
543529|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, FCF and market position, with specific numeric targets. Cautious and somewhat deflective on fuel-price consumption impact, saying it is too early to quantify, and on the ex-Ecom FCF question.
key_quotes: So, in effect, we are signing off FY26 with strong fundamentals across every line of business.
The core is profitable. The core is cash generative. SCS is pivoted.
But I'll be honest, Mukesh, I've been saying this for three years now. I don't lose a lot of sleep over this and I don't think our customers do either.
The steady state ROICs, currently we are at 16%, but in a steady state, this number for our transport business can certainly go to 25% plus.

financial_highlights.change: Service EBITDA up ~220 bps to 15.6% for transport (express + PTL)
One year ahead of plan; management said it absorbed integration costs

rows.why: Transport adjusted EBITDA rose 260 bps to 6.3% in FY26 and management targets at least 10% via PTL gross margin moving from 14% to 28% over 2.5-3 years, plus corporate overheads falling to ~7% of revenue; Express already at upper end of 16-18% normative band, but FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore and fuel-cost pressure could offset gains.

rows.why: Capex fell to 4.7% of revenue with a 4% target reiterated and AGV pilots in Mumbai to expand to other mega gateways within FY27; Delhivery Direct intracity is live in six cities with 130-160 crore FY27 spend toward a 200+ crore GMV run-rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Express volumes at 306 million in Q4 (up ~72-73% YoY) and PTL tonnage at 549k MT (up ~20% YoY), with PTL aiming from ~280-290k to ~550k tons per quarter over 2-3 years and e-commerce industry guided at 15-20% growth; fuel-driven consumption impact not yet quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex intensity is falling (7.8% in FY23 to 4.7% in FY26) and management reiterated a 4% target without a new plant or capacity plan; utilisation not disclosed, so no sign of a capacity-driven capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident and says it is moving slightly ahead of plan on capex and was FCF positive a year early, but gave no explicit FY27 revenue or margin number, so an upgrade is conditional on fuel and new-business costs.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.when: Q1 FY28 onward, with Q2 FY27 the first read
rows.why: Fuel-price pass-through effect on volumes is unquantified (management says Q2 will show more), FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore may weigh on margins, labour cost inflation from minimum wage and gig worker laws, and management flagged a 'volatile start' to FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Delhivery Direct intracity is live in six cities with an external GMV target of 200+ crore run-rate, AGV automation pilots are expanding within FY27, and SCS has two mandates activated in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Net working capital at 11 days, sustainable but limited further gains
rows.why: NWC fell from 38 days three years ago to 11 days; management calls this sustainable but flagged limits on further billing-cycle gains, so further release is unlikely to be large.

rows.label: FCF positive for first full year, cash above 4,500 crore
rows.why: FY26 FCF was about 89 crore positive, one year ahead of plan, with cash and equivalents over 4,500 crore after absorbing integration costs.

rows.label: Supply chain services breakeven and margin turnaround
rows.why: SCS service EBITDA rose to 10.9% (about 79 crore) in FY26 from 2.2%, and adjusted EBITDA reached breakeven, with two mandates activated in Q4 and each project clearing an internal hurdle rate.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, FCF, capex intensity and market structure, but cautious and deflective on the fuel-price impact on consumption and on the ex-Ecom FCF question; analysts pushed on fuel pass-through, Amazon's 3PL push, and the split of the 130-160 crore FY27 spend.

543529|2026-06.headline: Delhivery Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to nearly Rs.3,000 Cr, with PAT of Rs.17 Cr after a Rs.15 Cr-plus cost drag from two new contracts and unused assets.
543529|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as a record quarter for revenue but a weak one for profitability, hit by chronic labour shortages, election and weather disruptions, and start-up costs for two large new contracts. Express acquisition consolidation drove much of the 55% YoY growth in the reported figures. PTL yield rose to nearly Rs.12 per kg (per management's wording), and management attributed most of the improvement to organic gains rather than pass-through. Diesel price hikes in May are being passed through to customers with a lag, and management said FY27 outlook is unchanged at 20-30% growth.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.17 Cr (stat P&L ~Rs.30 Cr before ROU/intangible-related items)
financial_highlights.change: Management said PAT before unused-asset costs was ~Rs.62 Cr in press release; reconciliation given on call
Target 16-18% long term; internal exit target 15-15.5%
Stable across FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs.35 Cr per management, Rs.30-35 Cr normalised
financial_highlights.change: Relates to Rs.17 Cr in Q1 and delay in Q2
Q1 average linehaul cost ~12.2% of revenue, up ~0.6 pp (diesel)

segments.name: Express / e-commerce & B2B
segments.commentary: Express EBITDA margin exited at 13.4%, with an internal target of 15-15.5% exit and 16-18% long-term. Q1 growth of 55% was flattered by Express base effects, since the acquisition was reported in full only from Q2.

segments.name: PTL (Part Truck Load)
segments.commentary: Tonnage of 542,000 tonnes (+18% YoY) and yield of nearly Rs.12/kg (+20% YoY). Management said most of the yield gain was organic, about 37 paise per kg improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel-linked pass-through.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: Two new large contracts (industrials and durables) depressed margins in Q1 during fulfilment-centre build-up; billing starts on outbound, so inbound buildup costs are front-loaded. Management expects stabilisation over Q2 and early Q3.

segments.name: New initiatives (Local, Direct, Maps)
segments.commentary: Local ARR is at Rs.150 Cr in July, versus an earlier target of Rs.250 Cr exit ARR for FY27; management revised its expectation to Rs.160-175 Cr. Ahmedabad Local is expected to break even around month three. NBFC approval received in July.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30%; the range is wider because the outcome depends on Q2 and early Q3 trends.
FY27 profitability and medium/long-term targets were said to be unchanged, with no major structural headwinds seen by management.
Diesel: management says the pass-through is almost 100% covered (97-98% per Varun Bakshi). July is expected to reflect the May diesel hike with the lag gone.
Corporate manpower costs estimated at Rs.371 Cr for FY27 (as stated on call).
Unused-asset (lock-in/ROU) costs of around Rs.17 Cr are expected to continue until disposal, per management, and are treated as ongoing rather than one-time.
capex_capacity: Two new large SCS contracts required build-up of multiple fulfilment sites with a 45-60 day lead to inbound stock before outbound billing ramps.
Automation: in-facility movement and automated storage/retrieval being introduced at key transportation and fulfilment facilities.
Maps (proprietary GIS) launched on 8 August for internal deployment, with external availability planned later.
Expansion of cross-sell development teams for truck and LCV businesses; coverage now 100% of India versus earlier top-3 cities.
demand_pricing: Demand continued into Q2, with festive-season sales starting to lift volumes; August to date is said to be robust.
D2C volumes are running at 40-45% of PTL volumes and skew to heavier packages, which supports yields.
Pricing contracts are indexed to the prevailing month's diesel rate. Diesel-driven revisions were under negotiation from late April to mid-May, and pass-throughs are expected to show in Q2.
Management said pricing pressure has eased, with no price cuts for customers and reduced irrational competition. Competitor price cuts were disputed by management as not matching its own contracts.
New customer adds were mainly D2C and SME; management said self-serve sign-up through DelhiveryOne is growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-30% revenue growth guidance range, and what is the trend in new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was soft seasonally but robust after adjusting for Express, and the range is wider because Q2 and early Q3 trends are still forming. New customers are mostly D2C and SME, with festive demand building.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PTL yield increase seasonal or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield gains are planned and organic, with about 37 paise per kg of improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel pass-through; the sustained QoQ improvement is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps margin pressure is from diesel versus other costs, and how quickly can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is about 0.6 pp of revenue for PTL; the bigger hit is labour-related minimum wage and rider payout linkage, which lacks a pass-through clause. Diesel revisions have been mostly passed through, and the effect should be evident in Q2.

543529|2026-09.headline: Delhivery Q2 FY27 revenue crossed Rs 3,066 Cr (+20% YoY) with adjusted PAT of Rs 41 Cr; management says volume guidance of 20-30% is tracking toward the lower end.
543529|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as satisfactory against a challenging macro backdrop, with record shipment volume of 325 million (+32% YoY) and revenue of Rs 3,066 Cr (+20% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA came in at Rs 123 Cr (4% of revenue) and PAT at Rs 41 Cr, with cash of Rs 4,676 Cr on the balance sheet. Management said October volumes were strong and that the company is not revising its 20-30% volume growth estimate, which it now sees at the lower end of the range. Newer businesses (Local LCV rental, Direct consumer, International, Saver) were reported ahead of prior expectations, while Express margin is guided to be roughly flat with FY26 and the management said that a 17% full-year margin looks achievable.

segments.name: Express (PTL)
segments.commentary: Management expects the PTL business to remain a key growth driver and said Express margin is at roughly FY26 levels, with an aim of about 17% full-year margin. PTL realisation improved on contractual revisions and yield gains, and PTL revenue was reported up 23% YoY.

segments.name: Local (LCV rental, on-demand)
segments.commentary: Annualised revenue run-rate crossed Rs 200 Cr across 8 cities, ahead of the Rs 240-250 Cr exit target, and CM breakeven is now seen as early as Q4 vs earlier mid-FY28 expectation.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Standalone run-rate is close to Rs 150 Cr and has reached profitability, which management said came earlier than expected.

segments.name: Direct (consumer)
segments.commentary: Consumer business run-rate is close to Rs 100 Cr after about 15 months of investment. The Saver product is at close to Rs 140 Cr ARR, up 55% QoQ.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: Management said SCS margins are now normative and the segment has stabilised. The pipeline is intact, but sales cycles have lengthened, and the company is focused on retaining existing clients.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth: management is not revising the 20-30% FY27 estimate and sees the company at the lower end of that range, with October flagged as a strong month.

Express margin: about 17% expected for FY27, with the 16-18% band cited in the shareholder letter; management said 17% is roughly the expected level and flagged no disastrous event that would take it off that level.
Aggregated margin expansion of 130-150 bps conservatively over FY26-FY27 is estimated.
Local (LCV) FY27 loss envelope of Rs 130-160 Cr is maintained, with H1 loss of Rs 67 Cr; management expects to end near the lower end, subject to the contribution trajectory.
Corporate overhead as a percent of revenue is expected to come down, with the 7% level seen taking about 24 months.
Management expects a TAM of about Rs 15,000-20,000 Cr for PTL, with a 15-20% growth target in the medium term.
capex_capacity: Investment in automation: management described tractor trailers, sorters and ASRS as previous paybacks, and said robotics in mid-mile are at pilot stage with payback expected to match earlier TT and sorter cycles.
Company is a 40% shareholder in Falcon Autotech, with self-developed autonomous guided vehicles for in-facility movement.

Company is building out facilities in the top 15 cities for the intra-city NDD (next-day) network. Rapid commerce (dark store model) was stopped after a pilot in 20-30 dark stores across three cities.
Management noted that the company is investing to add capacity in new centres and said it is not looking to be asset light.
demand_pricing: Volume: strong Q2, with October described as a good month and the wider consumption environment holding up despite the macro challenges.

Pricing: about 96-97% of PTL is covered by automatic adjustments for diesel and wage changes. Management said a 2 rupee 40 paisa per-unit increase in PTL yield occurred Q1 to Q2 FY27, roughly half from contractual revisions.
Competition: management expects the marketplace share (about 85% of e-commerce volume) to remain stable, and said the non-e-commerce business is growing faster and is not materially concentrated.
Market size: management said the company is targeting enterprise and non-marketplace clients, with 128,000 enterprises above Rs 5 Cr revenue and 30,000 above Rs 100 Cr in its target base.
Sales productivity: the company is using AI to generate bids and has saved about USD 1 million a year on Google Maps API costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk to the 20-30% volume guidance, and where is the growth coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were strong, October was a good month, and there is no reason to revise the estimate; it is now at the lower end of the 20-30% range.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said unbilled revenue is an accounting accrual for partially completed shipments, so AI helps collections and billing accuracy but does not eliminate unbilled.

543533|2026-09.headline: eMudhra Q2 FY27 total income rose 19.6% to INR 209 crore and PAT rose 26.3% to INR 33.4 crore, but FY27 guidance was cut after a TLS certificate incident.

Operating cash flow was weighed by lower creditors after timely payments.

543547|2026-06.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (INR101 cr, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export price gains.
543547|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 29% YoY and EBITDA rose 27% to about INR101 crore at a 10% margin, the first quarter above INR100 crore. PAT was about INR64 crore, up 22% YoY. Growth was driven mainly by export pricing (about INR300 crore export revenue, mostly MENA) rather than volume, with export volumes up only single digits and total volume up about 1% YoY. Capacity utilisation averaged about 66% as the new 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant, commissioned in April 2026, ramps up at roughly 20-25%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth and a 13-14% revenue target, and said it expects to beat it.

financial_highlights.value: Up 29% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)
INR101 crore approx; first time above INR100 crore

financial_highlights.change: Up in absolute terms; management cites about INR2.5-3 per ton of war/volatility premium

financial_highlights.value: About INR300-330 crore in Q1, partly carried over from Q4 shipments (~1,000 t)
Risen in Q1 due to working capital borrowing; management says easing from July

segments.name: Cables and wires (export)
segments.commentary: Primary growth driver in Q1; about INR300+ crore export revenue, mainly MENA, with pricing rather than volume the main gain. Management says export volume grew only single digits.

segments.name: XLPE compounds
segments.commentary: Installed XLPE capacity rose to 214,500 t after the 48,000 t Bhiwadi greenfield plant (commissioned April 2026); company holds more than one-third share of the XLPE segment. Bhiwadi expected to add about INR500 crore revenue at full utilisation.

segments.name: Engineering plastics
segments.commentary: Low volume but management cites 10-15% EBITDA margin; focus kept on lighting-industry niche (about 4 years of work).

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: New vertical; first phase about 1 GW / 1 GWh, supply model first, EBITDA margin 6-8% initially, capex plus working capital INR150-200 crore funded from internal accruals; timeline shifting by a couple of quarters, with mid-FY29 cited for 1 GW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target about 15%, with the target volume at 231,000 t and about 60,000 t per quarter needed for the remaining quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guidance about 13-14%, built on FY26 average realisation of about INR145/kg with no price increase assumed; management says it expects to beat guidance.
Long-term EBITDA margin target 10-12% (INR16-17/t), but Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6 is not expected to be sustained every quarter.
Bhiwadi plant assumed at about 50% average utilisation in FY27, generating about INR200-250 crore of revenue; FY30 top-line ambition INR5,000 crore.
Resin prices expected to take 3-6 months to normalise after the Hormuz/war situation clears.
Committed capex for FY27 about INR150-175 crore (East MV cable capacity, HFFR expansion to 20,000 t, new Vapi site, BESS); about INR77 crore already spent in Q1.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 316,400 t per annum as of June 2026; management cites 334,400 t by year-end and about 231,000 t planned FY27 tonnage.
Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 t commissioned April 2026, running at about 20-25% utilisation; expected to ramp over the next couple of months.
HFFR capacity to be expanded to 20,000 t by FY27 end; new Vapi site for product consolidation; PVC addition of about 25,000 t mentioned.

East India (Bengal) plant for medium-voltage cable compounds being set up; the BESS location is being shifted from West to East, delaying timelines by a couple of quarters, with the state incentive policy expected around end-August.
BESS phase 1 about 1 GW / 1 GWh, funded from internal accruals; BOO/BOOT not planned for now.
demand_pricing: Export pricing was the main Q1 driver: freight and raw material uncertainty let the company quote war-risk premiums, and management says export realisations rose about 30%.
Domestic demand softened in Q1 because of high polymer prices; management expects volume recovery once price volatility eases.
Management says the company's cable-customer segment grows about 12-13% a year, which is the basis for the 15% volume target, with the extra 2-3% expected to come from market share gains.
Share gain thesis: the Bhiwadi plant targets Rajasthan and Delhi customers; some western capacity moves to European exports.
Management expects EBITDA/t to stay elevated only for a few months; prices in July were marginally lower and August is 'okay', but orders are spot with 10-20 day visibility.
Cash conversion cycle widened in Q1 due to higher inventory and debtors; expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q4 export revenue spilled into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 t moved from late-March shipments; value rose due to freight, so about INR300+ crore export revenue was reported in Q1, partly from Q4 volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA/t sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR19.6/t may not hold each quarter but could last a few months; the long-term target is INR16-17/t or 10-12% margin. The war-risk premium is about INR2.5-3/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as a supply model at 6-8% EBITDA margin, with EPC adding 2-5 points and system integrator another 2-3 points; long-term target 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance (13-14% revenue) below capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average prices, assumes about 50% Bhiwadi utilisation and 15% volume growth; management says it expects to beat guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs and cash conversion cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose from working-capital borrowing after the March raw material spike; they have eased since July. Cash conversion cycle expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management cites the Bhiwadi plant and importers being displaced by supply-chain disruption. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

Volume growth gap: Q1 volume up only about 1% YoY against the 15% FY27 target, requiring about 60,000 t per quarter in Q2-Q4; recovery depends on Bhiwadi ramp (20-25% now, about 50% assumed) and domestic demand returning as polymer prices ease.
Export pricing exposure: prices eased marginally in July, export revenue for Q2 may be below the ~INR300-330 crore of Q1; order book is spot with 10-20 day visibility.
Resin and crude path: Hormuz situation and Iran-related announcements could keep prices volatile; management expects resin prices to take 3-6 months to normalise after the situation clears.

BESS execution: relocation from West to East delays timelines by a couple of quarters; 1 GW mid-FY29 timeline, state incentive policy expected around end-August; bids being retendered at low prices; margin 6-8% initially.

Working capital and finance cost: finance cost rose on working-capital borrowing and cash conversion cycle widened; management expects easing from July and CCC of 55-60 days, which needs to be verified in Q2.

So, if you ask in terms of numbers, technically, it may be around 1,000-odd tons, which has been moved, but the value has changed later on because of increase in freight and all.

543573|2026-03.headline: Syrma SGS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR1,477 crore at 11.9% operating EBITDA margin; FY27 EBITDA guided to INR700 crore.
543573|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: consolidated revenue INR1,477 crore (+56% YoY, +16% QoQ), operating EBITDA INR174 crore (+51% YoY) at 11.9% margin, and PAT INR119 crore (+67% YoY). FY26 revenue reached INR4,857 crore (+27%), operating EBITDA INR545 crore (+68%, margin 11.3%), and the company moved to a net cash position of INR467 crore. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 30-35%, operating EBITDA margin of 10-10.5% (said to be conservative) and EBITDA of about INR700 crore, and is investing in a large PCB project. The Ksolare acquisition via the Premier Energies JV was dropped, and a greenfield renewable-inverter plan is being evaluated instead.

segments.name: Industrial

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: 26% of Q4 revenue; about 31% of FY26 revenue (INR1,452 crore). Management caps it below 35% and pegs it near 30%, growing about 8-10% in FY27; about 30% of order book.

segments.commentary: 24% of Q4 revenue; grew 39% in FY26. Auto exports crossed INR125 crore; about 29% of order book; FY27 growth expected to be mainly domestic.

segments.name: Healthcare (MedTech)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% in FY26 from INR291 crore to INR395 crore; management expects it to exceed INR500 crore in FY27. About 5% of order book.

segments.name: IT and railways
segments.commentary: Grew 182% YoY in Q4 and 74% in FY26; annualised revenue rose from about INR240 crore to INR476 crore. IT covers laptop, motherboard and memory products. About 11% of order book; management expects 30-40% growth going forward.

segments.name: ODM
segments.commentary: Revenue rose about 80% from INR453 crore to INR825 crore in FY26; share about 17% of revenue versus 12% a year earlier.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR1,200 crore+ in FY26 (24-25% of revenue), up 41%; Q4 run rate about INR125 crore per month. FY27 target about INR1,500 crore (20-30% growth).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-35%; management says the blended growth will be near 30-35% with individual verticals ranging from about 28% to 35%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11% (earlier stated as at least 10-10.5%), kept conservative despite FY26 margin of about 12%.
Targeting about INR700 crore of EBITDA in FY27, a 30% absolute increase per management.
FY27 exports targeted at about INR1,500 crore; FY27 capex of INR100-150 crore organic plus PCB project spend.

Working capital days to be pushed down further, but management said it will not chase growth at the expense of working capital.
