Commissioning of the first PCB phase expected towards the end of FY27 or start of FY28; partial government incentive claims thereafter, with at least a one-year lag. Management says the subsidy is expected at 50-60% of the spend.
ECMS approvals received for CCL (copper clad laminate), HDI and flex PCB; about INR800 crore capex expected to be executed between FY28 and FY30.
FY26 capex was about INR140 crore; FY27 organic capex planned at INR100-150 crore.
Real-time monitoring system being rolled out across assembly lines in phases; management reports a 5-7% improvement in operational efficiency so far.

Renewable energy/inverter: Ksolare acquisition via Premier Energies JV dropped after the seller did not meet conditions precedent; minimal expense charged to P&L. Management now plans a greenfield project and is evaluating technology partner proposals, with an update expected in the coming quarter.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR6,600 crore at March-end 2026 (auto 29%, consumer 30%, industrial 24%, healthcare 5%, IT and railways 11%). Net addition of about INR200 crore after Q4 deliveries; Elcome is about 5% of the order book.
Q4 run rate is about INR500 crore per month. Management says the second half is seasonally stronger than the first half.
Customer concentration (FY26): top 5 about 34% of revenue, top 10 about 47%, top 20 about 63%.
32 new customers onboarded in FY26 (about 7 in industrial). Management says they could add about INR1,000 crore to FY26 revenue and about INR2,500 crore per year long-term.

Pass-through clauses exist in customer contracts for metal and logistics cost variation, but recovery is negotiated and is not immediate. Management expects partial cost increases to be offset by better buying and efficiency, with costs shared across vendor, customer and end consumer.

Smart metering: about INR250-260 crore of revenue in FY26, with a gross material margin of about 12-15%; management is being selective given working capital intensity. Elcome has a 3-6 month working capital cycle, and defence is a high-margin ODM business.

Competition: management said competitive intensity will rise as Tier-2 global EMS players and large Indian groups enter; it claims a cost advantage. Global addressable market is cited at over $600 million, against about $500 million of current revenue.
EU FTA: about a 1-1.5% duty benefit in select cases; management says the longer-term impact is positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex profile for the PCB and other projects, and when do the government incentives start?
qa_highlights.answer: PCB phase 1 is INR400 crore (INR250 crore in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28). Organic capex is INR100-150 crore a year. Commissioning is expected towards the end of FY27 or the start of FY28, with incentives claimed in part and typically lagging by a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw-material and inflation outlook, and how are costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal prices, logistics and shipping routes are affected by the Middle East crisis. Contracts have pass-through clauses but recovery is negotiated and takes time. Management says better buying and efficiency can offset part of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guided at 10.5-11% when Q4 was 11.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is being conservative given geopolitics, shipping and metal-price volatility. It says it prefers to beat its guidance and will revise it at the Q1 call if conditions stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company fund the PCB capex without running short of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the project will be funded through debt, internal accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution, with subsidies of 50-60% expected. It says cash will not fall short over the project life. Balance-sheet cash is INR829 crore against a net cash position of INR470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth comes from market share gains versus industry growth, and how does the PCB business affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the growth to market share and wallet-share gains, portfolio expansion (MedTech, defence) and larger customer contracts. PCB revenue is incremental, starting in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EU and export outlook, and what is the PLI benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Export guidance is INR1,500 crore for FY27, about 25-30% growth. Management expects at least 25% growth over the coming years. FY26 gross PLI was about INR80 crore and net about INR38 crore; Q4 net PLI was about INR10-12 crore.

543573|2026-06.headline: Syrma SGS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY to Rs 1,604 crore and PAT rose 112% to Rs 106 crore; FY27 guidance of 35%+ growth reaffirmed and possibly exceeded.
543573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,604 crore (+67% YoY), with operating EBITDA of Rs 162 crore (+69%, 10.1% margin) and PAT of Rs 106 crore (+112%). Growth was led by consumer ramp-ups, exports (+61% to about Rs 387 crore) and ODM (Rs 270 crore, about 115% YoY but down sequentially from Rs 345 crore in Q4). Management attributed the quarter to normal run-rate business rather than one-time items, and said supply-chain constraints (PCB chemicals, component lead times) led to a deliberate build in inventory, pushing net working capital days from 63 to 71. Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said FY27 revenue growth would be 35%+, with a view to exceed guidance.

segments.name: Automotive

543591|2026-06.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR39 crore, down from INR52.6 crore in the previous quarter and well below INR348.9 crore in Q1 FY26. Management attributed the sequential drop mainly to lower global lounge traffic from the Middle East conflict, partly offset by India business. Gross profit was negative INR0.9 crore, reflecting an upfront minimum guarantee payment for global lounge expansion, and PAT was negative INR13.8 crore. Cash rose to INR193.3 crore on collections, and net worth stood at INR300.4 crore. Management guided to adjusted EBITDA breakeven by next year, while holding the earlier H2 FY28 commitment.

543591|2026-09.headline: Dreamfolks Q2 FY27 revenue fell to INR 31.1 crore (from INR 39.0 crore in Q1) while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 8.8 crore.

Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative INR 8.8 crore from negative INR 16.4 crore in Q1, helped by the absence of the one-time upfront minimum guarantee paid in Q1 for global lounge expansion. Management highlighted the return to positive gross profit, an 8.7% gross profit margin for H1 FY27, and non-airport-lounge services contributing more than one-third of topline. Net worth declined to INR 290.1 crore from INR 313.8 crore at March 2026, while liquid balances rose to INR 187.8 crore.

543596|2026-06.headline: TMB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 34.97% YoY to a record INR412 crores, with total business up 23% to INR1,21,715 crores.
543596|2026-06.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported its strongest quarter on record: net profit of INR412 crores (up 34.97% YoY), NII up 32.01%, and operating profit of INR611 crores (up 48.22%). Total business grew 23%, driven by advances up 27.01% (gold-heavy, with agri at 40% of the book) and deposits up 19.71%, with term deposits up 20.73% and CASA down 2.95% QoQ as the bank prioritised resource mobilisation. Management raised FY27 guidance for deposits, advances and total business by 2 percentage points each, and cut its cost-to-income guidance, while stating that ECL transition provisioning (INR276 crores set aside so far) will be phased in. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 0.69% and NNPA at 0.17%.

segments.name: Agri (incl. gold loans)
segments.commentary: 40% of advances; yield raised to 10.54% from 9.75%, which management attributes to deliberate gold loan repricing. Gold loan portfolio yield is 10.58%; management says the book can absorb about a 20% fall in gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: 28% of advances; YoY growth of 20.09% (earlier cited 14.89%), adding about INR500 crores per quarter. Yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 25% of advances. Home loans are declining but the decline is arrested; vehicle loans grew 25.7%. Retail shows a QoQ decline, which management partly attributes to migration from retail to agri gold loans.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 5.62% of advances; grew 6.69% YoY. Unsecured exposure is 10 bps of the book, with NPA of about INR56 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 CASA growth guidance of 17-18% reiterated; management expects CASA to recover from Q2 with 60 branch openings planned this year (6 opened in Q1).
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 18% from 16%; advances growth guidance raised to 21-22% from 20%; total business growth guidance raised to 20% from 18%.
NIM guidance: management expects to be well past 4% for the year versus the earlier 3.90% guide. ROA now expected to be well above 2% versus the earlier 1.9% guide.
ROE guidance revised to 15% (stated as a revised guidance). GNPA to stay below 1%.
Cost-to-income: earlier 46-47% range; management says it is revising this downwards by about 2 percentage points, after Q1 at 39.10%.

ECL: INR324 crores additional provision requirement at 30 June 2026; with INR250 crores COVID contingency provision and INR26 crores added in Q1, INR276 crores is set aside. No further provisions planned in Q2; phasing over 4-5 years permitted by RBI, with the bank aiming to complete it earlier.
FY27 IT budget of around INR280 crores; cybersecurity about 10% of this, with management signalling it will not be a constraint on spending.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 628 after 6 additions in Q1 (3 in Tamil Nadu, 3 outside); 171 branches are outside Tamil Nadu. Plan to open 60 branches in FY27 versus 44 in FY26.
IT spend of about INR280 crores in FY27: infrastructure 21%, new software acquisition and enhancement about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35% (as stated).
Business per employee INR23.75 crores; profit per employee INR32.12 lakh; 325 new employees recruited in Q1.
CD ratio 88.97% against a stated maximum of 99% on the bank's net worth; management expects term deposit focus to moderate CD ratio gains.
Leverage ratio 12.5% (regulatory minimum 3.5%); LCR 140.74%; NSFR 150.74%.
demand_pricing: Management expects gold loan growth to slow in H2 FY27 as gold prices stabilise around $4,000 per ounce; growth will be driven by tonnage and new customers rather than price.
Gold loan LTV: average 56.98%; consumption loans capped at 85% (principal plus accrued interest); agri gold loans have no LTV cap. Gold loans are 6-month or 1-year bullet structures, not EMI.
Gold loan share of advances is 46.97% (the transcript corrected 47.82%), with an informal internal cap of 50%.
Retail growth to come from vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and home loans (8-10% growth targeted for FY27) and LAP. MSME is targeted to grow 21-22%, combined with gold loans.
MSME to be grown through a hybrid CGTMSE-plus-collateral model; CGTMSE described as one of the ways to grow, not the main route.

qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the April guidance structure but raised it: deposits 16% to 18%, advances 20% to 21-22%, total business 18% to 20%, CASA 17-18% reiterated, NIM well past 4% (vs 3.90%), ROA well over 2% (vs 1.9%), ROE revised to 15%, GNPA below 1%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME (YoY growth now above 20% vs 14.89% earlier, about INR500 crores added per quarter) as the lever to fill the gap as gold loan growth slows in H2 FY27 with gold prices stabilising near $4,000 an ounce.

qa_highlights.question: Laksh (Share India Securities) asked for MSME growth guidance and whether El Nino or the war had affected the book.
qa_highlights.answer: No specific MSME guidance yet; management said it would come back after the quarter, but expects growth well above the 20%-plus number put on the table. No stress seen so far from El Nino or the war, based on cash-flow studies and customer outreach.

qa_highlights.question: Parth asked about the Enforcement Directorate order on the foreign-investor shares and whether they are now free of encumbrance.

Nair attributed part of the QoQ retail decline to migration from retail gold loans to agri gold loans.

qa_highlights.answer: The INR37 crore MSME slippage relates to only 2 accounts and is expected to be resolved in Q2. Gross NPA is INR160.35 crores vs INR202.34 crores in June 2025. Growth focus is home loans, vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and LAP.

qa_highlights.answer: IT budget is about INR280 crores: infrastructure 21%, software about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35%. ECL: INR276 crores set aside (INR250 crores COVID contingency plus INR26 crores in Q1) against INR324 crores required; no further provision planned in the current quarter, with completion targeted in FY28 and possibly earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vinith Jain asked whether there is an internal ceiling on the gold loan share, now 46.97% (corrected from 47.82%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management has an informal internal cap of 50% on the gold loan share. It expects the share to rise slightly but not significantly, and wants non-gold segments to grow in tandem.

qa_highlights.question: Nishit Shah (ViSolitech) asked whether CGTMSE is a route to grow MSME and whether a sub-40% cost-to-income ratio is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: CGTMSE is one route, used as a hybrid with collateral as skin in the game, not the main strategy. Management had earlier guided 46-47% cost-to-income, now revised down by about 2 percentage points; the sub-40% Q1 print included one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co) asked how the gold loan tonnage strategy differs from today and whether operating profit can hold near INR611 crores.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is shifting from price-led to tonnage and new customers, with branch advertising and gold loans delivered in under 10 minutes. On sustaining profit, management said MSME at a 10%-plus yield and other segments would support profit growth; it deferred a direct answer to the Q2 call.

543596|2026-09.headline: TMB posted record Q2 FY27 net profit of INR451 crore (+42.09% YoY) on 27.25% business growth, with net NPA at 0.14%.
543596|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 as its eighth straight quarter of beating the prior quarter's growth, with total business up 27.25% YoY to INR1,30,237 crore and net profit at a record INR451 crore. Net interest income rose to INR807 crore and NIM was 4.19%, down about 10 bps QoQ as term-deposit mix and refinance (about INR1,000 crore at 7-7.5%) pushed up funding costs. The bank made full provisions for SMA-1 and SMA-2 ahead of ECL norms effective 1 April 2027, with provisions of INR304.24 crore against an estimated INR385 crore ECL requirement. Management raised FY27 floors for deposits (20%+) and advances (22%+), and guided NIM at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR29,280 crore, of which agri about INR22,000 crore and retail about INR6,084 crore. Portfolio LTV 62.35%; about 3.1% of book would be above market value on a 20% gold price fall; gold loan SMA-0-to-3 at risk about INR28 crore (0.10%).

segments.name: Advances and MSME
segments.commentary: Advances up 29.32% to INR60,691 crore; MSME growth 23.62%. Unsecured exposure about 20 bps; the uptick was a loan to Kerala State Electricity Board secured against cash flows. About 52% of advances are repo-linked, 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 25.49% to INR69,546 crore, with term deposits up about 29%. Non-callable deposits were 40.62% of incremental term deposits (INR7,570 crore in H1). FCNR(B) raised about USD51.94 million; 1-year FCNR(B) rate now about 4.25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth floor raised to 20%+ from earlier 18%+; advances growth floor 22%+; CASA growth about 17% in H2.
NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, versus the earlier 4% guidance.
Cost to income expected to rise from 38.28% but stay well below 44% as branches open and IT investment continues.
Target of 60 branch openings in FY27 (9 opened in H1), with 20+ outside Tamil Nadu by year-end.
Long-term aim is to grow 4-5 percentage points faster than the industry over the next 3-5 years.
CD ratio can rise to 98% against 87.27% currently, given net worth of 12.53% of the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Nine branches opened in H1 FY27; 60 planned for the year, with 37 opened YoY (15 outside Tamil Nadu).
Business per employee at INR25 crore; profit per employee about INR35 lakh.
Ongoing IT investment and data/process automation cited as drivers of productivity and cost pressure.
Leverage ratio 11.99% vs 3.50% requirement; LCR 139.43%; NSFR 146.15%.
demand_pricing: Investment portfolio rose to about 22% of the balance sheet, yielding about 7% vs about 10.3% on advances, which weighed on margin mix.
Repo cut passthrough is automatic at each loan's quarterly reset; the 25 bps repo move flows to the 5.5% benchmark over about three months.
Refinance of about INR1,000 crore taken from SIDBI at 7-7.5% during the quarter.
Bulk deposits are 19% of total deposits; the bulk share of the INR7,570 crore incremental term deposits was not disclosed on the call.
Management sees no material oil-price impact so far on export credit or MSME books; drought risk is being monitored through daily gold LTV tracking.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank sustain high growth and how is the oil price affecting it?

543597|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 18% to INR823 crore and EBITDA reached about INR86 crore (10.4% margin), with Q4 revenue at about INR317 crore.

Q4 revenue was about INR317 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier. Management is guiding to a 35-40% revenue CAGR over three to five years and is expanding capacity in EMS, AC, refrigeration and compressors, with the new compressor line in commercial production since January 2026.

segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue; running at 70-80% utilisation through the year. Capacity to rise from 4 lakh CPH to 8 lakh (phase 1, by about end-August 2026) and 12 lakh (phase 2, by FY-end).

EBITDA margin for FY27 guided at 9-10%, described as 'closer to double digits'; management called 12% a wishful number.
PAT margin expected to improve by 50-100 bps over the next two years as Ind AS adjustments fade.

RAC utilisation target of 60-65% and volume growth of about 30-40% in FY27.

543599|2026-09.headline: Ksolves Q2 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores on client ramp-downs; EBITDA margin 25.7%, within guided band.
543599|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 37.8 crores, down 4.7% YoY and 8.8% QoQ, driven by client-specific ramp-downs at a couple of large enterprise accounts and cautious client spending. EBITDA was INR 9.7 crores at a 25.7% margin (vs 30.3% in Q1 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26), which management attributed to lower revenue partly offset by cost actions and AI-led productivity. PAT was INR 7.25 crores (19.2% margin), and H1 revenue grew 2.5% YoY to INR 79.2 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue to trail FY26 and EBITDA margin to stay within 25-30%, with H2 focus on pipeline building, AI opportunities and enterprise account recovery.

financial_highlights.change: vs 30.3% in Q1 FY27 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26
broadly in line with H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1 per share second interim; H1 total INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core business at 98.4% of Q2 revenue. Geography: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%; overseas 80%.

segments.name: BFSI / banking
segments.commentary: Three Q2 wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe). BFSI share of revenue rose from 7% to 8% (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY27 per analyst slide); management says the jump comes from H2. Company has about 11-12 BFSI clients.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 25% of revenue this year vs 27% last year per analyst reading of slides; one telecom client that was closing its business is now re-engaging.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; company did not reaffirm earlier guidance.
EBITDA margin expected within the 25%-30% guided range for FY27, with scope for improvement in Q4 as recent wins ramp up; management said margins would be at the upper end if sales traction holds.
Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions expected from end of Q3.
Management said it is optimistic about returning to growth in FY28, with a 20%-plus growth aspiration conditional on geopolitical stability.
Dividend to be decided each year based on profitability and cash needs; shareholder returns remain a priority.
capex_capacity: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495; hiring in FY27 limited to 5-10% of last year's level, and capacity is to be filled from the existing team before new hiring.
AI productivity: management says one person can now deliver 2x-3x prior output.

Built a low-code/no-code agent platform for a telecom client used by 500+ operations staff; migrated a US client's legacy codebase with 8 agents in about 7-8 months versus an estimated 1-1.5 years manually.
Opened a sales office in Australia for local bids; delivery team is based in India.
Being a Select Partner in Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks; 100% of engineers Claude certified.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective and discretionary spend under scrutiny; management said clients had put decisions on hold until around 10 September over AI wait-and-watch, and are now returning with AI-led requirements.
Customers now ask for Odoo, Salesforce or data engineering with agentic AI; management says the sales question has shifted from headcount to business outcome.
Two large enterprise accounts ramped down; management called these client-specific, not structural, and said the pipeline was not deep enough to offset them in the quarter.
Management said some clients tested building in-house AI tools but have since returned to outsourcing projects for features.
Top 10 clients contributed 50% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends continue at around 100% of PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder returns remain a priority; the Board will decide each payout based on yearly profitability and cash needs. H1 interim dividend totalled INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT).

qa_highlights.question: Do you have constant-currency numbers given rupee weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company is not currently calculating revenue in constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the two clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it was large enough to be a big hit; new Q1 and Q2 wins absorbed much of it, though a deficit remained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the margin move with sales traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be at the upper end of the guided range if revenue recovers; the INR 3.6 crore revenue drop was the main driver of the Q2 margin dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the banking wins contribute meaningfully, and how big can BFSI become?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are underway and take months to quarters; the South American bank relationship is ongoing but expansion is not in writing. Management hopes other banks will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Are you entering cybersecurity?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploring; management sees AI guardrails and security as a demand opportunity but has not defined the offering.

risks_watch: Revenue trend: FY27 guided soft, with dependence on recovery at re-engaged accounts and on H2 BFSI wins converting into revenue.
Margin: Q2 margin fell to 25.7% from 30.3% in Q1; watch whether cost actions hold the 25-30% band as revenue recovers.
Client concentration: top 10 clients are 50% of revenue, and two large accounts ramped down in Q2.
Currency: management does not track constant-currency revenue despite a weaker rupee, so FX effect on reported numbers is not visible.
Management did not reaffirm prior guidance; new cybersecurity vertical is still undefined.
543599|2026-09.management_tone: Candid but guarded: management called the quarter mixed and attributed the decline to client-specific ramp-downs, while staying confident about AI wins and a FY28 recovery. Answers on FY28 growth and client-level revenue were conditional or unquantified, and the company declined to give lost-revenue figures.
key_quotes: These are client -specific ramp -down, not a structural change in our business or our client relationship.
So simply put, this was a revenue -led dip.
We are now building a pipeline, even a strong pipeline enough that no client-specific decision can move our quarter the way this one did.
Ksolves is putting agentic AI into production for paying clients, not just running pilots.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495 and FY27 hiring is limited to 5-10% of last year's level, with existing team to be used first; no new plant, line or office capacity was guided beyond a sales office in Australia.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to trail FY26 after Q2 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores, with two large enterprise accounts ramped down and the pipeline not deep enough to offset them; H1 growth of only 2.5% YoY is fading.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Headcount is being cut and hiring held to 5-10% of last year, with no utilisation figure disclosed and no capex plans discussed, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not reaffirm prior guidance and cut FY27 revenue to trail FY26, so an upgrade is not signalled in the next 2-4 quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management did not reaffirm earlier guidance; FY27 revenue is guided soft and H2 BFSI wins and re-engaged accounts must convert, with top 10 clients at 50% of revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is exploring a cybersecurity vertical (AI guardrails and security) but has not defined the offering, and Odoo, Salesforce and agentic AI offerings are being sold without a stated launch date.

rows.label: BFSI and banking wins ramping
rows.why: Three Q2 banking wins (South America, UK, Europe) are underway but take months to quarters, and the BFSI share is 8% of revenue with about 11-12 BFSI clients; further bank expansion is not in writing.

rows.label: Return to growth in FY28
rows.why: Management is optimistic about FY28 growth with a 20%-plus aspiration, but this is conditional on geopolitical stability and the H2 recovery, and was not quantified.

rows.label: Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions
rows.why: Headcount fell about 10% (550 to 495) and management guided the full-quarter benefit of the Q2 cost actions from end of Q3, supporting margin within the 25-30% band.

tone.note: Management was confident about AI wins, the BFSI pipeline and a FY28 recovery, but cautious on FY27 revenue, declined to quantify the lost client revenue, and did not reaffirm prior guidance; analysts pressed on the size of the client losses, constant-currency numbers and dividend payout.

543600|2026-03.headline: Harsha Engineers Q4 FY26 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore; FY26 Engineering revenue INR1,444 crore, guided to double-digit FY27 growth.
543600|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated Engineering revenue of INR382 crore and EBITDA of INR77 crore, versus adjusted EBITDA of INR64.3 crore in Q3 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25. For FY26, Engineering revenue grew to INR1,444 crore from INR1,269 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR264 crore (about INR270 crore adjusted for the new Labour Code impact). Solar revenue was INR183 crore with PAT of INR10.2 crore. Management guided to double-digit FY27 consolidated growth, with India Engineering in the mid-teens, and to maintaining current margins. The call also covered weak Romania profitability, the Advantek ramp-up, and the China steel-cage expansion.

financial_highlights.change: Engineering revenue growth of about 15.7% YoY excluding Solar; consolidated growth of about 27% including Solar
vs adjusted INR64.3 crore in Q3 FY26 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR264 crore reported; about INR270 crore adjusted for Labour Code impact

financial_highlights.change: PAT INR10.2 crore vs adjusted PAT INR5 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: Positive EBITDA INR4 crore; combined loss INR11.4 crore (management also cited INR11.5 crore)
Turnover about INR120 crore; PAT about INR5 crore profit; EBITDA about 11%
Turnover about INR247 crore; PAT loss about INR14 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR9 crore (management correction from INR11 crore); prior year INR14 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs 134 days in previous quarter and 127 days in previous year

financial_highlights.value: INR120 crore consolidated; about INR20 crore in Q4

segments.name: Bearing cages (India Engineering)
segments.commentary: India-to-India cage business grew about 11% in FY26 per management. Large-size cages grew about 14% to about INR49 crore, with mid-teens to 15-20% growth expected.

segments.name: Bushings
segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crore in FY26, up about 25%, driven by design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes from bearings to bushings. Management targets 25-30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR60 crore. Growth drivers are AC compressor components and white goods. Management expects at least 20% growth next year and 15-20% mid-term.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR183 crore with PAT INR10.2 crore. Q4 revenue about INR91 crore, roughly doubled YoY. Management expects more than 25% growth and Solar EBITDA margin to hold near the FY26 level.

segments.name: Advantek (India, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still at low utilisation; FY26 EBITDA INR4 crore but net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest. Sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; current installed capacity seen generating INR250-300 crore turnover.

segments.name: China subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR120 crore, PAT about INR5 crore profit. Brownfield steel-cage expansion to be commissioned in H2 FY28; INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Romania subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Cage share of mix at about 22%, targeted to rise to 30-35%. Wind market in Europe not yet recovered.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected to be double-digit, with India Engineering in the mid-teens; India growth described as high-teens to mid-teens in the Q&A.
Management expects to at least maintain current margin profile in FY27, with an aim to improve it.
Over 2-3 years, management expects consolidated EBITDA to rise 100-200 basis points; India Engineering EBITDA has been consistently about 20%.
Maintenance capex in India of INR30-40 crore in FY27 and a similar amount in FY28; China expansion capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.
Advantek subsidiary expected to reach peak with current installed capacity in about two years; a second-phase capex plan is to be finalised in the next few weeks, with work starting this year.
Management indicated the India-level business could reach INR2,400-2,500 crore and consolidated INR2,700-3,000 crore on current capabilities, depending on capacity additions.
capex_capacity: Harsha has three facilities in India (the third, at Bhayla, commissioned in FY26), one in Romania and one in China.

Advantek is in its first year of operations and running at low utilisation; its sales are expected to grow at least 3x in FY27. Second-phase Advantek capex is being firmed up for additional capacity in key growth verticals.
China brownfield steel-cage expansion has begun; it will add steel cages to a predominantly brass-based portfolio, with commissioning in H2 FY28.
Management said the Advantek capex includes infrastructure that will not translate immediately into fixed-asset-to-revenue multiples.
Saket Kapoor noted PP&E closing balance of about INR615 crore.
demand_pricing: Export growth of about 17% in FY26 was attributed to improving European and US industrial markets; US import tariff on cages was cut to zero, aiding US picks-up.

Pass-through of raw-material costs (steel, brass, metal prices) to customers is contractual, with an average lag of about four months. Q4 growth was mainly volume-driven, as metal prices moved mainly from late December to February/March.

Europe demand is improving slowly, but management said there is no definitive recovery and that cost and pricing issues remain. Europe is about 30% of sales, China just over 10%, US 6-7% and Japan about 2%.
Domestic bearing makers are ramping capacity and are expected to invest further; management is bullish, though it flagged risks from the war and petroleum prices.
Cost pressure is building from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; logistics has not been impacted so far. Management is working to mitigate or pass through these costs.
Management said wallet share is about 70-90% in India but only 10-20% with large overseas customers and 2-3% with the Japan-based customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from pricing versus volume, and was commodity inflation fully passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% consolidated growth was mainly Solar; Engineering grew 15.7% YoY. Growth was mostly volume-led, and pass-through is automatic with an average lag of about four months.

qa_highlights.question: What were the absolute FY26 revenue and PBT figures for the China and Romania subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: China: turnover about INR120 crore with PAT about INR5 crore profit. Romania: turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Combined subsidiary loss was INR9 crore after correction; management said losses would reduce significantly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Europe demand and restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is slowly improving, with no sharp recovery. Restructuring is ongoing, the cost structure is not yet right, and Romania still has negative margins. Management is evaluating how long it can sustain these margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: India maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore per year; China expansion INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28; further Advantek phase-two capex is being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is Advantek's ramp-up timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current installed capacity expected to peak in about two years, with turnover of INR250-300 crore. Expansion beyond that is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What drives bushing growth and what is the stamping outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth comes from design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes away from bearings. Stampings (about INR60 crore in FY26) are driven by AC compressor and white goods components; management expects at least 20% growth next year.

risks_watch: Europe recovery is slow and unconfirmed; management has no clear customer read on demand, and Romania still runs negative EBITDA with restructuring incomplete.
Input cost pressure from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; pass-through lags about four months, so near-term margins could be squeezed.
Advantek: low utilisation, FY26 net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest; second-phase capex plan to be finalised in the next few weeks and its size not yet disclosed.
Subsidiary loss figures were corrected on the call (INR9 crore vs INR11 crore, Advantek INR11.4 crore vs INR11.5 crore); verify against the annual report.
Geographic mix and Solar growth (about 100% in Q4) drove the headline 27% growth; track Engineering-only growth (15.7%) against the mid-teens FY27 guidance.
Macro risks flagged by management: the war and petroleum prices could affect domestic bearing-maker demand in the short term.
key_quotes: And on your questions for the pass -through mechanism, yes, it is very well-established pass-through mechanism with the customer.
So, we are very bullish. There could be impact of, you know, current war and petroleum prices and all that.
So, last whole year, we are seeing demand has slowly improved over the year.
We are continuing to face massive inflationary pressure in Europe, which is also adding to this whole challenge.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
543600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

financial_highlights.change: +10% QoQ vs Rs 382 crore; +21% YoY vs Rs 349 crore
-9% QoQ vs Rs 77 crore; +7% YoY vs Rs 65.3 crore
Positive EBITDA of Rs 2.82 crore; down QoQ (Q4 seasonally strong)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 19 crore (per CFO) / Rs 90 crore (per CEO)
financial_highlights.change: Figures inconsistent in call; CEO cited +31% YoY

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 10 crore last year (per management)

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ; EBITDA and PAT up YoY but margin down QoQ on material pass-through lag and FX loss. Management guides high-teens India growth for FY27.

segments.name: Harsha Advantek (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales about Rs 30 crore (+7% QoQ), EBITDA margin about 9%. FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus vs Rs 43 crore in FY26; expected PAT positive by end-FY27.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore, EBITDA Rs 2.82 crore; management guides about Rs 200 crore FY27 revenue at 7-8% EBITDA margin, project-driven and seasonal.

segments.commentary: Q1 sales only about Rs 10 crore on capacity ramp-up constraints at new facility; management still targets about 50% growth on FY26 base of Rs 49 crore (the call also cites about 30%, so the target is unclear).

Management estimated the raw material increase would lift prices by about 3-4% (CFO said 40-50% of a 6-7% increase), though the CEO declined to quantify the price impact.
Top 10 customers about 80% of revenue; top customers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken, NBC, ZF, Flender) rank in a shifting order; management claims 80-90% wallet share with major Indian customers.

qa_highlights.question: Was the growth broad-based across segments, and was it driven by Europe or India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was broad-based, with industrial demand strengthening in India and European demand recovering. It called 20% FY27 consolidated growth a very tough stretch and expects mid-to-high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth.

qa_highlights.question: Which raw materials drove the cost increase, and how is foreign EBITDA margin trending?

qa_highlights.question: How large are the Romania losses, and is the subsidiary restructuring on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Romania did not significantly improve ex-FX and copper prices hurt results. Sanjay Majmudar guided combined China and Romania loss of about Rs 2-3 crore for FY27 versus about Rs 10 crore last year, with Romania possibly profitable next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are bushing and stamping growth sustainable, and is large-cage growth credible after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth is driven by conversion and wallet share, with conversion expected to support growth for at least a couple of years. Stamping growth comes from new products maturing over about one year. Large-cage Q1 was about Rs 10 crore due to ramp-up constraints at the new facility, and management still expects about 30-50% growth, citing order book and pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CapEx outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Bhayla status?
qa_highlights.answer: China Phase-2 is on track for Q3 FY28 commissioning. Bhayla building construction was delayed by heavy rain and expected to start this month, with the third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27. Annual CapEx is guided at Rs 50-80 crore, with Rs 180-200 crore over 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India growth is volume versus price, and what price increase is being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is the focus and the price impact is not being predicted. Maulik Jasani estimated the 6-7% RM increase would lift selling prices by about 40-50% of that, roughly 3-4%. The Japanese customer was Rs 21 crore in Q1 versus Rs 16.5 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Advantek EBITDA and margin expectations, and what is the normal India Engineering margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Advantek Q1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and it is expected to be slightly below the India blended margin in FY27, matching it from FY28. Vishal Rangwala said the 24% Q1 standalone margin is high and a normal sustainable margin is 20-22%. Jason Soans's question on the 22-24% guidance was answered by Maulik Jasani, who said margin percentage will fall as pass-through lifts realisations.

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag of one to two quarters: Q1 margin compressed on an 8% RM rise, and recovery depends on metal prices stabilising (management had no view on normalisation).
Solar EPC volatility: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore vs a Q4-heavy seasonal pattern; FY27 guide of about Rs 200 crore at 7-8% EBITDA margin.
Romania: still loss-making, one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1, no break-even timeline, and copper prices weighed on results.
Large-size cages: Q1 sales about Rs 10 crore and new facility still ramping; the FY27 growth target is stated as both about 50% and about 30%, so it needs clarification.
Bhayla Phase-2 construction delayed by monsoon rain, and China commissioning slipped to Q3 FY28 with revenue from FY29; watch construction milestones next quarter.
Advantek PAT-positive target by end-FY27, with FY27 sales target of about Rs 140 crore plus against Rs 43 crore in FY26.
key_quotes: As you would have seen on a consolidated basis, we have posted a 25% growth in Quarter 1 and year-over-year
However, there will be a lag of one or two quarters. Thus, we should be able to pass through this cost increase in the subsequent quarter.
I think 20% is a very tough stretch.
So, we expect that absolute value increase will continue, but definitely percentage will reduce because the material pass through will enhance the sales price recovery

It was cautious and often hedged on margins, raw material pass-through, Romania's path to break-even, and the large-cage ramp, and several answers were inconsistent or deferred to later quarters.

543600|2026-09.headline: Harsha Engineers Q2 FY27: consolidated Engineering revenue INR428 crores (+18% YoY) and EBITDA INR81.1 crores; India growth above 24%, Romania being downsized.
543600|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 as business as usual and largely on track, with India Engineering revenue up over 24% YoY and H1 up about 23%. Consolidated Engineering revenue reached INR428 crores versus INR363 crores a year earlier, and consolidated EBITDA margin rose to about 18.6%, helped by metal pass-through, lower solar mix and operational efficiency. Management reaffirmed full-year FY27 guidance of mid-to-high teens India growth and 10-12% consolidated growth, but stressed it is conservative given metal-price inflation and a planned Romania downsizing. Romania downsizing details, capex timing and Advantek losses remained open items for next quarter.

vs INR63 crores YoY and INR69.8 crores QoQ
vs 15.9% in previous quarter (as cited in Q&A)
Q2 consolidated, as cited in Q&A

segments.commentary: Management expects about 30% growth in FY27, driven by windmill gearbox customers, with a long-term target of about INR300 crores in three to four years. One new-contract commercialisation is seen as slightly delayed but still expected.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: Expects over 30% growth in FY27 versus about INR72 crores in FY26, with the accumulator product launched recently; long-term target about INR300 crores over four years. Management said it may bring forward the INR150-200 crore run-rate milestone.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR11.9 crores and EBITDA INR0.73 crores. FY27 and FY28 guidance is INR150-200 crores, dependent on government import and subsidy norms, which are viewed as cyclical.

segments.name: China
segments.commentary: Sequentially softer versus Q1 but up YoY; current-portfolio growth estimated at 5-7%, with EBITDA margin in single digits. New capacity targeted for Q2-Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Romania
segments.commentary: Management is downsizing operations and cutting costs, aiming to arrest operating losses by end FY27. FY28 revenue expected to be lower but still positive for profitability; details to come in about one quarter.

segments.commentary: H1 FY27 loss about INR7 crores versus about INR12 crores a year earlier. FY27 revenue guidance INR140 crores or slightly higher; H2 expected to be profit positive. Standalone-to-consolidated gap is about INR12 crores loss, with foreign subsidiaries' Q2 loss INR1.7 crores.

Resourcing/outsourcing project: commercial sales to begin in Q3 and normalise by Q4 FY27, with peak run-rate about INR70-75 crores per year; a further INR75-100 crores of Cage opportunities from Europe and North America in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Romania: will operating profitability convert into net profit, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to confirm net profitability; it is working on cost structure and will update quarterly. Details of downsizing were deferred to about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18.6% margin driven by pass-through or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both: some metal pass-through, lower solar contribution, and operational efficiency. India margin was seen as steady around 22%, with consolidated margin of 17-18% for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 consolidated guidance only 10-12% after 21% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited metal inflation, quantitative growth of 12-15%, and Romania downsizing reducing contribution. India guidance is conservative, not an implied slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and split between Advantek and China?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India capex is about INR110 crores over 1-1.5 years and China about INR100 crores; about INR70 crores spent in H1. Completion targeted by June 2027 with go-live later.

qa_highlights.question: Advantek peak interest and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined interest and depreciation around INR7.5-8 crores currently, rising to a maximum of about INR10 crores once fully running; Advantek capex loan about INR250 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bushing contract delayed and what about large windmills?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bushing contract commercialisation is slightly delayed but still expected. It is supplying Bushings to a 16 MW windmill application and sees a continued opportunity.

543619|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore with PAT INR 42.7 crore and executable order book of about INR 697 crore, 3.3x FY26 revenue.
543619|2026-03.overview: Management (Joint MD Gaurav Lath) framed Concord as evolving from a railway equipment maker into a full-stack railway technology and lifecycle platform, built on four pillars: green mobility, smart locomotive intelligence, railway safety (Kavach/MSDAC), and AI-driven diagnostics. FY26 figures stated were revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore, PAT INR 42.7 crore, EBITDA INR 62.1 crore, and an executable order book of about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026. Working capital was the main analyst concern: receivables and short-term debt rose sharply, which management attributed to back-ended railway billing in Q4 and said will persist through the growth phase. Several questions on Fusion Electronics revenue, Kavach tender outcomes and loco-Kavach opportunity size got non-committal answers.

segments.commentary: Acquired last year; management called it a turnaround with no meaningful revenue yet. At full scale it can do about INR 200 crore revenue on installed capacity, with capacity doubling planned. Management expects the first revenue-contributing year in the current year.

segments.name: Locomotive solutions
segments.commentary: Management said locomotive solutions are currently the larger contributor to growth, including DPWCS (distributed power wireless control systems). No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota)
segments.commentary: Field trials started; management hopes for a successful year. Trial completion and ISA approval are targeted within FY27. Kavach pillar is positioned as large and long-duration, with no revenue figure given.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Demonstrated India's first indigenous zero-emission diesel-to-battery locomotive retrofit. Also cited a recent NTPC order, with no value disclosed.

Management said it has been frugal on investment and will consider raising its Progota stake when returns justify it; no decision announced.
Field-level in-house engineering team on locomotives reportedly gives execution efficiency for loco Kavach installation.
demand_pricing: Executable order book about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026, about 3.3x FY26 revenue.
Management described an unprecedented order book; no split by product or customer was given.
Kavach: a tender for about 4,500 loco units closed 14 April 2026 with no outcome yet. Management said tender finalisation takes time and Concord has quoted several tenders.
Management did not confirm the analyst's figure of about 17,000 loco units tendered; it said the total loco population is 13,000 to 16,000 including train sets and MEMUs.
No direct response on whether the LNG and geopolitical crisis could slow railway spending, beyond general references to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise sharply, and will this working capital pattern continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to back-ended Q4 billing and customer acceptance cycles with railways. Said receivable cycles had improved by June versus last year, and confirmed similar working capital will recur.

qa_highlights.question: How should debt and balance sheet strength be seen over the next few years, given short-term debt rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is always heavier and working capital will spike with the INR 697 crore order book, then ease. It declined to give peak debt estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% to 25% EBITDA guidance conservative given around 30% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for realistic guidance and that technology adoption is faster than expected, without accepting the conservatism framing.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and is there any liquidity challenge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said railway payments are streamlined and sovereign-backed with no penalty or bad-debt risk, and that cash flow will not deter growth. Confirmed that some money started coming in from April, but gave no timeline for positive operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company face penalties for delayed order execution, and will it grow execution faster than 40% to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company executed similar growth last year and planned more structured execution for the large order book. No penalty figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can Fusion Electronics deliver this year, and why has it shown little revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a turnaround with a typical 300-day integration cycle and said full-scale revenue could be about INR 200 crore. It expects revenue contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will Kavach orders be executed, and when will the 4,500-unit loco Kavach tender be decided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kavach orders have two to three phases (production, inspection, installation), with part of the invoice paid on delivery and the balance after installation. The tender outcome timing was not given; it said finalisation is a process.

543619|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose ~95% YoY to ~INR 159 crore, EBITDA ~INR 46.7 crore at 29.3% margin, unexecuted order book INR 846 crore.
543619|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ~INR 159 crore (up ~95% YoY), EBITDA of INR 46.7 crore (up ~110%) and PAT of INR 31.2 crore (up ~95%), with a 29.3% EBITDA margin. Debtor days fell from 210 to 178 and inventory days from 313 to 259 over six months. Management said the unexecuted order book stood at INR 846 crore as of 30 September 2026, against an opening INR 697 crore, and targeted a 40-50% revenue CAGR over three to five years. Key uncertainties remained on Kavach approved-vendor status, which is still in trials with no timeline given, and on the main board migration, which is awaiting eligibility.

financial_highlights.change: down from 210 days in six months
opening FY27 INR 697 crore; H1 inflow INR 308 crore

segments.name: Locomotive subsystems (ex-Advanced Rail, now merged)
segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of current revenue and about 80% of the future order book (excluding Kavach) come from locomotive subsystems and green mobility. Advanced Rail is now a single unit with Concord.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota associate, 46.5% stake)
segments.commentary: Progota is an associate, so only profit share is booked, not revenue consolidation. Management said Kavach is still in trials for approved-vendor status; no timeline given. Shareholder query on Kavach segment revenue was deferred to the IR team.

segments.name: Fusion (PCB / EMS, acquired)
segments.commentary: Backward integration into PCB, PCB assembly and SMT EMS has started. Management expects around INR 400 crore revenue at full scale; plant described as production ready, and first revenue hoped for in FY27.

segments.name: Green mobility / propulsion
segments.commentary: One battery locomotive delivered and running for over 12 months. A green hydrogen propulsion order is to be executed next year, and a 3100 HP hydrogen loco is in development. IGBT propulsion is in development.

H2 has historically been about 60% of the year's revenue versus 40% in H1; management expects the same pattern in FY27 and ex-Kavach growth of similar magnitude next year.
International markets expected to contribute one-fourth to one-half of revenue over three to five years; a few orders of a few million dollars possible in the current or next year.

Q4 FY26 revenue was INR794 crore (up 100% YoY), with EBITDA INR111 crore and PAT INR70 crore, though management said utility-scale dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter. Management is building a 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line and 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant at Narmadapuram, with cell COD targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27 and frames in Q1 FY27.

543626|2026-03.headline: Electronics Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR1,913 crores and SSSG hit 12.2%, with EBITDA margin up to 6.7%.

Same-store sales growth was 12.2% in the quarter, helped by GST rate cuts, festive demand and mobile launches, while FY26 SSSG was 5.3%. FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR7,183 crores with EBITDA of INR438 crores (6.1% margin) and PAT of INR107 crores. North cluster margin to be 3-4% higher than now by FY28 (not stated as an exact level).

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hyderabad SSSG double-digit in Q4 and how should FY27 be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the GST cut benefit across categories (TVs, washing machines, dishwashers, refrigerators, cooling products) plus mobile launches; early Q1 trends were good.

qa_highlights.question: How did gross margin hold up as large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins were supported by higher-margin categories (mobile accessories, built-in appliances, audio) and better throughput; management expects margins to hold or improve.

qa_highlights.question: Store opening cadence and cash flow deployment?

qa_highlights.question: Delhi/NCR margin path?

qa_highlights.question: Franchise model?

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Kolkata while NCR is still stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Delhi stabilisation is done and growth will be organic; Kolkata is a new cluster with a 12-14 month learning cycle, starting with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.

Working capital days fell to 42 from 73 and working capital borrowings dropped to INR 97 crore from INR 658 crore at the start of the quarter. segments.commentary: Revenue +29% YoY with record EBITDA margin of 4.9%. Management said North market for cooling products was negative versus 2024.

543638|2026-03.headline: Tracxn Q4 FY26 revenue from operations Rs 20.5 crore; EBITDA negative Rs 6.6 crore, PAT marginally negative Rs 0.6 crore, adjusted PAT positive Rs 2.5 crore.
543638|2026-03.overview: Tracxn reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 20.5 crore, with EBITDA negative at Rs 6.6 crore and PAT marginally negative at Rs 0.6 crore after non-cash ESOP charges. Management said FY26 revenue was Rs 84 crore and that Q4 volume growth accelerated, with paid customers rising 19% YoY to 2,289. Management described the deal environment as weak in deal volume (near a 10-year low) while M&A and IB activity was rebounding, and it is adding GTM headcount and AI distribution channels for FY27. Blended ASP per account fell, driven mainly by mix shift toward lower-priced accounts rather than price cuts.

543652|2026-09.headline: Fusion Finance Q2 FY27 net profit rose to INR86 crores and annualised ROA hit about 4%, while AUM growth guidance is being moderated.
543652|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 disbursements were INR1,726 crores, up 33% YoY but broadly flat QoQ, and AUM reached INR8,007 crores (+14% YoY) after floods disrupted July and August collections in five states. Gross NPA fell to 1.6% from 2.51% QoQ (2.28% including the INR54 crore ARC sale), and profit after tax reached INR86 crores versus a loss of INR22 crores a year earlier. Cost of borrowing fell for a fifth straight quarter, with marginal cost at 9.35%, and NII margin rose to 12.52%. Management said the INR10,000 crore AUM ambition will likely slip given the H1 disruption, while credit cost and ROA targets are unchanged.

segments.name: Core JLG microfinance
segments.commentary: Remains the majority of the business; average MFI AUM per branch rose to INR5.4 crores from INR5.1 crores, with about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned.

segments.name: Premium JLG (income above INR3 lakhs)
segments.commentary: Vishwas product launched in Q2 accounted for about 20% of MFI disbursements in September and October; ticket size capped at INR1 lakh, and loans are reported as MFI JLG under bureau rules.

segments.name: Secured MSME
segments.commentary: About 10% of MSME disbursements now originate through MFI branches, with MFI branches acting as MSME spokes expanded from 50 to 100; MSME disbursements grew about 10% QoQ in October, with MSME ticket size cap raised to INR50 lakhs from INR25 lakhs.

segments.name: Maharashtra (about INR117 crore book)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency fell to 98.84% in October from 99.4%; net flow rate 0.57%, with the drought-affected sub-book of about INR26-27 crores at about 97.25% collection efficiency.

segments.name: Karnataka (about 1.25% of portfolio)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency 99.95% in October with negative net flow rate; management reports no stress in the market.

guidance_outlook: AUM ambition of INR10,000 crores is still a medium-term objective, but management said it may moderate and arrive later; no new year-end AUM number given.
Credit cost guided at 2% to 2.5% for the year: about 1.8% base (flows of about 15-16 bps per quarter) plus about 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs.
Exit-quarter ROA target of 4% has already been achieved (annualised ~4% in Q2); medium-term ROA target is 4%+.
Management expects at least 15-20 bps NIM expansion next quarter and sustained margins thereafter; a further 12-15 bps per quarter of yield uplift is expected over the next two quarters.
Q3 disbursement momentum: October up about 10% over the prior-quarter monthly average (INR568-570 crores), across both MFI and MSME.
Medium-term AUM growth ambition of 20-25% per year, with a calibrated timeline for the INR10,000 crore target.
Management expects a possible 50-75 bps rise in marginal cost of borrowing over the next two quarters, which it says would have a muted impact; rate pass-through is 6-9 months away if needed.
Retention of repeat customers rose to 38-39% from 28-29%; target is 50% over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: MFI branch network: 950 branches now run on-ground credit assessment, up from about 200 branches.
Branch footprint: about 102 branches being rationalised and 50 new branches planned in markets with strong opportunity.

New LOS and LMS systems live in about 15% of branches, with broader transition targeted before financial year-end; AI capabilities in development for collections, customer service and credit assessment.
Recovery of 90+ DPD legacy portfolio brought in-house; recoveries exceeded INR30 crores in Q2, including INR21 crores from written-off accounts.
demand_pricing: Collection efficiency returned to 99.75% in Q2 with net flow rate below 0.10%; October gross collection efficiency 99.78% (September 99.77%).
Disbursements in October up about 10% over the prior quarter's monthly average of INR568-570 crores, with MFI and MSME each growing about 10%.
Yield rose about 24 bps QoQ from the rate hike taken at the start of FY27; cost of borrowing fell about 35 bps QoQ.
PTC raised INR320 crores at an all-in cost of about 8.5%, now about 10% of borrowings; management aims to raise the PTC share further.
CGSMFI2.0 scheme: accepted about INR468 crores of sanctions at about 9.23% all-in cost out of about INR1,100 crores available; the company declined sanctions with unfavourable terms.
Delinquent receivables on direct assignment fell to 12.65% of AUM from 13.75% QoQ; the company aims to reduce direct assignment reliance.

qa_highlights.question: What were October collection efficiency and disbursement numbers, including for Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross collection efficiency was 99.78% in October (September 99.77%). Maharashtra's INR117 crore book fell to 98.84% (from 99.4%) with a 0.57% net flow rate; Karnataka was at 99.95% with negative net flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company accelerate growth in H2 or wait for drought-affected areas to stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has moved almost all of Maharashtra and some bordering Karnataka branches to stricter guardrails with no new customers there, and is pressing growth elsewhere. Maharashtra is about 2% and Karnataka about 1.25% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress building in districts from rainfall deficit or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no carry-over of stress from September or October into the next month outside Maharashtra. The premium JLG product carries a 0.19% par in the third cycle and above over the past 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrower count falling and what is retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 4% of customers hold more than three lenders and will be exited. Repeat-loan retention rose from 28-29% to 38-39% since August, with a target of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 credit cost guidance and how much H1 profit is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 2% to 2.5% for the year, with a base of about 1.8% and a further 30 bps per quarter if a shock occurs. Management said INR86.47 crores of profit is recurring with no exceptional items; net credit cost is about 1.2% annualised after recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise, and will rates be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 15-20 bps margin rise next quarter from yield and PTC-driven borrowing cost benefits, and sees a further 12-15 bps per quarter yield uplift. Any pass-through of rate increases is 6-9 months away and not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company give a year-end AUM number and a higher exit ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a new year-end AUM figure, citing many moving parts and a likely moderation of the INR10,000 crore target. It said the company enters November with no carry-over of stress and expects growth from individual loans, premium JLG and MSME.

risks_watch: Maharashtra drought: 60% of drought impact not yet seen per management; sub-book at 97.25% collection efficiency, with stricter guardrails and no new customers in the affected areas.
AUM growth: the INR10,000 crore target may slip; growth in the next 4-5 months depends on October's 10% momentum continuing.
Cost of funds: management expects 50-75 bps of rate increase over two quarters, and margin guidance depends on PTC share rising and the CGSMFI2.0 benefit.
Credit cost: 2-2.5% guidance includes a 30 bps per quarter shock allowance; the ARC sale of INR54 crores lifted Stage 3 coverage to 93.4%.
Premium JLG and MSME: higher-ticket products are a new risk; loans above INR3 lakhs income are non-qualified but reported as MFI JLG.
Tax: unrecognised DTA of INR271 crores as of September 30 could be used in future.

543653|2026-03.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.
543653|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 top-line growth of close to 18%, with revenue from operations around INR720 crores, EBITDA about INR88 crores (roughly 12.2% margin) and PAT about INR56 crores. For FY26, revenue was about INR2,994 crores on 9.5% volume growth, with consolidated gross margin of 35.1% and EBITDA margin of 13.7%, up over 120 bps. Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

segments.commentary: Family pack grew about 20% in Q4 and impulse about 14%. Family pack price was raised and impulse grammage cut.

segments.commentary: Bikaji brand revenue crossed INR100 crores in FY26, with a target of 50-60% growth annually for 2-3 years.

Consolidated gross margin target is to maintain FY26 level (35.1%) in FY27; EBITDA expected to improve through fixed-cost leverage and CMU (co-manufacturing) output.

New warehouse adjacent to the plant: trials began about two weeks before the call, full operations from about 15 June 2026; storage rises from under 2 days of finished goods to 6-8 days.

Production shift from Bikaner to co-manufacturing units (CMU) expected to add operational efficiency in FY27.
Sweets capacity at 100%+ utilisation in festive months but very low utilisation off-season.
demand_pricing: Price rise of about 3% taken in April 2026; management said it is enough to offset current raw material and packaging inflation and will decide on further hikes depending on the war.
Edible oil costs up about 12-14%; packaging material up about 25-30% at peak, then eased to INR220-225 from INR260-270 per unit cited.
Pulses and flour prices have not seen major increases.
Post-April demand momentum reported as continuing with no slowdown despite the price pass-through.

Bengal election-related migration of workers and a 2.5-day factory shutdown after the Chairman's death cost about 4-4.5 days of production in Q4 and Q1 to date; management said sales were partly lost but demand was not.
Delhi market underperforming; UP growing upwards of 20%, and UP's TAM equals the other five focus states combined.
Management expects regional and local brands to exit under GST rationalisation, with benefits to organised players over 2-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall to about 11% from about 13.5-14% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to advertising, which was about 3.2-3.3% of sales in Q3/Q4 versus about 1% in H1, plus about 50 bps of one-time doubtful-debt provisions in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between consolidated growth of 19% and standalone growth of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is mainly THF retail, worth about 2.2 percentage points of growth, with Bikaji USA and Ariba also contributing; management confirmed there is no inorganic contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sweets growth constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Sweets is capacity-constrained in festive months and under-utilised off-season; a new Bikaner factory and small all-season SKUs at INR5-10 are planned, with FY27 sweets budgeted at about 12.5% growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Current direct reach is 3.5 lakh outlets; the next 1.5 lakh are expected mainly from focus states, with core states moving toward direct distribution rather than wholesalers.

qa_highlights.answer: Western snacks grew about 8.5% in Q4 after 25% in Q3; management attributed it to weaker family-pack traction and a soft category, and expects 20%+ growth going forward from a base of 1.1% national share.

543653|2026-09.headline: Bikaji Q2 FY27 top line grew close to 13% as Diwali shifted to Q3; management guides FY27 growth to about 17% and Q4 EBITDA to 13.5%.
543653|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew close to 13% in Q2 FY27, but the quarter was distorted by Diwali and sweets/gifting shifting into Q3 (October). Snacking carried the quarter, with value growth of about 22% and volume growth of about 15%, while total volume growth was about 5%. Gross margin was 34.4% in Q2, with standalone gross margin hit by about 1.7% from raw material inflation (pulses, edible oil, packaging, diesel), and consolidated EBITDA was about 12.6% in H1. Management says a roughly 3% MRP price increase takes effect from around 15 November, with full price impact in Q4, and expects Q3 to be margin-pressured and Q4 to normalise.

543654|2026-03.headline: Medanta FY26 total income rose 20% to INR 45,089 million and Q4 set a record, with Noida losses narrowing to INR 236 million in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was bromine volume 4,175 tons vs ~4,500 implied by 55 tpd run rate, and is the 20,000-ton FY27 target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 325 tons short: about 200 tons lost to grid power cuts (3-3.5 days) and about 150 tons to planned shutdowns; exit run rate of 20,000-25,000 tons still the target, with Q2 and Q3 the real test.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for bromine realisations over next 3-4 quarters given contract structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident of holding the weighted average blend; long-term contracts are 60-70% of volume, spot 30-35%, and some spot impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Salt shipments shortfall and whether demand or logistics is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has not moved backwards; the shortfall reflects QVC deferrals and logistics issues including vessel slots and cut-offs; Kandla added as third port from Q2 to reduce blank sailings.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving if diesel and routes normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide numerically; said other expenses rose about INR40 crore YoY, ~60% from logistics (mainly distance) and ~40% from diesel, with normalisation expected to reflect from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why are derivative prices up only ~10% vs bromine ~25%, and status of Gujarat lease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the numbers quoted were not accurate, bromine is 40-50% of derivative cost so pass-through is fractional; lease closure expected in coming months, rents being paid and accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for zinc bromide and off-grid scale-up, and SiCSem timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-grid pilot needs several months to prove out; megawatt-plus plants in India not timed. SiCSem 24-27 months to commercial SOP from FSA; construction from late Aug/early Sep 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why has bromine volume been flat for five years versus capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited structural changes in brine feedstock needing recovery-system redesign, plus cyclonic rainfall in Kutch (average rainfall up to ~900 mm); 40,000-ton expansion timed to FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for oilfield chemicals and timing of volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian drilling demand is small and most demand is overseas; pack and starch (Nagri) volumes expected H2 FY27, bentonite and barite (Mandvi) by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Semicon capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Kumar said 15-20% of USD249 million already spent, 60-65% in FY27 and 40-45% in FY28.

Brine field expansion: most of phase one complete; commissioning possibly postponed to post-monsoon; land lease extension with Gujarat government under discussion.
SiCSem (USD249 million capex) in execution; environmental clearance and consent to establish pending; general contractor onboarded.

demand_pricing: Bromine demand firm across most geographies; supply imbalance of prior two quarters normalised and pricing corrected; landed prices in China down 30-40% in 12 weeks. Contracts: 60-70% long-term, 30-35% spot.

Industrial salt pricing stabilised after FY26 declines; Q1 realisations broadly flat; competition high from new capacity in Australia and elsewhere. Chlor-alkali demand positive but PVC demand hit by conflict.
QVC (salt customer) still on hold due to Middle East conflict; oil and gas derivative offtake volatile. 60-70% of salt volume on customer-nominated vessels, causing delays and blank sailings.
Sea freight up 30-35%; HSD diesel up nearly 60% YoY in April-June, normalised in July. Road distance from Jakhau roughly doubled to 500+ km.
Bromine derivatives: product mix shift (NPBR volumes ~350 tons in Q1 vs 25-30 tons a year ago), sodium bromide stopped, cost savings at Jhagadia.
risks_watch: Logistics: Hajipir road works due end-September; any slip extends salt volume decline and freight costs; diesel prices and sea freight (up 30-35%) remain elevated.
Bromine volume recovery: power cuts, planned shutdowns, sulphur and coal cost inflation and need for recovery improvements to reach 4,500 tons/quarter.
Bromine pricing: China landed prices down 30-40%; spot share 30-35% exposed to correction.
Salt demand: QVC on hold due to Middle East conflict; customer order deferrals and commercial discipline may affect conversion.
Gujarat brine lease extension not yet closed; brine phase one commissioning timing.
SiCSem and off-grid execution: environmental clearance pending; pilot performance not yet proven; Idealis and SOP feedstock sourcing still challenging.
Q2 and Q3 FY27 volumes are the key test; Q2 expected to be weaker on monsoon-related schedules.
